papers.abstract_full: Childhood obesity is a major global health concern with a strong heritable component. While most cases are polygenic and environmentally driven, a subset of children present with rare genetic forms of obesity, including syndromic and monogenic disorders. Over the past three decades, advances in gene discovery-from candidate gene studies to genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-have significantly improved our understanding of the biological pathways regulating appetite and energy balance, particularly the leptin-melanocortin pathway. Early identification of genetic obesity is clinically relevant, as it allows for tailored management, targeted pharmacological interventions, genetic counseling, and a reduction in psychosocial stigma. However, distinguishing rare genetic obesity from common polygenic obesity remains challenging in clinical practice. This narrative review summarizes the current knowledge on the genetic architecture of pediatric obesity, explores the transition from gene discovery to precision medicine, discusses available diagnostic algorithms and genetic testing strategies, and proposes an updated diagnostic flowchart. In a more clinically useful model, genetic obesity is not defined solely by the presence or absence of a pathogenic variant, but as a continuum in which phenotype, genetic variants, age, and environmental exposure interact and define risk prediction and therapeutic strategies, especially in the pediatric population.

papers.abstract_full: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) has undergone severe loss of genetic diversity due to domestication, necessitating the exploitation of wild relatives for trait improvement. While structural variations (SVs) represent a major source of genetic diversity, high-throughput SV genotyping remains technically challenging, and existing single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays fail to capture presence/absence variations (PAVs) that differentiate wild from cultivated germplasm. Here, we developed the 'Watermelon 40K SNP-SV Chip,' the first liquid-phase genotyping chip enriched with SV markers, leveraging a telomere-to-telomere super-pangenome of seven Citrullus species. The chip comprises 7087 SV markers (enriched for PAVs) and 11 383 SNP/InDel markers. Technical validation in 12 accessions and large-scale genotyping of 228 diverse accessions demonstrated high reproducibility (≥98.5% concordance) and robust call rates (>97%), though performance declined in deeply divergent wild species. Genome-wide association studies revealed SV-specific signals for flesh color and rind pattern that co-localized with known quantitative trait loci (QTL), including a strong candidate regulatory PAV upstream of LCYB. The predominance of rare variants (74.3% SVs with minor allele frequency < 0.05) limits statistical power for detecting QTL underlying polygenic domestication traits such as yield but confers exceptional utility for tracking wild introgressions in early-generation breeding populations. The 40K SNP-SV chip bridges the gap between fundamental SV research and practical breeding, enabling SV-assisted genomic selection for watermelon improvement.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the uptake and determinants of liver cancer screening in Southwest China remains limited. This study aimed to assess the participation rate, influencing factors, and screening outcomes among high-risk individuals in a population-based liver cancer screening program. METHODS: A community-based screening program was conducted across 18 districts or counties in Chongqing, China, from October 2013 to October 2022. High-risk individuals identified through a risk assessment system were invited to receive alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) testing and abdominal ultrasonography. A generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was applied to identify individual-level and structural factors associated with screening uptake. Reasons for non-participation and liver cancer detection rates were also assessed. RESULTS: Among the 369,393 individuals who completed the risk assessment, 37,381 were identified as being at high-risk for liver cancer. After exclusions, 34,647 were included in the final analysis. Of these, 14,062 underwent screening, yielding an uptake rate of 40.59%. Screening participation was significantly associated with younger age, occupational exposures, alcohol consumption, lower levels of physical activity, hepatitis B infection, history of liver cirrhosis, comorbidities, and family history of liver cancer. At the structural level, developed status, use of multiple mobilization strategies, and receiving allowances were positively associated with uptake. Among 20,585 non-participants, the most frequently reported barriers included no symptoms (93.61%), fear of diagnosis (92.60%), and lack of knowledge about cancer prevention and treatment (89.30%). Liver cancer was detected in 14 of the screened individuals, corresponding to a detection rate of 0.10%. CONCLUSION: Participation in liver cancer screening is shaped by a combination of individual and structural factors. Targeted interventions addressing key barriers (such as low risk perception, fear, and knowledge gaps) and structural factors (such as diversified mobilization and financial incentives) may help improve screening uptake among the high-risk populations. WHYWE DID THIS STUDY: There is limited information about how well liver cancer screening works for people living in Southwest China. We wanted to find out how many high-risk people took part in local liver cancer screening, what factors influenced their decision to participate, and how many liver cancers were found through the program. WHAT WE DID AND FOUND: We studied a community-based screening program covering 18 districts or counties in Chongqing between 2013 and 2022. People at high risk of liver cancer were invited to receive AFP testing and abdominal ultrasound scans. Only around 4 out of 10 high-risk people attended the screening. Participation was higher among younger people, and among those with hepatitis B, liver cirrhosis, a family history of liver cancer, alcohol consumption, occupational exposure to hazards, or multiple comorbidities. People in developed areas, people contacted through multiple mobilization methods, and people who received financial allowances were also more likely to attend. Most people who skipped screening said they had no symptoms, feared being diagnosed, or lacked knowledge about cancer prevention. Among those screened, only 0.10% were diagnosed with liver cancer. WHAT THESE RESULTS MEAN: Both personal health conditions and structural conditions influence screening attendance. Future efforts should improve risk awareness, reduce fear of diagnosis, and spread health knowledge, while implementing community-level incentives, to increase screening uptake among high-risk residents,which may help find liver cancer at an earlier, more treatable stage.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 278 ATAAD survivors discharged from Henan Provincial Chest Hospital between 1 August 2023 and 30 July 2024. Clinical and nurse-led follow-up records through 1 August 2025 were reviewed for assessments at discharge and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. The primary trajectory analysis used PCL-5 scores from 1 to 12 months among participants with at least two valid assessments. One- through four-class latent class mixed models were compared according to convergence, Bayesian information criterion, classification quality, and minimum class size. Baseline correlates were examined with multinomial regression. Lagged models separated between-person means from within-person changes in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking; social support was examined across the 3-to-6-month interval. RESULTS: A three-class solution was selected: low-decreasing (n=153, 55.0%), recovering (n=77, 27.7%), and persistent-high (n=48, 17.3%). Within-person increases in illness threat, insomnia, and repetitive negative thinking were associated with higher subsequent PCL-5 scores, whereas higher social support was associated with a lower subsequent score. Baseline associations were attenuated after multiplicity correction. CONCLUSION: The model identified three PTSS trajectories during the first year after ATAAD discharge. Repeated nurse-led assessment may help identify survivors with a persistent symptom burden, and changes in illness threat, insomnia, repetitive negative thinking, and social support may inform the timing and focus of transitional care. The effectiveness of screening or targeted care was not tested.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Improving feed efficiency while understanding resource-allocation trade-offs remains a challenge in livestock breeding. We defined an energy allocation coefficient to growth (α) as the ratio of estimated net energy retained in growth to net energy available after accounting for predicted maintenance requirements and investigated its genetic background in American Angus cattle. We compared a two-step (TS) approach, treating α as a derived pseudo-phenotype in linear animal models, with a one-step (OS) approach, jointly estimating breeding values and variance components through a nonlinear energy-balance model. Genetic parameters were estimated using pedigree- and genomic-based models, and genetic relationships with growth, feed efficiency, and body composition traits were evaluated. RESULTS: The derived α averaged 0.77 ± 0.28 and ranged from 0.07 to 3.10. Log(α) was heritable (h² ≈ 0.13-0.20), with highly consistent breeding value rankings across approaches (ρ > 0.94). Genetic correlations were 0.63 ± 0.03 with average daily gain, -​0.80 ± 0.02 with feed conversion ratio, -​0.54 ± 0.03 with residual feed intake, and 0.61 ± 0.03 with residual average daily gain, indicating substantial but incomplete genetic overlap with conventional growth and feed efficiency traits. The genetic correlation with dry matter intake was weak (-​0.14 ± 0.04) and close to zero with body composition traits (-​0.13 to 0.04). CONCLUSIONS: The α is a derived indicator of relative energy allocation toward growth, calculated using a nutritional energy-balance framework, and contains additive genetic variation in American Angus cattle. Despite modest differences in variance partitioning between TS and OS, the underlying genetic signal was largely consistent across model formulations. The TS framework is compatible with standard genetic evaluation procedures and provides a practical approach for genetic analysis of this derived coefficient. The incomplete genetic overlap between α and conventional feed efficiency traits supports further evaluation of α as a complementary indicator of efficiency from a resource-allocation perspective. Future work should evaluate its relationships with health, reproduction, and resilience-related traits to determine whether α provides additional information for investigating resource-allocation trade-offs and future breeding applications.

papers.abstract_full: Racing performance is an important component of genetic evaluation and breeding decisions in racehorses, but it is a complex trait influenced by genetic and multiple non-genetic factors, including race conditions, management, handicap, and jockey effects. Different specifications of these effects may produce different estimates of genetic parameters and breeding values, highlighting the need to compare alternative model structures. This study aimed to estimate genetic parameters, compare alternative statistical models, and evaluate their suitability for genetic evaluation of racing performance traits in the Turkmen horses bred in Iran. Data comprised 10 830 official race records from 1 667 horses, including 899 stallions and 768 mares, collected from 2003 to 2023. Three racing performance traits were evaluated using eight hierarchical models that differed in their random-effect structures. Model 8 (M8) was selected as the best-supported model for all three race performance traits, including race completion time (RCT), rank at the end of competition (REC), and average speed (AS). Heritability estimates were 0.006 ± 0.001 for RCT, 0.06 ± 0.01 for REC, and 0.004 ± 0.001 for AS. Prediction bias ranged from 0.12 to 0.20, and prediction accuracy ranged from 0.60 to 0.78. The low heritability estimates indicate that additive genetic variance accounted for a relatively small proportion of phenotypic variation in this population under the models considered. Although the parameter estimates and model rankings are population-specific, the findings illustrate a broader methodological consideration for genetic evaluation of racing performance: model specification should account for relevant race-level and jockey-related effects when these factors contribute substantially to observed performance. This consideration may inform genetic evaluation strategies in other racing horse populations with similarly complex performance environments.

papers.abstract_full: Circulating adiponectin is generally considered metabolically protective, but higher levels have been associated with adverse outcomes in some cardiovascular diseases and states of high disease burden, a pattern referred to as the adiponectin paradox. This study assessed genetic evidence relating the adiponectin axis to pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and pulmonary hypertension (PH)-related phenotypes, with consideration of body mass index (BMI) and ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2-related regulation. We integrated publicly available GWAS data for adiponectin, BMI, and PAH/PH with GTEx quantitative trait locus data. The primary two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis used the GCST90293086 adiponectin GWAS as the exposure and the Rhodes/GCST007228 PAH GWAS as the outcome. Supplementary analyses included FinnGen Release 12, BMI-adjusted multivariable MR, receptor-side cis-MR and MRBEE, ADIPOR2 colocalization, local linkage disequilibrium and proxy variant annotation, and lung tissue sQTL analysis. The primary IVW analysis included 21 variants and indicated a nominally significant positive association between genetically predicted adiponectin and PAH risk (OR = 1.452, 95% CI: 1.033-2.042; p = 0.03195). Complementary MR estimates were similar in direction but did not reach statistical significance. In BMI-adjusted multivariable MR using a different FinnGen PH-related outcome, the adiponectin estimate was negative. Because the outcomes differed, this contrast cannot be attributed to BMI adjustment alone. Receptor-side analyses provided supportive genetic evidence involving ADIPOR1/ADIPOR2, including ADIPOR2 colocalization and lung tissue sQTL findings. These exploratory findings do not establish a direct harmful causal effect of circulating adiponectin or confirm a receptor-mediated molecular mechanism.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Dairy cattle in South Africa (SA) have to produce in varying environments which can roughly be separated as total mixed ration (TMR) and pasture (PAST) production systems according to the level of rainfall in the herd area. Previous studies aimed to determine a possible genotype × environment interaction (GxE) using 305-day lactation records, finding no interaction, but different heritabilities. An alternative random regression (aRR) model was developed using SA Holstein test-day records of herds with known production system used (TMR or PAST, analysed independently). The aRR model separates the animal genetic (additive) effect into a general production level and a linear persistency effect and shows clear differences in the genetic variances and heritability estimates over the lactation between TMR and PAST. The aim of this study was to further investigate the existence of a possible GxE interaction, using comparable data, methods and RR model to differentiate each trait (milk, fat and protein production for the first 3 lactations) separately for the two production systems (TMR or PAST). The possible reranking of sires on resulting estimated breeding values from the analysis between TMR and PAST were also investigated. RESULTS: Genetic correlations (0.83 to 0.93) of the genetic general production level effect between TMR and PAST were strong, while corresponding correlations of the genetic linear persistency effect were moderate (0.40 to 0.60) for all traits. Significant reranking of sires between TMR and PAST are predicted for genetic linear persistency, as well as genetic total production. CONCLUSIONS: Genetic correlations show a significant genotype by environment interaction for the genetic linear persistency effect between the two production systems in SA Holsteins. Genetic evaluations should analyse production traits in the different systems as genetically different traits, utilizing an applicable random regression model that can effectively dissociate genetic general production level from genetic linear persistency. Estimating separate breeding values for persistency for each production system is justified.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Kernel fat content (KFC) is a key determinant of oil quality and nutritional value in maize, yet the genetic architecture underlying its natural variation remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) using 239 maize inbred lines genotyped with 1.25 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), applying six complementary statistical models: MLM, MLMM, FarmCPU, BLINK, SUPER, and 3VmrMLM. RESULTS: KFC exhibited substantial phenotypic variation across the three environments, ranging from 5.48% to 8.72%, with a broad-sense heritability (H²) of 0.81. In total, 200 significant quantitative trait nucleotides (QTNs) were detected, each explaining 0.53%-23.49% of the phenotypic variance. Twenty QTNs were consistently identified across multiple models and/or environments and were consolidated into 18 non-redundant QTL intervals. Within these intervals, 58 candidate genes were annotated. Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses revealed significant enrichment in catalytic activities and metabolic pathways, notably α-linolenic acid metabolism-a core pathway in fatty acid biosynthesis. Based on multi-model co-localization and pathway evidence, Zm00001d025166, encoding a plastid-localized putative quinone-oxidoreductase, was prioritized as the primary candidate gene. Haplotype analysis identified two major haplotypes, with Hap1 conferring significantly higher KFC than Hap2 (7.09% vs. 6.46%, p = 0.003), although the difference was modest. Selective sweep analysis detected moderate selection pressure on this gene in U.S. breeding germplasm compared with Chinese and CIMMYT accessions, while weak differentiation between tropical and temperate ecotypes suggested a conserved role in fatty acid metabolism. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide a foundation for marker-assisted selection in high-oil maize breeding and demonstrate the value of multi-model GWAS strategies for dissecting complex quantitative traits.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent condition that progresses from simple steatosis to advanced fibrosis, significantly affecting liver function and systemic health. Despite its widespread impact, therapeutic options remain limited, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive exploration to identify potential therapeutic targets. METHODS: We developed an analysis pipeline anchored on liver gene expression, integrating differential meta-analysis of transcriptomic data across three MASLD stages, transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR), and transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) to identify candidate genes potentially involved in MASLD progression. We further prioritized these genes using a scoring system that incorporated gene expression-clinical phenotype correlation meta-analysis, proteome-wide association studies (PWAS), and external genetic data from the GWAS Catalog and ExPheWAS. In addition, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) analysis was performed to characterize the expression patterns of prioritized genes across liver cell types and disease stages. RESULTS: By integrating transcriptomic, genetic, and phenotypic evidence, we prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD. snRNA-seq analysis of liver cells from healthy to cirrhotic stages revealed stage- and cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes. Through experimental validation in a lipid overload hepatocyte model, we confirmed a role for MLIP in lipid metabolism. To facilitate community access and data exploration, these data were organized and deposited into a publicly accessible interactive web portal (www.masldportal.net). CONCLUSIONS: Our integrative, liver expression-anchored multi-omics framework prioritized 39 candidate regulators of MASLD and highlighted MLIP as a functional modulator of hepatocellular lipid accumulation. These results provide a systematic foundation for understanding MASLD biology and for guiding future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

We analyzed European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics for PTSD (N_eff ≈ 1.22 million), CVD outcomes (CVDoutcomes; coronary artery disease, stroke, hypertension; N_eff = 126,000-574,000), and CVD risk factors (CVDrisk; high-density l…
papers.abstract_full: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with elevated cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but the extent of shared inherited liability is unclear. Large genome-wide association studies (GWAS) allow for multivariate evaluation of common genetic architecture. We analyzed European-ancestry GWAS summary statistics for PTSD (N_eff ≈ 1.22 million), CVD outcomes (CVDoutcomes; coronary artery disease, stroke, hypertension; N_eff = 126,000-574,000), and CVD risk factors (CVDrisk; high-density lipoprotein, triglycerides, fasting glucose, waist circumference; N = 211,000-526,000). Using genomic structural equation modeling, we modeled latent genetic structure across PTSD and CVD phenotypes and conducted multivariate GWAS of latent factors with gene and gene-set annotation. A three-factor model distinguishing PTSD, CVDrisk, and CVDoutcomes best fit the data, χ2 = 256.9, CFI = .990, SRMR = .040. PTSD showed a moderate genetic correlation with CVDrisk, rg = .340, p < .001, and a significant but negligible genetic correlation with CVDoutcomes, rg = 0.030, p < .001, suggesting minimal shared genetic liability at the latent-factor level. Multivariate GWAS identified seven loci for PTSD, 96 for CVDrisk, and 51 for CVDoutcomes. Gene-based tests implicated 85, 910, and 390 genes, respectively, with 18 overlapping between PTSD and CVDrisk. Enrichment highlighted RNA metabolism for PTSD and lipid/vascular pathways for CVD traits. Additional locus-level overlaps emerged, including a genomic hub in the major histocompatibility complex region on Chromosome 6 for both phenotypes. PTSD shares moderate polygenic overlap with CVD, particularly CVDrisk, but many loci are trait-specific, implicating lipid metabolism, vascular tone, immune/inflammatory pathways, and RNA regulation as potential links.

papers.abstract_full: Fruit quality has become a primary breeding objective in tomato because it determines consumer acceptance, processing efficiency, and market value. However, quality-related traits are quantitatively inherited and strongly influenced by environmental conditions, making genetic improvement challenging. In this study, genome-wide association studies (GWAS) was conducted to elucidate the genetic architecture of six economically important fruit quality traits, including luminosity, hue, chroma, soluble solids content (°Brix), titratable acidity, and fruit fresh weight (FW), using a diverse panel of 305 tomato accessions evaluated over two growing seasons. Substantial phenotypic variation was observed for all traits, with significant effects of genotype, year, and genotype × year interaction, indicating that fruit quality is governed by both genetic and environmental factors. Fruit weight, luminosity, hue, chroma, and °Brix exhibited high broad-sense heritability, whereas titratable acidity showed moderate heritability. Correlation analysis revealed strong positive relationships among color-related traits, while °Brix was positively associated with acidity but negatively correlated with fruit color attributes and FW. Skim sequencing generated 4,618 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), and GWAS was performed using multiple models. GWAS identified 15 non-redundant marker-trait associations (MTAs) across chromosomes, with several loci consistently detected across statistical models. A prominent locus, SL4.0ch03_12722521, on chromosome 3 was associated with luminosity, hue, and chroma, explaining up to 53.86% of phenotypic variation (PVE), suggesting pleiotropic regulation of fruit color. Stable loci controlling FW and soluble solids were also identified on chromosome 5, explaining up to 52.88% PVE. Candidate genes of significant MTAs included sucrose synthase, sec14p-like phosphatidylinositol transfer protein, bHLH transcription factor, and chitinase genes, indicating potential roles in carbohydrate metabolism, fruit development, cell wall remodeling, pigmentation, and ripening. These findings provide valuable genomic resources for improving fruit quality and accelerating the development of elite tomato cultivars.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: The risk of invasive bacterial infections has dropped significantly among febrile infants due to widespread vaccination efforts. In older infants (age 91 days and older), diagnostic guidance is limited, and blood culture ordering is based on clinical judgment. We sought to evaluate blood culture ordering practice, bacteremia incidence, and the patient characteristics of true positive blood culture results. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of febrile pediatric patients aged 91 to 365 days who presented to Kaiser Permanente Northern California emergency departments (EDs) between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2019, who had blood cultures drawn. We identified variables related to blood culture ordering using a generalized linear mixed model and adjudicated all positive results to determine rates of true bacteremia or contamination, as well as clinical characteristics of children with true positive bacteremia. RESULTS: Among 5543 febrile infants, 611 (11.0%) underwent blood culture testing. CONCLUSION: In febrile infants aged 91 to 365 days, true bacteremia was rare and associated with significant comorbidities or an obvious infectious source. papers.abstract_full: AIM: To investigate the changes in corneal densitometry (CD) after small incision lenticule extraction combined with accelerated corneal cross-linking (SMILE Xtra) for correcting moderate to high myopia and to analyze their correlation. METHODS: In this non-randomized retrospective comparative study, participants who underwent surgery were enrolled in the standalone SMILE group and SMILE Xtra group, respectively. Preoperative and postoperative uncorrected visual acuity, spherical equivalent (SE), and CD values were recorded at 1, 3, 6, and 12mo. Measurements were taken in the central (0-2 mm), paracentral (2-6 mm), and peripheral (6-10 mm) zones, as well as in the anterior 120 µm, central, and posterior 60 µm layers of the cornea. A generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) was used to compare CD values between groups and at different time points, and the correlation between postoperative CD values and residual bed thickness (RBT) was analyzed. RESULTS: Totally 31 participants (62 eyes, mean age 20.32±2.76y) were in the standalone SMILE group and 28 participants (53 eyes, mean age 20.45±2.08y) in SMILE Xtra group. At 12mo postoperatively, there were no statistically significant differences in uncorrected visual acuity or SE between the two groups (P>0.05). Preoperative CD values in all regions showed no significant differences between groups (all P>0.05). In the central (0-2 mm) and paracentral (2-6 mm) zones, and the anterior, central, and total stromal layers, group, time, and interaction effects were all significant (all P<0.001). At 1, 3, and 6mo postoperatively, CD values in the SMILE Xtra group were significantly higher than those in the SMILE group within the 0-2 mm and 2-6 mm diameter ranges, as well as in the anterior, central, and total layers (all P<0.05). At 12mo postoperatively, CD values in the anterior layer remained significantly higher in the SMILE Xtra group compared to the SMILE group (P=0.007), whereas no statistically significant differences were observed in other diameter ranges or stromal layers (all P>0.05). Correlation analysis revealed that at 12mo postoperatively, CD values in all regions of both groups showed a significant positive correlation with RBT (all P<0.05), except for the anterior layer in the SMILE group, which showed no significant correlation with RBT (r=0.114, P=0.380). CONCLUSION: SMILE Xtra induces transient early increase in CD, primarily in the anterior and central layers. Although values stabilize or decline by 12mo postoperatively, the clinical significance of these long-term patterns requires cautious interpretation, considering the potential influence of post-surgical structural changes. Further research is necessary to fully elucidate the underlying contributions to these densitometric changes.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Climate change and limited resources are intensifying abiotic stresses in wheat production, creating an urgent need for varieties that combine high yield with reliable performance under variable conditions. However, selecting for yield under optimal or single-stress conditions often fails to predict how genotypes will perform under complex, real-world challenges. METHODS: We evaluated 56 wheat genotypes under four environments: fully fertilized and irrigated (FFI), water deficit (WD), nitrogen deficit (ND), and combined water-nitrogen deficit (CWND). To quantify resilience, we developed a composite D-value index by integrating stress-response ratios of seven agronomic traits using PCA, fuzzy membership normalization, and entropy-weighted aggregation. RESULTS: Both WD and ND reduced grain yield by 21-22% relative to FFI, while CWND caused a further decline (-31%), representing the greatest reduction among all treatments. Stress environments fundamentally altered the relationships between key agronomic traits. Genotype performance varied considerably across environments: XM296 maintained relatively high yield under single stresses but showed limited multi-trait stability under combined stress; LX99 showed stable performance across diverse stresses while retaining high yield potential; in contrast, XN20 exhibited relatively high tolerance at the expense of low productivity. CONCLUSIONS: Given the environment-dependent nature of resilience, breeding strategies should balance broad adaptation with improvements targeted at the dominant stress patterns in key production regions. This approach will better translate genetic gains into stable yields in farmers' fields.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a leading cause of chronic low back pain (LBP), severely impairing patients' quality of life and imposing a substantial global socioeconomic burden. Conservative treatment remains the first-line clinical option, but the commonly prescribed drug celecoxib carries a risk of gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation. Traditional Chinese medicine preparations have been proposed as alternatives, although current evidence is insufficient. Jintiange (JTG) capsule, developed as a substitute for tiger bone, exerts its pharmacological effects by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis and regulating the NF-κB pathway. Previous studies have identified a close association between the p38MAPK/NF-κB pathway and pain induced by LDH. However, the efficacy of JTG in treating LDH remains unclear. High-quality research is thus urgently needed to provide evidence-based support for its clinical application. METHOD: This randomized, single-center clinical trial will enroll 68 participants, centrally allocated 1:1 to receive either JTG capsules plus comprehensive Western medicine (celecoxib + eperisone) or Western medicine alone. All participants will complete an 8-week treatment phase (celecoxib for 2 weeks + eperisone for 8 weeks; with JTG capsules added for 8 weeks in the experimental group), with a follow-up at Week 12 (4 weeks after treatment completion). The primary outcome is the change in the Japanese Orthopaedic Association (JOA) score for LBP, a validated instrument for evaluating treatment efficacy in LDH. Secondary outcomes include the Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score, SF-12 quality-of-life score, and elastic modulus of the lumbar muscles. Safety monitoring and adverse-event recording will occur throughout the study. The primary endpoint will be analyzed using the analysis of covariance. Longitudinal VAS scores at Weeks 2, 8, and 12 will be analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures. PGIC will be analyzed as an ordinal categorical outcome, while other secondary outcomes will be analyzed using appropriate parametric or nonparametric methods. All analyses will be performed using SPSS 28.0, with no interim analysis planned. DISCUSSION: This trial will evaluate the clinical efficacy of JTG capsules combined with Western medicine for LBP and will explore its safety profile as a secondary/exploratory endpoint. Given the open-label combination design, safety findings will be interpreted with caution, and causality attribution to JTG alone will be limited. The findings are expected to provide an evidence-based treatment option, supporting the potential role of Chinese patent medicine in LBP management. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Registry of Clinical Trials: ChiCTR2300069735.

papers.abstract_full: Soybean (Glycine max L.) is a globally important crop and a major source of edible oil and plant-based protein; however, spring-season cultivation exposes soybean to elevated temperatures during critical reproductive stages, adversely affecting yield and seed quality. A panel of 100 advanced soybean accessions was screened across two variable planting dates of the spring season for two consecutive growing years, 2020 and 2021. Phenotypic data of six yield-related traits, i.e., plant height (PH), number of pods per plant (Pods), number of seeds per plant (Seeds), 100-seed weight (HSW), yield per plant (YPP), and days to maturity (DM) were collected. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) was conducted using the Fixed and Random Model Circulating Probability Unification (Farm-CPU) method by using 42,449 high-quality single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) from the SoySNP50K array. A total of 77 significant marker trait associations (MTAs) were identified. The highest number of MTAs is linked with plant height, and the lowest number of MTAs is linked with yield per plant. Genome-wide means of major allele frequency (MAF), genetic diversity (GD), and polymorphic information content (PIC) were 0.78, 0.28, and 0.28, respectively. Population structure and phylogenetic tree analysis were used to divide the whole population into two distinct groups. Furthermore, seven SNPs, i.e., ss715582919, ss715588087, ss715588504, ss715592876, ss715599604, ss715599732, and ss715599766, were associated with multiple traits across planting dates. Various clusters of significant SNPs were marked on chromosomes Gm08, Gm10, Gm17, Gm02, Gm12, Gm15, and Gm16 associated with various yield traits. Candidate gene analysis identified genes related to thermotolerance (HSP90, HSFA2), flowering time (FT2a), pod number (NAC29), and carbohydrate transport (SWEET15) within flanking regions of key SNPs. A comprehensive insight into the genetic architecture of soybean yield under spring-season conditions is a prerequisite for the development of climate-resilient soybean genotypes. These findings will contribute to devising future breeding strategies in soybean.

Participants were allocated to an intervention group (n = 38) receiving a structured education program via Skyroom and Whats…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Despite the well-documented benefits of breastfeeding, exclusive breastfeeding rates remain suboptimal globally. This study aimed to assess the impact of a health literacy-based educational intervention on breastfeeding self-efficacy among primiparous women. METHODS: A randomized clinical trial was conducted with 77 primiparous pregnant mothers in Chalus, Iran. Participants were allocated to an intervention group (n = 38) receiving a structured education program via Skyroom and WhatsApp, or a control group (n = 39) receiving routine care. Breastfeeding self-efficacy was assessed using the BSES-SF questionnaire at baseline, immediately post-intervention, and at three and six weeks postpartum. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 20 with chi-square, Fisher's exact, Mann-Whitney, and mixed model tests. RESULTS: At baseline, the groups had similar self-efficacy scores (intervention: 40.84 ± 10.62 vs. control: 38.07 ± 7.52, p = 0.264). The intervention group demonstrated a significantly greater increase in self-efficacy immediately post-intervention (61.57 ± 5.05 vs. 45.01 ± 6.76; p < 0.0001), and this significant difference was maintained at three weeks (58.47 ± 5.44 vs. 48.23 ± 7.14; p < 0.0001) and six weeks (57.47 ± 5.31 vs. 49.48 ± 6.59; p < 0.0001) post-intervention. CONCLUSION: A health literacy-based education program significantly improved breastfeeding self-efficacy in primiparous women. This approach, particularly when delivered via accessible digital platforms, shows promise as an effective strategy to promote exclusive breastfeeding.

papers.abstract_full: Aims/hypothesis: To evaluate the effectiveness of a personalised intervention program aimed at improving medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes who are non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication, compared to usual care including access to a diabetes website, after a six-month follow-up. Methods: Parallel-group randomised controlled trial with six-month follow-up conducted in community pharmacies in the Netherlands and United Kingdom. People with type 2 diabetes, 35-75 years and non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication were recruited. The intervention group received the personalised intervention program and the control group received usual care and an informative diabetes website. The primary outcome was medication adherence measured by telephone pill count and secondary outcomes were self-reported medication adherence, systolic blood pressure and HbA1c level. Linear regression analysis and longitudinal mixed model analysis were performed to assess intervention effectiveness. Results: The study population comprised 68 participants, 66.2% men with a median age of 65.0 [Q1 to Q3 59.3 to 71.0] years. Linear regression analysis for the primary outcome medication adherence showed no significant effect of the intervention (B -0.014, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.14). In addition, no significant differences were found between the intervention and control group for self-reported medication adherence (OR 3.18, 95% CI 0.89 to 11.37) and systolic blood pressure (B -1.41, 95% CI -9.64 to 6.83). Finally, the intervention group did not show better HbA1c levels compared to the control group (B 0.68, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92).  Conclusions/interpretation: We did not observe a statistically significant difference, nor a clinically point estimate of difference, in medication adherence between the intervention and control group of a personalised intervention program aimed at improving medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes who are non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication after six-months follow-up. We therefore do not recommend implementation of the intervention program in daily practice. Trial registry number: Registered in the Dutch Trial Register (Trial NL8747) and ISRCTN Registry (  ISRCTN36009809 ). Social media post: No effect of a personalised intervention program was observed on medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes. Future studies should first focus on alternative recruitment methods for non-adherent people with type 2 diabetes, before the effectiveness of the intervention can be re-evaluated in a larger study sample. Keywords: Medication adherence, type 2 diabetes, intervention, pharmacy, effectiveness

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  The gut microbiome has been associated with diverse human diseases, but systematic genetic evidence for potential causal relevance, disease-system clustering, and circulating metabolic pathways remains limited. Methods  We integrated four gut microbiome genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets with 4,934 disease GWAS outcomes. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method as the primary analysis, was performed to evaluate potential causal associations between gut microbial traits and diseases. Multiple sensitivity analyses and reverse MR were conducted to assess robustness and potential reverse causality. Hypergeometric tests were used to examine disease-system enrichment of microbial lineages with significant MR associations. For significant MR associations, Bayesian colocalization analysis was performed to assess shared local genetic signals. Circulating metabolite GWAS data were further incorporated into two-step MR mediation analysis to explore candidate metabolic pathways. Results  We identified 1,943 significant associations between 630 gut microbial traits and 925 disease outcomes across multiple disease systems. Enrichment analysis revealed system-specific clustering patterns, including enrichment of Burkholderiales-related taxa in circulatory diseases, Bacteroidota-related taxa in mental, behavioural, or neurodevelopmental disorders,  Eisenbergiella  -related taxa in musculoskeletal diseases, and  Faecalicatena  -related taxa in endocrine and metabolic diseases. Colocalization analysis identified 58 colocalization signals with supportive evidence of shared local genetic signals, involving 34 microbial traits, 45 disease outcomes, and 33distinct genomic windows. Mediation analysis highlighted triglycerides in intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL-TG) as a frequent candidate mediator, particularly linking Burkholderiales-related taxa to ischaemic cardiovascular diseases. Conclusions  This large-scale genetic study provides a systematic map of potential causal associations between the gut microbiome and multi-system diseases. By integrating MR, disease-system enrichment, colocalization, and mediation analyses, our findings suggest that specific gut microbial lineages may contribute to disease susceptibility through shared genetic architecture and circulating metabolic pathways. In particular, the Burkholderiales-IDL-TG-ischaemic cardiovascular disease axis may represent a candidate microbiome-metabolism-disease pathway that warrants further validation in experimental and clinical studies.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Knowledge-graph models can rank existing drugs for a disease, but their benchmarks mostly reward rediscovering known treatments, and their scores rarely come with evidence a researcher can check. We built OREVID, an open tool that shows a ranked candidate only when an evidence line supports it and reports how often each line was right on held-out data, and compared it with TxGNN on identical data. Methods. The graph combines PrimeKG, Open Targets, STRING and PubTator3 (157,822 nodes, 9.46 million edges). For each disease, 22 degree-weighted metapath features and two gene-level columns (whether the drug moves its targets in the direction human genetics asks, from protein and expression QTLs that colocalise with the disease's genome-wide association studies, and whether it acts on a gene Orphanet lists for the disease) feed a LightGBM LambdaRank model trained with masked neighbourhoods. A candidate is shown only if it is indicated for an ontology-neighbour disease or for a disease sharing at least 3 associated genes (hypergeometric p < 10⁻⁵ over the genes with at least one associated disease). The acceptance criteria for these rules were set in advance; the rules were revised on the hidden-treatment benchmarks and then measured on an external set of approvals not used to choose them. TxGNN was retrained with its official code on the same PrimeKG splits, and all tasks and predictions are released as OREVID-bench. Results. Zero-shot Recall@100 (mean ± SD over five splits) was 0.812 ± 0.038 for OREVID, 0.412 ± 0.042 for TxGNN and 0.358 ± 0.040 for a popularity baseline, with OREVID ahead on every split (paired difference with TxGNN 0.400, 95% CI 0.354–0.444, resampling diseases). On nine disease areas held out it was 0.627 against 0.237, ahead in all nine, although TxGNN had the higher AUPRC in four. A drug acting on a disease gene, with no other evidence, was right 1.8–3.4% of the time, no better than candidates with no evidence line at all. papers.abstract_full: Purpose  In East Asians most primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) occurs at statistically normal intraocular pressure (IOP). We sought plasma proteins linked to POAG through genetic signal not shared with IOP. Methods  We integrated the BioBank Japan POAG GWAS with a Japanese plasma pQTL resource (Nagahama; SomaScan v4) using SMR/HEIDI and colocalization against POAG and IOP datasets, including a Genomic-SEM–derived non-IOP POAG component, adding a symmetric proteome-wide cross-ancestry colocalization, fine-mapping and multi-signal colocalization of the RGMB region, a formal heterogeneity test, and expression mapping in retina and trabecular meshwork. Results  Of 679 plasma proteins, four colocalized with POAG in East Asians only, five in Europeans only, none in both. SMR nominated RGMB as a suggestive risk factor (b_SMR = +0.277; HEIDI P > 0.05; PP4 = 0.684; rs1037599); none survived Bonferroni correction. RGMB did not colocalize with European IOP, a European non-IOP POAG component, or European POAG on the same platform, despite a common, directionally consistent pQTL instrument. Multi-signal colocalization reproduced both the East Asian signal and the European null. The per-allele POAG effect differed between ancestries (Cochran’s Q P = 0.0036; I² = 88%), the better-powered European data excluding an effect of East Asian magnitude. RGMB and its receptors were expressed in trabecular meshwork cells and unchanged by TGF-β2. Conclusions  This triangulation nominates the RGMB–neogenin–BMP axis as a POAG candidate detected in East Asians but not Europeans, which does not colocalize with IOP-related traits. The findings are exploratory; ancestry-matched replication and functional validation are required.

papers.abstract_full: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have made association discovery systematic and cumulative, yet evidence for interpreting associated loci remains selective, heterogeneous and difficult to accumulate across studies. Here we present Post-GWAS Intelligence (PGI), which couples context-dependent post-GWAS analysis to a common representation of analysis-derived evidence. Its multi-agent engine, VariantAgent, executes workflows, records tool-derived results in standardized variant-centred units and generates trait-level interpretations linked to their analytical basis and evidential status. Complementary benchmarks showed that VariantAgent outperformed tested general-purpose and biomedical agents, with its largest advantage when success required both a correct answer and a valid analytical trace. Across 34 published GWAS, VariantAgent achieved a mean per-study recovery of 82.1% for directly comparable findings. The largest gains lay downstream of association mapping, where uniform analysis extended published interpretations and identified regulatory relationships at established risk loci not previously reported in the source studies. Analysis of 1,041 GWAS yielded 530,949 evidence units and corresponding reports, which PGI organized into a cross-trait catalogue. Catalogue interrogation resolved an apparent cross-trait overlap into distinct signals and trait-specific biological hypotheses. This work demonstrates how PGI can extend genetic discovery beyond association mapping by enabling biological evidence to accumulate across studies.

papers.abstract_full: Mutations affecting the transcription factor hepatocyte nuclear factor-1β (HNF-1β) are the most common monogenic cause of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. The mechanism whereby HNF-1β regulates gene transcription remains unclear. Here, we performed an unbiased proteomic screen and found that endogenous HNF-1β interacts with core subunits of the nucleosome remodeling and deacetylase complex (NuRD) in renal epithelial cells. Genome-wide ChIP-seq studies demonstrated colocalization of endogenous HNF-1β and the core NuRD subunits GATAD2A, CHD4, and MBD3 at 2,776 primarily intergenic and intronic sites in native chromatin from wild-type renal epithelial cells. NuRD co-occupancy at 628 of the sites (22.6%) was reduced in the absence of HNF-1β. Of the 628 HNF-1β-dependent NuRD-occupied sites, 113 sites (18.2%) showed higher ATAC-seq peaks, indicative of open chromatin, and enrichment of histone H3 lysine-27 (H3K27) acetylation, indicative of active enhancers, in wild-type cells compared to HNF-1β-deficient cells. Correlation with transcriptomic profiles in wild-type and HNF-1β-deficient cells revealed that most of the sites were located near genes that are activated by HNF-1β. Knockdown of CHD4 with shRNA resulted in decreased expression of 67 HNF-1β-regulated genes that contained nearby NuRD and HNF-1β co-occupied sites. Collectively, these results demonstrate that HNF-1β recruits the NuRD complex resulting in H3K27 acetylation and chromatin opening and leading to gene activation. Our findings reveal a new mechanism of HNF-1β-dependent gene expression and expand the role of the NuRD complex in gene activation at distal enhancers.

papers.abstract_full: Objectives: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) is a cyclical hormone-related condition, causing significant mood symptoms in the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle. Despite the substantial impact it can have on daily life, little is known about how it shapes reproductive decision-making. This study explored how people with PMDD experience and reflect on reproductive decisions, and the role of healthcare support in this. Design: Semi-structured qualitative interviews, informed by a feminist critical realist approach. Methods: Twenty UK-based adults who had received a diagnosis of, or self-identified as having, PMDD took part. Semi-structured interviews explored experiences of how, if at all, PMDD had impacted thoughts and decisions around pregnancy or parenthood. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by a lived experience advisory group. Results: Four themes were developed: PMDD as a whole-family experience; intergenerational awareness and responsibility; assessing readiness and capacity for parenthood; and self-advocacy and negotiating an unsupportive system. Participants not only spoke about how PMDD symptoms shaped their decision-making, but also considered relational impact, the potential heritability of PMDD, and the limited healthcare support available. Support from loved ones, familiarity with their own symptom patterns and establishing strategies for managing PMDD were often described as facilitators of decision-making. Across themes, findings were interpreted within a “good mother” ideal, helping to explain why reproductive decisions often carried emotional and moral weight. Conclusions: PMDD can shape reproductive decision-making in complex ways. Findings demonstrate the need for PMDD-specific support that helps people make informed decisions aligned with their circumstances and needs.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Genomic prediction in polyploid crops requires decisions about how allele dosage is encoded at biallelic SNPs. In triploid breeding systems produced from tetraploid × diploid crosses- the mating design used commercially for seedless watermelon and other economically important crops- each locus can carry the alternative allele in zero, one, two, or three copies. This four-state genotype is frequently compressed to a diploid-like three-state encoding for compatibility with standard prediction pipelines. The long-term cost of this compression, and the conditions under which it becomes practically important, remain unquantified. We used stochastic simulation to isolate the effect of dosage encoding on prediction accuracy and long-term selection response in a triploid hybrid breeding program. We compared two encodings: the proper four-state dosage encoding (C: 0/1/2/3) and a diploidized three-state encoding that collapses the two heterozygous classes (B: 0/1/1/2). We evaluated these encodings across a 72-scenario factorial grid varying dominance, heritability, and training size. Overall, encoding C outperformed encoding B under the additive-plus-dominance kernel model in 66 of 72 scenarios. The difference was largest when the dominance proportion was low and shrank monotonically as dominance became more important. In a subsequent recurrent selection study, overall, encoding C produced 7.6% higher cumulative hybrid genetic value than encoding B at cycle 10 (30 years of breeding). However, the per-cycle prediction accuracy advantage of dosage-aware encoding is modest (0.028 accuracy units). Our results place a lower bound on the value of dosage-aware genotyping in polyploid breeding and identify the trait architectures for which the investment is most warranted.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Phenomic selection has emerged as a promising yet controversially discussed alternative to genomic selection. Its appeal lies in the relatively low cost of marker acquisition and the increasing availability of phenotypic data. Crops like rapeseed, in which Near Infrared Spectroscopy (NIRS) is routinely applied for assessment of seed quality, can benefit from phenomic selection without any additional costs as the spectral data is already collected routinely in breeding programs. Despite this potential, several challenges hinder its effective implementation. Among these, the quality of spectral wavelengths is frequently debated as a key factor influencing model performance. Broad-sense wavelength heritability is commonly employed as an indicator of wavelength relevance in NIRS-based prediction models. Here we demonstrate that heritability alone does not fully capture the predictive relevance of individual wavelengths. Owing to the high degree of collinearity among wavelengths, only a small fraction of approximately 1.1% is necessary for accurate trait prediction. Moreover, phenomic selection models often rely on molecular proxies that are correlated with the target trait. In rapeseed, for instance, protein or oil content are correlated to seed yield and lead to a potential bias for such traits, which may ultimately reduce the response to selection and undesired selection pressure for correlated traits. In contrast, we found that other traits like flowering time are lacking such molecular correlations and appear to be unaffected by this issue.

papers.abstract_full: Linear mixed models (LMM) are a popular modeling and inference framework, widely used in bioinformatics and other scientific fields. To obtain an unbiased estimation of the variance components, an LMM has to be fitted using restricted maximum likelihood (REML), a computationally intensive step. Most REML software is closed source, and currently there is no  Python library offering complete LMM functionalities, such as the specification of spatial and genomic variance structures, multivariate analyses, random regression and factors, and heteroscedastic residuals. Here we propose  pyreml , an LMM solver that fills this gap, comes with a user-centered interface and speeds up calculations by running on GPU. We show that  pyreml fits a genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) model more than one order of magnitude (  > 12 ×) faster than the current state-of-the-art, closed source REML software. We also show that  pyreml can estimate a latent factor-analytic variance structure, a challenging feature that no current open source REML solution implements. Finally, we illustrate the use of  pyreml to analyze longitudinal data, and to perform spatial analysis. Anchored by 500+ functional tests assessing the equivalence of its outputs to those from reference software (  lme4 ,  rrBLUP and  BLUPF90 ), we demonstrate  pyreml to be a performant, reliable and open-source solution available for academic, research and industrial LMM users.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: To estimate the incidence of recognised incidental durotomy in irrigated uniportal and biportal endoscopic lumbar surgery, and to describe conversion, delayed cerebrospinal fluid sequelae and repair. METHODS: The protocol was registered (PROSPERO CRD420261507619) and the review follows PRISMA 2020. MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Europe PMC were searched directly to 16 September 2026. Embase, Scopus and CINAHL were not directly accessible and were approached only indirectly, a limitation of the search. Consecutive series reporting recognised intraoperative tears with a denominator were eligible. Proportions were pooled with a binomial generalised linear mixed model (GLMM), with the prespecified Freeman-Tukey model as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Nineteen series (6 823 operations, 177 recognised tears) were included. The pooled rate was 2.74 % (95 % CI 1.72 to 4.16; Freeman-Tukey 3.00 %), with I2 86 % and a prediction interval of 0.44 % to 15.3 %. Disc herniation strata pooled at 1.07 % and stenosis strata at 5.47 % (odds ratio 4.53, p = 0.003). After adjustment for indication, biportal and uniportal series did not differ significantly (odds ratio 1.58, 95 % CI 0.63 to 3.94; very low certainty). Conversion occurred in 6 of 113 documented tears (5.3 %) and delayed fistula or pseudomeningocele in 3 of 80 (3.8 %). CONCLUSIONS: Rates vary widely between series, and no single pooled figure describes the risk of an individual operation. About one tear per hundred discectomies and one per twenty stenosis decompressions is a reasonable basis for consent, adjusted for revision and experience. A difference between techniques is neither shown nor excluded. Occult tears after transforaminal discectomy should be quoted separately.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: To compare the diagnostic accuracy of three cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) acquisition protocols, one low-resolution (LR) and two high-resolution (HR) protocols, using a metal artifact reduction tool (MAR) for detecting a second canal in mandibular incisors adjacent to a zirconia implant. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Twenty single-rooted mandibular incisors were included, twelve with one canal and eight with two canals confirmed by micro-CT. The roots and a zirconia implant were placed into the alveolar sockets of the right and left mandibular central incisors of a dry human mandible, respectively. In total, 240 CBCT scans were obtained using FOV 5x5 cm, 90 kVp, with and without implant, for each root. The variable parameters included the MAR tool, one LR-protocol (0.2 mm voxel, 5 mA), and two HR-protocols (0.085 mm voxel, 4 and 10 mA). Five calibrated examiners independently evaluated the scans. An ordinal cumulative link mixed model (CLMM) with crossed random intercepts for roots and examiners was used for data analysis (α = 5%). RESULTS: The CLMM revealed a significant main effect for implant presence (p = 0.049) and canal status (p < 0.001), but not for protocol (p = 0.135) or MAR (p = 0.392). Significant protocol x canal status (p < 0.001) and implant x canal status (p < 0.001) interactions were found, whereas MAR interactions were not significant (p > 0.05). In two-canal roots, the zirconia implant significantly induced false-negative shifts under HR-4 (p < 0.0001) and LR (p < 0.0001) protocols, whereas HR-10 preserved sensitivity (p = 0.7760). In single-canal roots, implants induced false-positive shifts in HR-10 (p = 0.0011) and HR-4 (p = 0.0011). CONCLUSION: Zirconia implants impair second canal detection via false-negative and false-positive errors. High-resolution CBCT (HR-10) should be prioritized to preserve diagnostic sensitivity, whereas MAR offers no clinical benefit and cannot compensate for reduced resolution or exposure. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: CBCT diagnostic performance near zirconia implants relies on acquisition protocol rather than MAR activation. High-resolution CBCT (HR-10) mitigates implant-induced false negatives, whereas lower-resolution or lower-milliamperage protocols compromise diagnostic accuracy.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Molybdenum (Mo) and cadmium (Cd) can contaminate feed, water, and agricultural environments, thereby threatening food-producing animals. However, their combined effects on splenic mitochondrial homeostasis in ruminants remain unclear. AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the effects of Mo and Cd, individually and in combination, on splenic injury, mitochondrial homeostasis, mitophagy-related markers, and ferroptosis-related alterations in sheep. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Seventy-two 2-month-old lambs were randomly assigned to four groups: control, Mo, Cd, and Mo + Cd groups, and were orally administered 45 mg Mo•kg⁻¹ body weight and/or 1 mg Cd•kg⁻¹ body weight daily for 75 days. Splenic morphology, oxidative stress, iron metabolism, mitochondrial ultrastructure and dynamics, mitophagy-related markers, TBK1-OPTN-related signaling, and ferroptosis-related indices were evaluated. RESULTS: Mo and/or Cd exposure induced splenic morphological alterations, including disorganized tissue architecture, indistinct red-white pulp boundaries, and thickening of the central arteriole wall. These changes were accompanied by decreased glutathione content and catalase activity and increased malondialdehyde, H₂O₂, 4-HNE, and Fe²⁺ levels. Transmission electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial cristae disruption, vacuolization, and shrinkage. GPX4, FTH1, and SLC7A11 expression decreased, whereas NCOA4 expression increased. Mo and Cd exposure also altered mitochondrial dynamics, increased PINK1, Parkin, and LC3B expression, reduced p62 expression, and enhanced PINK1-Parkin colocalization. Increased TBK1 phosphorylation, OPTN expression, and NCOA4-LC3B colocalization were also observed. CONCLUSION: Mo and Cd co-exposure impaired splenic mitochondrial homeostasis and was associated with coordinated mitophagy- and ferroptosis-related alterations in sheep.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a leading cause of disability worldwide, driven by the complex interplay of aging, obesity, and mechanical stress, which converge on progressive deterioration of cartilage, subchondral bone, and synovial tissue. Current treatments alleviate symptoms but fail to halt the degenerative process, making joint replacement surgery the only definitive option for advanced disease. A central mechanism underlying OA pathogenesis is mitochondrial dysfunction in chondrocytes, in which the balance between oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and glycolysis is disrupted, leading to impaired OXPHOS, accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), and sustained overproduction of matrix-degrading enzymes and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Mitochondrial transplantation has emerged as a promising strategy to restore cellular bioenergetics, and platelets, which contain functional, respiration-competent mitochondria, represent an accessible allogenic donor source. METHODS: Mitochondria isolated from platelets of healthy donors were structurally and functionally characterized and transplanted into primary human OA chondrocytes by mitoception at increasing chondrocyte-to-mitochondria ratios. Internalization was assessed by flow cytometry and confocal colocalization analysis. Bioenergetic effects were quantified by Seahorse extracellular flux analysis; mitochondrial membrane potential and superoxide production were measured by flow cytometry; extracellular matrix protein expression was evaluated by immunofluorescence and RT-qPCR; and the inflammatory secretome was profiled by Luminex multiplex assay. RESULTS: Isolated platelet mitochondria preserved outer membrane integrity, membrane potential, and ADP-coupled respiratory activity prior to transplantation. They were efficiently internalized by OA chondrocytes in a dose-dependent manner, with optimal uptake observed at chondrocyte-to-platelet-equivalent mitochondria dose ratios of 1:100. Transplantation increased maximal respiratory capacity and spare respiratory reserve without altering basal respiration, was accompanied by elevated type II collagen and aggrecan protein levels, and selectively reduced secreted IL-1β and osteopontin while leaving IL-6, TNF-α, IL-10, and IL-1RA unchanged. Mitochondrial superoxide production was modestly increased and was prevented by the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoTEMPO, while mitochondrial membrane potential remained unchanged. CONCLUSIONS: Platelet-derived mitochondrial transplantation expands the respiratory reserve and modulates the catabolic-anabolic balance of human OA chondrocytes without inducing mitochondrial depolarization, providing a mechanistic basis for allogenic, blood-derived mitochondrial therapies in joint disease.

They were efficiently internalized by OA chondrocytes in a dose-dependent manner, with optimal uptake observed at chondrocyte-to-platelet-equivalent mitochondria dose ratios of 1:100.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Colistin remains a last-resort antibiotic for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet mobilized colistin resistance (MCR) genes threaten its continued utility. South Asia is a recognized hotspot for antimicrobial resistance, but the magnitude and distribution of MCR-mediated resistance across human, animal, food, and environmental sources in the region remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO CRD420261414120). Five databases were searched without date restriction. Study proportions were pooled using a random-effects binomial-normal generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with a logit link, the pre-specified primary analysis; the Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation with the DerSimonian-Laird estimator was used as a sensitivity comparison. Subgroup analyses were performed by country, setting, and publication period. Risk of bias was assessed using the JBI prevalence checklist. RESULTS: Thirty-four data points (7,407 isolates; 1,243 MCR-positive) from Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and India were included, drawn from 31 unique studies. Using the GLMM, the pooled MCR prevalence was 14.70% (95% CI 13.37-16.13%; I² ≈ 97.8%). The results remain unchanged when re-estimated with the Freeman-Tukey/DerSimonian-Laird sensitivity method (14.94%; 95% CI 7.98-23.49%). Bangladesh showed the highest country-level prevalence (37.34%; 95% CI 34.93-39.81%), while India showed the lowest (1.68%; 95% CI 0.98-2.86%). The animal and food compartment carried higher prevalence (35.69%; 95% CI 33.51-37.93%) than the clinical (3.87%; 95% CI 2.90-5.13%). mcr-1 was identified in 31 of 34 data points (91%). A directional temporal increase across successive publication periods reached statistical significance under GLMM-based logistic meta-regression (odds ratio 1.10 per year, 95% CI 1.06-1.15; p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: MCR-mediated colistin resistance is widely disseminated across South Asia and disproportionately concentrated in the animal-food reservoir. Coordinated One Health surveillance and regulatory action on colistin use in livestock are urgently needed.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Schizophrenia is a severe psychiatric disorder with a highly complex, polygenic architecture. Although whole-exome sequencing (WES) has identified rare coding variants conferring substantial risk, large-scale studies have predominantly focused on European populations, and the interplay between rare and common genetic risks remains largely elusive. Here, we present a comprehensive WES analysis of a Japanese cohort (3,831 cases and 5,119 controls), confirming a robust enrichment of ultra-rare protein-truncating variants (PTVs) and damaging missense variants in evolutionarily constrained and synaptic genes. To increase discovery power, we conducted a cross-population meta-analysis incorporating 32,729 cases and 108,160 controls, in which 13 previously reported risk genes were reconfirmed at exome-wide significance, while two additional genes,  ZMYM2  and  SLC6A1  , newly reached this threshold. The Japanese cohort strengthened evidence for the established SCHEMA risk gene  RB1CC1  and contributed qualifying variants supporting the associations of both additional genes. Within the same clinical cohort, we jointly evaluated carrier status for ultra-rare PTVs in known risk genes, pathogenic copy number variants (CNVs), and top-decile polygenic risk score (PRS) status. All three risk factors remained associated with schizophrenia after mutual adjustment. Our findings extend rare-variant evidence for schizophrenia to a Japanese population and support integrated assessment across rare coding, structural, and polygenic risk.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Occupational noise is a pervasive occupational hazard. While it is a well-established cause of hearing loss, only a few studies have suggested a potential association with cardiovascular diseases, and the evidence remains limited. Furthermore, individual susceptibility varies substantially, and metabolic characteristics, such as body mass index (BMI), may play a modifying role. OBJECTIVE: To systematically examine the effect of BMI modification on occupational noise exposure duration and hypertension risk. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among workers at an automobile manufacturing plant. Demographics, occupational history, and medical examinations were collected. Modified Poisson regression models were used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs). The modifying effect of continuous BMI was evaluated by incorporating an interaction term, with a sensitivity analysis performed using binary BMI classifications. Johnson-Neyman technique was used to determine the point at which the association was no longer statistically significant. RESULTS: There were 21.6% of participants with hypertension in this plant. Occupational noise exposure duration was positively associated with the risk of hypertension. The continuous BMI showed a significant negative interaction with noise exposure duration (PR = 0.987, 95% CI [0.979-0.995], P = 0.001). Specifically, at a BMI of 18.5 kg/m2, each additional year of noise exposure duration increased hypertension risk by 11.9% (PR = 1.119, 95% CI [1.047-1.196]); at a BMI of 24.0 kg/m2, this association was attenuated but remained significant (PR = 1.041, 95% CI [1.008-1.075]); and at a BMI of 28.0 kg/m2, no significant association was observed (PR = 0.987, 95% CI [0.956-1.019]). With Johnson-Neyman, the BMI value above which the estimated association was no longer statistically significant was identified at 27.02 kg/m2. In sensitivity analysis, treating BMI as a binary variable, the association between noise exposure duration and hypertension risk was attenuated and no longer statistically significant in overweight/obese individuals but remained significant in normal-weight individuals, and the negative interaction between noise exposure duration and BMI remained statistically significant (PR = 0.919, 95% CI [0.863-0.979], P = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: The association between occupational noise exposure duration and hypertension risk was modified by BMI in this cross-sectional study of automobile manufacturing workers. The association was more pronounced among normal-weight workers, whereas it was attenuated and no longer statistically significant at higher BMI levels. These findings suggest that BMI may be an important consideration in occupational health surveillance and hypertension risk assessment among noise-exposed workers, warranting further longitudinal investigation.

papers.abstract_full: Background Citrate anticoagulation during plateletpheresis can reduce ionized calcium and cause neuromuscular or gastrointestinal symptoms. Identifying donor and procedure-related factors may support earlier recognition and prevention. This study assessed factors associated with clinically identified citrate toxicity among plateletpheresis donors. Methods This analytical observational cross-sectional study included 60 plateletpheresis donors at Dhaka Medical College and Hospital, Bangladesh. Citrate toxicity was defined by any prespecified symptom or sign during the donation encounter. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance. The parsimonious adjusted model included pre-procedure oral calcium exposure, body mass index (BMI), pre-donation platelet count, and anticoagulant citrate dextrose solution A (ACD-A) volume. Calcium administration was non-randomized, and total and ionized calcium were not measured. Results All 60 donors were male; 28 (46.7%) developed citrate toxicity. Compared with donors without toxicity, affected donors had lower mean BMI (24.03 versus 25.56 kg/m2; p=0.020), lower pre-donation platelet count (2.53 versus 3.23×1011/L; p<0.001), and greater mean ACD-A exposure (333.39 versus 259.13 mL; p<0.001). In adjusted analysis, absence of pre-procedure calcium was associated with higher toxicity prevalence (adjusted PR {aPR} 4.42, 95% CI: 2.59-7.56), each 1 kg/m2 higher BMI with lower prevalence (aPR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.85-0.98), and each 50 mL higher ACD-A volume with higher prevalence (aPR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.24-2.18). Pre-donation platelet count was not independently associated after adjustment (aPR: 0.79 per 0.5×1011/L, 95% CI: 0.56-1.12). Conclusions Clinical citrate toxicity was common and was associated with absence of pre-procedure calcium, lower BMI, and greater ACD-A volume. These findings identify potential monitoring markers but do not establish causality because procedural factors and symptoms were recorded within the same encounter and ionized calcium was not measured. The calcium association should be interpreted as exploratory and hypothesis-generating, rather than as evidence of prophylactic efficacy.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic changed healthcare-seeking behaviour and clinical priorities, potentially influencing the detection of intestinal parasitic infections (IPIs). Data evaluating these effects remain limited. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective was to assess changes in the laboratory positivity rate of intestinal parasitic infections (IPIs) among clinically suspected patients during the COVID-19 pandemic, including the period of empirical ivermectin use. The secondary objective was to compare IPI positivity rates across different age and gender groups over the study period. METHODOLOGY: This was a retrospective laboratory-based observational study conducted at AIIMS Rishikesh from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2022. Stool samples underwent macroscopic examination, saline and iodine wet-mount microscopy, and modified Ziehl-Neelsen staining for coccidian parasites. The timeline was divided into three policy-defined periods: pre-COVID (January 1 to December 31, 2019), early COVID-19/ivermectin-included period (January 1, 2020, to August 31, 2021), and late COVID-19/post-ivermectin period (September 1, 2021-December 31, 2022). We applied a chi-square test and Bonferroni correction. Effect sizes are reported as prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Of 5,389 samples, 97 (1.80%) were confirmed positive for IPIs; 103 parasites were isolated from 97 patients, with five patients harbouring co-infections. Overall positivity rates were highest in the age group of 41-50 years (3.00%; 13/433) and comparable between male (1.88%; 64/3,405) and female (1.66%; 33/1,984) patients. The pre-COVID positivity rate (2.78%; 37/1,330) exceeded that of the early COVID period (1.14%; 17/1,493; PR = 2.44, 95% CI: 1.38-4.32; p = 0.001). papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Medication fields created for chronic-disease management may mislead when reused as medication-exposure measures in broader older-adult populations. Using routine exercise-frequency as routine-recorded physical activity (PA), we compared PA + records (daily, at least weekly, or occasional exercise) with PA- records (no exercise) and examined how nonblank medication-field presence changed after management-registration context was incorporated. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used 2,270 examination records from a 2025 rural primary-care program in northeastern China; PA was available for 2,226 records. The outcome was any nonblank text in the main-medication field. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with small-sample-adjusted cluster-robust inference across 20 sites. Sequential models incorporated demographics, site, and four hypertension/diabetes management-registration categories. Logistic regression estimated standardized proportions and absolute differences. Medication text underwent secondary audit, including 200 randomly sampled retained entries independently reviewed by two pharmacists. RESULTS: Nonblank medication fields occurred in 1,114/1,157 (96.3%) records with hypertension and/or diabetes management registration versus 27/1,113 (2.4%) with neither registration. Field presence was low without registration and near-complete with hypertension-only or dual registration; the diabetes-only stratum was small (n = 37). Overall field presence was 56.4% in PA+ and 42.8% in PA- records (PR 1.317, 95% CI 1.076-1.612). After registration context was incorporated, the PR was 1.001 (95% CI 0.960-1.043); full adjustment yielded 1.002 (95% CI 0.959-1.046). Standardized proportions were 51.26% and 51.14%, a difference of 0.12 percentage points (95% CI -2.07 to 2.30). Among 1,368 retained entries, archived labels classified 75.9% as antihypertensive, 14.5% as glucose-lowering, 0.5% as other cardiovascular, 1.7% as other medications, and 7.4% as unresolved. Inter-reviewer agreement for broad therapeutic class was 99.5% (κ = 0.982), and parser-manual-reference concordance was 99.0%; these assessments did not verify medication exposure. CONCLUSION: Nonblank main-medication-field recording was strongly patterned by chronic-disease management registration, and the apparent overall PA-related contrast was markedly attenuated after this context was incorporated. Blank fields cannot establish medication nonuse, and nonblank or consistently parsed text cannot establish complete, current medication exposure.
