papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Systemic inflammatory indices, linked to immunosenescence-related diseases, have not been thoroughly studied in hearing loss. This study aimed to determine whether systemic inflammatory indices are associated with hearing loss in midlife and later life. METHODS: This serial cross-sectional, community-based investigation was conducted within the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2020 in United States. Hearing loss was defined as a pure-tone average of ≥ 20 decibel hearing level at 0.5, 1, 2, and 4 kHz in the better ear. Six systemic inflammatory indices included systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), neutrophil lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and lymphocyte monocyte ratio (LMR). Prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) derived from modified Poisson regression models (with adjustment for potential confounding factors) represented the associations between each systemic inflammatory index and hearing loss. RESULTS: A total of 7920 adults aged 40-85 years were included. The mean (standard deviation) age was 58.6 (11.8) years, 4310 (54.4%) were women, and 2262 (28.6%) had hearing loss. After adjustment, hearing loss was associated with SIRI (PR 1.14, 95% CI, 1.08-1.20), SII (PR 1.07, 95% CI, 1.02-1.13), PIV (PR 1.11, 95% CI, 1.06-1.16), NLR (PR 1.10 95% CI, 1.04-1.17), and LMR (PR 0.87, 95% CI, 0.81-0.94). CONCLUSION: This study provides insights into the associations between systemic inflammatory indices and hearing loss, offering potential implications for risk stratification. While these indices are potential indicators for chronic inflammation in adults with hearing loss, further external validations are needed.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: The Home Owners' Loan Corporation (HOLC) created color-coded maps of more than 200 U.S. cities in the 1930s to facilitate mortgage lending, with redlined neighborhoods marked in red and assigned the "worst" grade (D). Historic redlining has persistent present-day consequences, although few studies have explored redlining in relation to cardiovascular disease risk factors. Cross-sectional associations between living in an area of historic redlining and prevalent obesity, hypertension, and diabetes were evaluated. METHODS: At enrollment, participants reported physician-diagnosed diabetes and hypertension, height, weight, and residential address. Redlining was based on available HOLC neighborhood grades (A/B/C/D) linked to participant addresses (N = 1653) at the census-tract level. Modified Poisson regression was used to determine prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for HOLC grade and obesity, hypertension, and diabetes. Effect measure modification was evaluated by race (Black/White) and oil spill cleanup worker status (yes/no). RESULTS: Historic redlining (D vs. A/B) was associated with a higher prevalence of obesity (PR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.09-1.87), hypertension (PR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.09-1.87), and diabetes (PR = 1.58, 95% CI: 0.71-3.48). In stratified analyses, associations of redlining (D vs. A/B/C) with hypertension (PR = 1.19, 95% CI: 0.91-1.55) and diabetes (PR = 1.47, 95% CI: 0.66-3.66) were suggested only among Black participants. Redlining was associated with obesity among workers (PR = 1.49, 95% CI: 1.23-1.82) but not among non-workers. CONCLUSION: Legacy consequences of historic redlining may negatively impact the cardiovascular health of present-day residents.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective for HIV prevention, but its real-world impact depends on sustained adherence. Long-acting injectable cabotegravir (CAB-LA) may reduce the burden of daily or event-driven pill use. In China, many oral PrEP users obtain medication online, but little is known about their prior CAB-LA awareness or willingness to consider it. OBJECTIVE: This study assessed prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA, reported barriers and facilitators, and associated factors among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online. METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed baseline data from the Real-world E-consumer Cohort of Oral PrEP (RECOPE), a prospective cohort in China. Participants completed a self-administered web-based questionnaire assessing prior CAB-LA awareness, hypothetical willingness after standardized CAB-LA information, sociodemographic characteristics, recent sexual behaviors and sexually transmitted infection (STI) diagnosis, and oral PrEP-related characteristics. Modified Poisson regression with robust SEs estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs. Primary regression analyses were restricted to sexually active participants. RESULTS: Among 621 oral PrEP users, the mean age was 29.9 (SD 6.4) years; all were assigned male sex at birth, and 608 (97.9%) identified as men. Overall, 216 of 621 (34.8%, 95% CI 31.1%-38.6%) participants reported prior CAB-LA awareness. After receiving standardized information, 428 of 621 (68.9%, 95% CI 65.2%-72.4%) participants expressed hypothetical willingness to use CAB-LA if it became available in China. Convenience was the most frequently reported facilitator among willing participants (395/428, 92.3%), whereas high cost was the most frequently reported barrier among those who did not express willingness (123/193, 63.7%). In adjusted analyses, event-driven PrEP users had a lower prevalence of prior CAB-LA awareness than daily PrEP users (aPR 0.66, 95% CI 0.50-0.86), whereas participants who had switched oral PrEP regimens in the past 3 months had higher prior awareness (aPR 1.34, 95% CI 1.07-1.68). Hypothetical willingness was more prevalent among participants reporting an STI diagnosis in the past 3 months (aPR 1.22, 95% CI 1.08-1.39) and chemsex (aPR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26), whereas higher PrEP-related stigma was associated with slightly lower willingness (aPR 0.99 per 1-point increase, 95% CI 0.98-0.99). CONCLUSIONS: Among oral PrEP users in China obtaining PrEP online, prior CAB-LA awareness was limited, whereas hypothetical willingness was common after standardized information was provided. Prior awareness differed by oral PrEP regimen and recent regimen switching, whereas willingness was associated with recent STI diagnosis, chemsex, and PrEP-related stigma. Convenience was a major appeal, while cost remained an important barrier. These findings support improving access to balanced PrEP information and addressing practical barriers as long-acting PrEP becomes more widely available.

papers.abstract_full: Pharmacogenomics integrates tumor molecular features with drug responses to support precision oncology, but biological domain shifts and optimization conflicts hinder transfer from screened cell lines to unlabeled patient tumors. We developed TRACER (Transfer of Response Across domains via Conflict-aware End-to-end Regulation), an end-to-end framework combining supervised drug-response prediction, biologically conditioned neighbor alignment and response-protected gradient regulation. By projecting only conflicting components of the auxiliary alignment gradient, TRACER preserves the response-optimization direction learned from experimental labels. Across ModelID-disjoint, seen-drug splits, TRACER-Full achieved a global Pearson correlation of 0.5125 $\pm $ 0.0192 on per-drug z-standardized test pairs, compared with 0.5179 $\pm $ 0.0193 for Response-only, a mean difference of $-0.0054$. Mean oncogenic Hallmark neighbor consistency increased by $0.1162 \pm 0.0210$ in alignment-excluded The Cancer Genome Atlas audit samples. At the patient level, a source-validation-defined drug partition and uniform stability analysis supported four predicted pharmacological response subtypes (PRSs) in breast invasive carcinoma (BRCA), four in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) and two in sarcoma (SARC). PRS-construction-excluded drugs characterized distinct predicted mechanism-level profiles, and pan-cancer indication recovery provided a lineage-aware internal consistency assessment of the patient rankings. TRACER provides an interpretable and auditable framework for response-preserving cross-domain alignment and it generates patient pharmacogenomic hypotheses for subsequent functional validation.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) mutation is a key molecular marker in gliomas and is generally associated with favorable prognosis. However, its dynamic changes and prognostic significance during tumor recurrence remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 42 patients with paired primary and recurrent glioma samples. IDH1 mutation status was determined by PCR, and the expression of IDH1 R132H protein was evaluated using a semiquantitative scoring system ranging from negative (-) to strongly positive (+++) based on expression intensity by immunohistochemistry (IHC). Changes in molecular features and WHO grade were analyzed, and their associations with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and postrecurrence survival (PRS) were evaluated using Cox regression models. RESULTS: IDH1 mutation status remained largely stable between primary and recurrent tumors, with most patients retaining their original genotype. In contrast, WHO grade progression was observed in 45.2% of cases, indicating ongoing tumor evolution. IDH1 R132H protein expression exhibited dynamic changes, with both upregulation and downregulation detected at recurrence. In primary tumors, IDH1 mutation was independently associated with improved PFS (HR = 0.351, p = 0.016), whereas higher IDH1 R132H expression was associated with improved OS (HR = 0.371, p = 0.032). In recurrent tumors, IDH1 mutation showed a trend toward inferior PRS, although this association did not reach statistical significance, suggesting that the prognostic relevance of IDH1 alterations may vary during glioma evolution. CONCLUSIONS: Although IDH1 mutation remains largely stable during glioma progression, its prognostic associations may vary between primary and recurrent disease. IDH1 R132H protein expression also shows dynamic changes and may provide complementary prognostic information. These exploratory findings support integrating genetic and protein-level biomarkers when evaluating glioma progression and warrant validation before informing the clinical application of IDH inhibitors.

papers.abstract_full: Most genetic studies of psychiatric disorders have been conducted predominantly in populations of European ancestry, limiting evidence for the transferability of polygenic scores (PGS) to other populations. This cross-sectional study evaluated the predictive performance of European-derived PGS for bipolar disorder (BD) and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) in an Indian sample. Participants (N = 2531) included individuals with BD (N = 463), OCD (N = 554), and controls (N = 1514) recruited from hospital- and community-based samples. Genotyping was performed using the Illumina Global Screening Array. PGS were derived from the summary statistics of European-ancestry genome-wide association studies using two Bayesian methods, PRS-CS-auto and SBayesRC. Principal component analyses demonstrated genetic overlap of the study population with other South Asian populations. BD PGS showed significant predictive performance, explaining approximately 6%-7% of liability-scale variance with PGS-only AUCs of ~0.71. OCD PGS showed lower but significant predictive performance, explaining ~2%-3% of variance with AUCs of approximately 0.59. Bayesian approaches showed better predictive performance than conventional clumping-and-thresholding. These findings demonstrate that European-derived psychiatric PGS can retain predictive information in an Indian population, although performance differed between disorders. The application of Bayesian PGS methods in this Indian cohort supports their utility for cross-ancestry prediction, while reinforcing the need for larger genomic studies in South Asian and other underrepresented populations.

papers.abstract_full: Background/Objective: Anemia patterns may differ between population and hospital-tested cohorts. This paper aims to examine anemia frequency and red-cell size across estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in hospital records. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 37,831 adults aged 18-100 years tested at King Khalid Hospital, Saudi Arabia, during 2017-2021. For each individual, one complete blood count (CBC) record and one creatinine record from the same calendar month were analyzed. eGFR was calculated using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation. Modified Poisson, logistic and natural cubic spline models adjusted for age, sex, and calendar year. Results: Anemia occurred in 8762 participants (23.2%): 22.9%, 17.1%, 34.6%, and 72.1% at eGFR ≥ 90, 60-89, 30-59, and <30 mL/min/1.73 m2, respectively. Relative to eGFR 60-89, adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs; 95% confidence intervals [CIs]) were 1.26 (1.19-1.33) for ≥90, 1.90 (1.75-2.07) for 30-59, and 3.98 (3.69-4.30) for <30. The association was nonlinear (p < 0.001). Among participants with anemia, the normocytic proportion increased from 56.6% at eGFR ≥ 90 to 82.7% at <30. In men, the adjusted normocytic-versus-microcytic odds ratio (OR) for <30 versus 60-89 was 2.70 (1.71-4.27). Conclusions: eGFR < 60 was associated with more frequent anemia. The proportion of anemia classified as normocytic was also greater in lower eGFR categories. Objective: To estimate the frequency of DEB screening positivity and examine associated characteristics in a Tunisian T2DM clinic sample. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 400 adults assessed between January and April 2023 using the Sick, Control, One stone, Fat, Food (SCOFF) questionnaire; Bulimic Investigatory Test Edinburgh (BITE); four-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-4); and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Exploratory analysis estimated crude prevalence ratios (PRs). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) came from a logistic model including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), diabetes duration, and PSS-4. Separate secondary models replaced PSS-4 with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale anxiety subscale (HADS-A) or depression subscale (HADS-D). Results: DEB positivity was 26.8% (107/400; 95% confidence interval [CI], 22.6-31.3%). Crude DEB prevalence was higher in women than men (30.4% versus 19.2%; PR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.06-2.35), in participants with HADS-A ≥11 versus <11 (PR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.64-3.17), and with HADS-D ≥11 versus <11 (PR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.08-2.05). In the primary adjusted model, DEB positivity was associated with younger age (aOR per year, 0.952; 95% CI, 0.922-0.982), higher BMI (aOR per kg/m2, 1.083; 95% CI, 1.042-1.126), and higher PSS-4 (aOR per point, 1.133; 95% CI, 1.067-1.203). HADS scores were positively associated in separate adjusted models. Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) was high in both groups (10.36% versus 9.91%; difference, 0.45 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.01 to 0.92). Conclusions: Approximately one-quarter of this clinic sample had a positive DEB screen. Associations with psychological symptoms support attention to eating concerns and emotional well-being in diabetes care. However, cross-sectional data limit causal interpretation, and future longitudinal studies are warranted.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in India. However, screening uptake still remains low. A family history of breast cancer may influence screening behavior through increased risk perception. These psychosocial determinants can be explained using the Health Belief Model (HBM), which further influences the decision to undergo cancer screening. This study aimed to compare the uptake of breast cancer screening methods [breast self-examination (BSE), clinical breast examination (CBE), and mammography] among women with and without a family history of breast cancer. Additionally, sociodemographic and HBM-related correlates of screening uptake were also assessed. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in Northern India among 224 women aged ≥30 years, including 112 women with a household family history of breast cancer (FH+) and 112 without (FH-). Data were collected using a pre-tested questionnaire covering sociodemographic details, screening practices, and HBM constructs. Screening uptake between groups was compared using the chi-square test. Univariate log-binomial regression was performed to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for factors associated with screening uptake. RESULTS: Women in the FH+ group had significantly higher uptake of CBE (33.0% vs. 17.9%; p = 0.009) and mammography (25.0% vs. 14.3%; p = 0.044) compared to the FH- group, while BSE uptake did not show any significant difference. Regression analysis supported these findings, with a higher uptake of CBE (PR = 1.9; 95% CI: 1.2-3.0) and mammography (PR = 1.8; 95% CI: 1.0-3.1), but not BSE. Age >50 years and employment were associated with higher CBE uptake, while postgraduate education and urban residence were associated with BSE uptake. Women with a family history reported higher mean scores for perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, and self-efficacy. CONCLUSIONS: Breast cancer screening uptake remains suboptimal in this population. Family history appears to influence provider-based screening more than self-examination practices. Interventions should prioritize increasing awareness and accessibility of CBE and mammography, particularly among women without a family history, along with an emphasis on psychosocial determinants of screening behavior.

papers.abstract_full: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, with a disproportionate burden in low- and middle-income countries and among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Understanding socioeconomic inequalities in NCD risk factors is important for developing targeted prevention strategies. This study assessed factors associated with socioeconomic inequalities in chronic NCD risk factors among adults in the DIMAMO Health and Demographic Surveillance System (HDSS) in rural South Africa. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 398 adults aged ≥18 years attending primary healthcare facilities within the DIMAMO HDSS catchment area. SES was measured using an asset-based wealth index derived through principal component analysis and categorized into quintiles. Data on tobacco use, harmful alcohol use, physical inactivity, low fruit and vegetable intake, high salt intake, self-reported hypertension, and diabetes, were collected using adapted WHO STEPS and SAGE questionnaires. Crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs and aPRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors. SES was not significantly associated with hypertension after adjustment. Participants in the richer (aPR = 1.58; 95% CI: 1.03-2.41) and richest (aPR = 1.78; 95% CI: 1.11-2.85) SES quintiles had a higher prevalence of harmful alcohol use than those in the poorest quintile. Physical inactivity was less prevalent among participants in the middle, richer, and richest quintiles. Tobacco use was less prevalent among females and participants with secondary or tertiary education. Self-reported diabetes tended to be more prevalent among richest quintile, although the association was not statistically significant. Age, sex, educational attainment, and employment status were associated with several NCD risk factors. Socioeconomic inequalities in NCD risk factors were evident in this rural population. Higher SES was associated with harmful alcohol use and a lower physical inactivity. These findings highlight complex socioeconomic patterning of NCD risk factors and support context-specific interventions and longitudinal research.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Neuroprotective therapies are frequently used for acute ischemic stroke in China. We examined associations of neurologists? self-rated familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations with reported prescribing frequency. Methods: A hospital-based quota survey recruited attending-level or senior neurologists involved in acute ischemic stroke care across mainland China from May 27 to July 16, 2025. High-frequency use was defined as prescribing neuroprotective therapy to at least 60% of patients. High familiarity and importance were ratings of 4 or 5 on 5-level scales; consistently high benefit expectations required ratings of 4 or 5 in all 4 scenarios. Modified Poisson generalized estimating equations estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) with hospital-clustered robust standard errors. Results: Among 1982 neurologists from 251 hospitals, 1007 (50.8%) were men and 1745 (88.0%) practiced in tertiary hospitals. High-frequency use was reported by 1596 respondents (80.5%), high familiarity by 1006 (50.8%), and consistently high benefit expectations by 1290 (65.1%). Lower familiarity with high-frequency use was reported by 743 respondents (37.5%). High familiarity (adjusted PR, 1.053; 95% CI, 1.007?1.102), high perceived importance (adjusted PR, 1.294; 95% CI, 1.148?1.458), and consistently high benefit expectations (adjusted PR, 1.198; 95% CI, 1.131?1.269) were associated with high-frequency use after adjustment for demographic and professional characteristics. Conclusions: Frequent self-reported neuroprotective prescribing coexisted with lower self-rated familiarity in a substantial subgroup. Familiarity, perceived importance, and benefit expectations were associated with prescribing frequency. These cross-sectional, class-level measures cannot establish prescribing appropriateness or causality. Studies linking drug-specific observed prescribing to indications and patient outcomes are needed.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Lingnan water villages in the Pearl River Delta, China, represent a unique form of living cultural and ecological heritage. Although their heritage and landscape values are widely recognized, less is known about how these everyday rural environments contribute to visitors' restorative experience and rural well-being. This study investigates the perceived restorative potential of Lingnan water village landscapes using the Perceived Restorativeness Scale (PRS), Attention Restoration Theory (ART), and structural equation modeling (SEM). Survey data were collected from 415 visitors across six representative villages. Results indicate that natural landscapes and traditional street-alley spaces form a dual foundation for restoration, while folk culture is particularly associated with psychological “Being Away” and fascination. The healing potential is not dominated by a single element but emerges from the synergy of ecology, spatial structure, and cultural practices. This study contributes to rural studies by reframing therapeutic landscapes as a mechanism of rural well-being, place-making, and differentiated revitalization in peri-urban heritage villages. It also offers practical implications for integrating ecological conservation, cultural continuity, and experience-oriented rural tourism.

papers.abstract_full: Polygenic scores for major depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder have been related to treatment outcome. We analysed 4,007 patients of European ancestry from 7 cohorts: three with major depression (STAR*D, GSRD, PANDORA), two with bipolar disorder (STEP-BD, Barcelona) and two with schizophrenia (CATIE, HSRRm). The three scores were computed with PRS-CS from the latest Psychiatric Genomics Consortium studies. The primary outcome was good response or good course, harmonized from each cohort’s instrument. Firth logistic regression within cohorts, adjusted for age, sex and ancestry components, was followed by random-effects pooling. A higher depression score was associated with lower odds of a good outcome (odds ratio per standard deviation 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.99, p = .04; false discovery rate q = .11). The estimate remained below one in all 8 sensitivity analyses, including adjustment for baseline severity, and was negative in all 5 cohorts with a continuous improvement measure. The schizophrenia score pointed the same way (odds ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.85-1.01) with no heterogeneity. The bipolar score showed no pooled effect (odds ratio 0.97), and its direction differed by diagnosis. In pooled data spanning three diagnoses, higher polygenic liability to depression was nominally associated with a less favourable treatment outcome, although the association did not survive correction for multiple testing; schizophrenia liability showed a similar directional trend. These findings support further evaluation of disorder liability in multivariable models of treatment outcome.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Methadone maintenance therapy is the standard treatment for opioid dependence during pregnancy, as its long half-life helps prevent relapse to short-acting abused opioids. However, the cellular mechanisms underlying methadone's neurodevelopmental toxicity remain poorly understood. Lipid dysregulation has emerged as a pathological feature in several neurological conditions and may contribute to cognitive impairment in children exposed to methadone in utero. OBJECTIVES: To determine whether methadone exposure alters lipid homeostasis in astrocytes and to assess whether such alterations are associated with cellular dysfunction and inflammatory responses. METHODS: Primary rat astrocytes were treated with methadone for three days. Lipid accumulation, lipid droplet formation, and lysosomal distribution were assessed using BODIPY-493/503, perilipin-2 immunostaining, and LysoTracker, respectively, followed by confocal microscopy and colocalization analyses. Ultrastructural changes were examined by electron microscopy. Lipid composition was quantified by mass spectrometry-based lipidomics. Findings were validated in cortical organotypic cultures and in the cortex of pups born to methadone-exposed dams using RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and ultrastructural analyses. Translational relevance was further assessed in primary human fetal astrocytes. RESULTS: Methadone exposure induced a dose and time-dependent accumulation of lysosomal lipids in primary neonatal rat astrocytes, independent of lipid droplet formation and opioid receptor activation. Electron microscopy revealed multilamellar bodies characteristic of drug-induced phospholipidosis, a known effect of many cationic amphiphilic drugs. Lipidomics confirmed elevated levels of ceramides and triglycerides. Methadone-treated astrocytes displayed impaired lysosomal degradation capacity, indicating functional compromise. Similar lysosomal and inflammatory alterations were observed in methadone-exposed organotypic cultures and in the cortex of offspring from methadone-treated dams. Human fetal astrocytes replicated these findings, demonstrating cross-species conservation. CONCLUSION: Methadone induces phospholipidosis and lysosomal dysfunction in astrocytes, accompanied by neuroinflammatory activation during brain development. These findings uncover an unrecognized mechanism linking methadone's amphiphilic properties to developmental neurotoxicity and emphasize the need to re-evaluate the safety of methadone use during pregnancy.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption is a critical pathological event contributing to secondary injury and poor outcomes following traumatic brain injury (TBI). While neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are known to exacerbate neuroinflammation, the precise molecular mechanisms by which they compromise cerebral microvascular integrity remain elusive. This study aimed to investigate the role of the NETs-AIM2 inflammasome axis in mediating endothelial damage and to explore the therapeutic potential of targeting this pathway. METHODS: A controlled cortical impact (CCI) mouse model was utilized to simulate TBI. NET formation was modulated pharmacologically using the peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitor Cl-amidine or genetically via adenoviral overexpression of PAD4. BBB permeability, brain edema, and cerebral blood flow (CBF) were assessed using Evans Blue extravasation, wet-to-dry weight ratio, T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, and laser speckle contrast imaging. Neurological function was evaluated via modified Neurological Severity Score (mNSS) and rotarod tests. Molecular mechanisms were dissected using Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and cell-type-specific co-localization analyses. RESULTS: TBI induced significant PAD4-dependent NET formation, peaking at day 3 post-injury, which temporally coincided with BBB breakdown and neurological deficits. Cl-amidine treatment effectively preserved tight junction proteins (zonula occludens-1, Occludin) and adherens junction protein (vascular endothelial-cadherin), reduced Evans Blue extravasation, attenuated brain edema and lesion volume, promoted CBF restoration, and improved mNSS scores and rotarod performance. Mechanistically, NETs acted as upstream danger signals that specifically triggered AIM2 inflammasome activation, which was predominantly localized in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells rather than glial cells. This endothelial-specific AIM2 activation subsequently initiated PANoptosis-a multifaceted cell death program characterized by simultaneous pyroptosis, necroptosis, and apoptosis-in the vascular endothelium. Pharmacological inhibition of AIM2 effectively suppressed all three death pathways and preserved BBB integrity. Adenoviral overexpression of PAD4 exacerbated endothelial PANoptosis, whereas AIM2 inhibition reversed these effects, establishing the causal relationship. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate a pathogenic axis wherein TBI-induced NETs drive endothelial PANoptosis via specific activation of the AIM2 inflammasome in cerebral microvascular endothelial cells, leading to BBB failure. Targeting this signaling cascade represents a promising therapeutic strategy to protect the neurovascular unit and improve functional recovery after TBI. Traumatic brain injury is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. After severe head injury, the brain’s protective barrier—which normally prevents harmful substances from entering the brain—often breaks down, allowing fluid and toxic materials to leak into brain tissue, causing dangerous swelling and further damage.In this study, we discovered a harmful chain reaction that destroys the brain’s protective barrier after injury. We found that immune cells called neutrophils release sticky web-like structures made of DNA into the injured brain. Although these DNA webs normally help fight infections by trapping germs, they cause serious harm in brain injury. These DNA webs trigger a molecular alarm system in the cells lining blood vessels in the brain. Once activated, this alarm system causes these cells to die through multiple pathways simultaneously, leading to the collapse of the brain’s protective barrier.Using mice with controlled brain injuries, we tested whether blocking this harmful process could protect the brain. We found that preventing DNA web formation or stopping the molecular alarm system significantly reduced blood vessel damage, decreased brain swelling, and helped injured mice recover better movement and coordination abilities.Our research identifies promising new targets for treating brain injury. By developing drugs that block either DNA web formation or the alarm system they trigger, we may be able to prevent barrier breakdown and improve recovery outcomes for patients. This is particularly important given that millions of people worldwide suffer traumatic brain injuries each year from vehicle accidents, falls, sports injuries, and violence.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), neurons surrounding the hematoma are highly vulnerable yet potentially salvageable. Our previous gene chip analysis suggested that the ASCL1-RET signaling axis is involved in neural injury after ICH. This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of RET in the perihematomal region after ICH. METHODS: We established an in vivo mouse model of ICH and in vitro primary astrocyte and neuronal culture models. RET expression and phosphorylation were examined by Western blotting and immunofluorescence. RET was silenced in astrocytes using shRNA lentivirus. Neuronal apoptosis was assessed by TUNEL assay and cleaved caspase-3 expression. The PI3K/AKT pathway was examined to explore the underlying mechanism. RESULTS: p-RET expression was significantly upregulated in the perihematomal region after ICH, peaking at day 1 and co-localizing with neurons, astrocytes, and microglia. Hemin stimulation of primary astrocytes induced astrocyte reactivity and RET phosphorylation. Conditioned medium from hemin-stimulated astrocytes reduced neuronal apoptosis, an effect abolished by RET knockdown in astrocytes. Changes in PI3K/AKT phosphorylation were associated with RET-dependent astrocyte-mediated neuroprotection. CONCLUSION: Astrocytic RET protects neurons from hemin-induced apoptosis and is associated with modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling, supporting a RET-dependent contribution to astrocyte-neuron crosstalk and suggesting RET as a potential therapeutic target for neuroprotection after ICH.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Arteriosclerosis obliterans (ASO) is a vascular occlusive disease characterized by pathological vascular remodeling, in which the aberrant behavior of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) plays a central role. The specific role of microRNA-140-5p (miR-140-5p) in ASO remains unclear. METHODS: Vascular tissue samples from ASO patients (n = 15) and healthy controls (n = 10) were analyzed. Expression of miR-140-5p and Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 Receptor (IGF1R) was measured by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and Western blot. The methylation status of the MIR140 promoter was assessed by bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP). Functional assays including EdU, Transwell, and flow cytometry were performed on cultured human VSMCs transfected with miR-140-5p mimic or inhibitor. A dual-luciferase reporter assay was used to verify the targeting relationship. An in vivo rat carotid artery balloon injury model was established. RESULTS: miR-140-5p expression was significantly downregulated in ASO tissues compared to controls, associated with hypermethylation of the MIR140 gene promoter. In vitro, overexpression of miR-140-5p inhibited VSMC proliferation and migration while promoting apoptosis. IGF1R was identified as a direct target gene of miR-140-5p, and its expression was upregulated in ASO tissues, showing an inverse correlation with miR-140-5p. Immunofluorescence double staining confirmed that IGF1R co-localized with α-SMA, a marker of VSMCs. To confirm functional mediation, we performed rescue experiments using an IGF1R expression construct lacking the 3'-UTR, which renders it resistant to miR-140-5p-mediated suppression. Forced expression of this construct counteracted the inhibitory effects of miR-140-5p on VSMC proliferation and migration, as well as reversed miR-140-5p-induced apoptosis, confirming that IGF1R is a key downstream effector. In the rat model, local delivery of a miR-140-5p agomir significantly attenuated neointimal hyperplasia following arterial injury. CONCLUSION: Promoter hypermethylation leads to silencing of miR-140-5p in ASO. Downregulation of miR-140-5p results in elevated IGF1R expression, which subsequently promotes VSMC dysfunction, contributing to ASO pathogenesis. These findings highlight the miR-140-5p/IGF1R axis as a potential therapeutic target, although the pro-apoptotic effect of miR-140-5p warrants careful evaluation of vascular integrity and safety in future translational studies.

papers.abstract_full: STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective multicenter cohort study. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament (OPLL) identifies a CT-defined fracture/dislocation-free injury phenotype in older patients with traumatic cervical spinal cord injury (SCI), whether midsagittal canal occupancy reflects admission neurological severity, and whether OPLL predicts AIS-grade conversion. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: OPLL is considered a structural substrate for cervical cord injury without bony failure after trauma. However, its roles as an injury-pattern marker, severity metric, and recovery predictor remain unclear. METHODS: We analyzed 328 patients aged ≥65 years with traumatic cervical SCI from a 7-center registry. OPLL was present in 117 (36%) and classified on CT by subtype. CT-defined fracture/dislocation-free injury was the mechanistic endpoint, and ≥1-grade AIS improvement the functional endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression, multiple imputation, and center-level and energy-stratified sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: OPLL-positive patients more often had fracture/dislocation-free injury (83% vs. 69%; adjusted OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.01-4.01). Estimates were consistent across sensitivity analyses, including multiple imputation (OR 2.20, 1.13-4.29), and numerically stronger after high-energy trauma (78% vs. 49%; interaction P=0.12). DISH showed the opposite association (OR 0.42, 0.20-0.89). Intramedullary T2 signal co-localized with the OPLL level in 94-98% of localizable T2-positive OPLL cases. Canal occupancy did not discriminate severe injury (AUC 0.44, 95% CI 0.29-0.59). OPLL was not associated with AIS-grade conversion (39% vs. 40%; OR 0.93, P=0.81) across sensitivity and fixed-time-point analyses. Age was the most consistent recovery predictor (OR 0.92/year, 95% CI 0.88-0.95). CONCLUSION: In older patients with traumatic cervical SCI, OPLL on emergency CT identifies a fracture/dislocation-free injury pattern and localizes the injured cord, supporting MRI evaluation of the ossified level even without fracture. OPLL neither grades severity by canal occupancy nor predicts AIS-grade conversion and is better interpreted as an anatomical rather than prognostic marker. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: 3.

papers.abstract_full: The draft genome sequence dataset of Serratia nematodiphila strain AMFE 036/1 was generated from an isolate obtained from Nham, a traditional Thai fermented beef sausage in Amnatcharoen province, Thailand. Whole-genome sequencing was performed using the DNBSEQ platform. Following quality filtering and preprocessing, 4,975,255 high-quality paired-end reads were retained, corresponding to an average sequencing depth of approximately 44×. A 5.4-Mbp draft genome comprising 53 contigs was generated by de novo assembly, with an N50 value of 245,680 bp and a GC content of 59.5%. Genome quality assessment using CheckM2 indicated a completeness of 100.00% and contamination of 0.07%, while BUSCO analysis yielded a completeness of 96.4% (pseudomonadota_odb12.2); both estimates indicate a near-complete genome. Genome annotation using the NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline identified 5,196 predicted genes, including 5,111 coding DNA sequences and 85 RNA genes. Functional annotation identified genes associated with hydrolytic enzyme activities, including five putative extracellular serralysin-family metalloprotease genes (EC 3.4.24.40), three of which were co-localised with cognate Inh-type metalloprotease inhibitor genes. Secondary metabolite biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) prediction using antiSMASH identified ten BGC regions across the genome, of which two exhibited 100% similarity to known clusters in the MIBiG database, corresponding to prodigiosin and yersinopine biosynthetic pathways. Genome-based taxonomic analyses confirmed the closest relationship with S. nematodiphila DSM 21420T (dDDH, 95.30%; ANIb, 99.17%; ANIm, 99.39%). The dataset can be used for comparative genomics, phylogenomics, genome mining, and functional annotation studies involving food-associated Serratia species.

papers.abstract_full: AIM: To investigate whether hypoxia-activated microglia drive pathological neovascularization through extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and endothelial integrin signaling, a mechanism that may function in parallel with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) signaling. METHODS: The oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) mouse model was used. Retinal phenotypes were assessed by flat mounts, histology, and vascular leakage assays. Key pathways were screened by transcriptomics and validated via Western blot, immunofluorescence, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). In vitro, brain microvascular endothelial cells were treated with conditioned medium from hypoxic microglia (Hyp-CM), with cell migration and tube formation assessed. Interventions employed the integrin β3 (ITGB3) inhibitor cilengitide, the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) inhibitor PF-573228 and a neutralizing anti-VEGF antibody. In vivo, cilengitide was administered by intravitreal injection to evaluate its therapeutic effect on neovascularization. RESULTS: OIR retinas showed significant avascularity, pathological neovascularization, and barrier disruption. Transcriptomics revealed activation of ECM-receptor interaction and focal adhesion pathways, with upregulation of Fn1 and Itgb3. Increased protein levels of fibronectin (FN) and ITGB3, alongside elevated phosphorylation of FAK and protein kinase B (Akt), were confirmed in vivo. Activated microglia co-localized with upregulated FN and ITGB3. Conditioned medium from Hyp-CM activated the ITGB3-FAK-Akt pathway in endothelial cells and promoted their migration and tube formation. These effects were nearly abolished by cilengitide or PF-573228. VEGF neutralization partially reduced Hyp-CM-induced migration and tube formation. Intravitreal injection of cilengitide significantly reduced retinal neovascularization in OIR mice. CONCLUSION: Hypoxia-activated microglia promote pathological angiogenesis, and the FN/ITGB3/FAK/Akt axis is identified as a key mediator of this process, revealing a novel mechanism that operates in parallel with VEGF signaling. Targeting this "hypoxia-microglia-ECM-integrin" axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome anti-VEGF resistance in ischemic retinopathy.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Ovarian cancer (OC) lethality is frequently associated with an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). While monocytes appear to function as notable regulators within the TIME, their causal involvement in OC pathogenesis remains poorly defined. METHOD: To investigate the causal involvement of monocytes in OC, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from the GEO and TISCH databases. Comparative cell proportion analysis was conducted using Fisher's exact test. Cell-cell communication networks were mapped with CellChat to characterize tumor-specific interactions via ligand-receptor pairs (e.g., MIF, MDK). Causal associations were identified through Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-sample MR, integrating eQTLGen statistics (n = 31,684) with OC GWAS data (1,588 cases). Instrumental variables were prioritized based on F-statistics > 10 and LD clumping. Bayesian colocalization and the HEIDI test (P > 0.05) were employed to rule out linkage disequilibrium. Finally, functional roles of candidate genes were validated via qRT-PCR, Western blot, and in vitro polarization assays. RESULT: Quantitative analysis revealed a significant enrichment of monocytes in the OC group (24.58%) compared to healthy controls (2.44%, P < 0.001), which was independently validated by immunofluorescence staining. CellChat identified tumor-specific signaling axes, including MIF-(CD74 + CXCR4) and MDK-NCL, that were predominantly active in the OC microenvironment but nearly quiescent in healthy tissues. We identified five monocyte-related genes-SGK1, PRKCA, TBC1D4, VPS8, and PPFIBP2-that demonstrated consistent causal associations with OC risk and passed the HEIDI test (P > 0.05), ruling out linkage disequilibrium. Functional enrichment suggested these genes modulate PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling. In vitro assays confirmed that SGK1 is specifically upregulated in M2-polarized macrophages. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of SGK1 using si113 significantly reversed the immunosuppressive M2 phenotype and impaired tumor cell invasion, highlighting its potential as a precision therapeutic target. CONCLUSION: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics and MR to identify five monocyte-related genes causally linked to OC risk. Among them, SGK1 may play a substantial role in promoting immunosuppressive macrophage polarization and may represent a promising therapeutic target to remodel the TIME and enhance anti-tumor immunity in OC.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Receptor activity-modifying protein 3 (RAMP3) has been implicated in stromal regulation in cancer. However, its role in tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling and immune checkpoint resistance remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to define the role of RAMP3 in shaping the immunosuppressive TME and evaluate its potential as a therapeutic target to enhance immunotherapy responses. METHODS: We used syngeneic mouse models of breast cancer with genetic manipulation of RAMP3 to investigate tumor progression, immune remodeling, and response to immune checkpoint blockade in vivo. Tumor growth, metastasis, and survival were evaluated. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on murine tumor tissues, and a publicly available spatial transcriptomic dataset was analyzed to characterize immune cell states and spatial organization within the TME. Human breast cancer datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas were analyzed to assess the clinical relevance of RAMP3-associated immune signatures. RESULTS: Our results suggest that RAMP3 contributed to the establishment of an immunosuppressive TME. In mouse models, RAMP3 deletion suppressed primary tumor growth, reduced lung metastasis, and improved survival. These effects were associated with a shift from M2-like tumor-associated macrophages to antigen-presenting macrophage states, increased CD8+ T cell infiltration, and reduced T cell exhaustion. Mechanistically, RAMP3 deficiency was associated with reduced IL-4/STAT6 signaling in macrophages and decreased expression of immunosuppressive genes, including the chemokine CCL8. Pharmacological inhibition of CCL synthesis phenocopied the effects of RAMP3 deficiency, and RAMP3 deficiency enhanced the efficacy of PD-1 blockade. Spatial transcriptomic analysis demonstrated co-localization of RAMP3 and CCL8 within the TME. In the TCGA-BRCA cohort, a higher weighted RAMP3/CD163/CD8A risk score was associated with poorer overall survival and remained significantly associated with overall survival in complete-case multivariable Cox models adjusted for clinicopathological variables. CONCLUSIONS: RAMP3 was identified as a potential regulator of the immunosuppressive TME and its functional impact was demonstrated in vivo. Integration with human clinical datasets supports further investigation of RAMP3 as a potential therapeutic target for overcoming resistance to immune checkpoint therapy in breast cancer.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Low socioeconomic position (SEP) is a significant determinant of poor health. The embodiment of SEP into biology functioning and then on health status involves chronic stress mechanisms, which may be measured by allostatic load (AL). This article examines how different dimensions of SEP, representing life-course exposures shape AL trajectories, according to sex. We aim to provide evidence of this relationship over time through repeated biological measurements, which is rarely done in the literature. METHODS: We used five waves of the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA), including 12,135 participants. We measured AL using nine biomarkers at four time points, enabling individual AL trajectories over up to 15 years, and estimated average sex-specific trajectories between ages 50 and 90. SEP variables were ordered along the life course: education, occupation, and wealth. We used mixed-effects models to assess the impact of SEP on AL trajectories, including a sex interaction to examine sex-specific trajectories. RESULTS: AL increased until age 80, then declined, with women exhibiting higher AL trajectories than men. Lower education was associated to higher AL trajectories, after adjusting for confounders, comorbidities, health behaviours, and anthropometrics. Lower wealth remained significantly associated with higher AL trajectories, whereas the association with manual occupation was no longer observed. The observed social gradient in health, whereby the higher one's social position, the better one's health, shows differences between men and women. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight complex lifecourse mechanisms underlying social inequalities in health and sex-specific patterns, supporting the need for targeted interventions to address health inequities.

papers.abstract_full: Background  Ovarian aging poses a serious threat to women’s reproductive health. Medicine–food homology (MFH) herbs, owing to their favorable safety profile and suitability for long-term use, have become important interventional resources. However, conventional formula screening relies largely on empirical statistics and lacks mechanistic evidence and a systematic screening strategy. Methods  In this study, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis, human-use evidence mining, UPLC/Q-TOF-MS chemical profiling and pretrained protein–molecular representation models to establish a multi-strategy framework for the discovery of MFH herbal combinations. Single-cell transcriptomic datasets related to ovarian aging from the GEO database were analyzed to identify key pathological processes and candidate targets. High-frequency MFH herbs were selected by mining classical prescriptions and clinical literature. By comparing six protein–molecular pretrained representation combinations, ESM-T5 was identified for compound–target affinity prediction and validated by molecular dynamics simulation and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays, ultimately identifying the Astragalus–ginseng (Huangqi–Renshen) herb pair (HXF) as the core candidate. Functional expression validation of key targets was performed, and the efficacy of HXF and the expression of related molecules were verified in a D-gal-induced KGN granulosa cell senescence model and a cyclophosphamide-induced rat model of diminished ovarian function. Results  Single-cell analysis revealed that ovarian aging was characterized by impaired steroidogenesis, enhanced MDK–NCL communication between granulosa cells and immune cells, and extracellular matrix remodeling, with CYP19A1, SERPINE1 and MDK as key targets. By further integrating human-use evidence mining and UPLC/Q-TOF-MS compound annotation, an MFH compound library comprising 712 molecules was established. ESM-T5 prediction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and SPR assays confirmed that multiple constituents of Astragalus and ginseng exhibited favorable binding activity toward key targets. At the cellular level, knockdown of MDK or SERPINE1 attenuated the senescence phenotype, whereas knockdown of CYP19A1 aggravated it. Its effects may be associated with promoting steroidogenesis, suppressing SERPINE1/IL18-related inflammation and matrix remodeling, and modulating MDK–NCL signaling. These findings provide a strategic reference for the mechanism-oriented discovery of MFH herbal combinations. Further molecular simulation, functional expression validation, in vitro cell assays and in vivo animal experiments showed that Astragalus–ginseng ameliorated diminished ovarian function and aging-related phenotypes. This provides a scalable strategic reference for the mechanism-oriented screening of MFH herbal combinations and for the development of intervention strategies against complex diseases.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (G…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]). FINDINGS: Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups. INTERPRETATION: Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes. TRANSLATION: For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.abstract_full: The large-scale annotation and spatiotemporal characterisation of cis-regulatory promoters and enhancers remain limited in many non-model organisms, largely due to fragmented availability of multiomic datasets across species and developmental conditions. Heliconius butterflies, which have been used to investigate wing development and patterning, have provided key insights into the genetic architecture underlying morphological diversification and adaptive pigmentation. Despite this, we are limited in what we understand of how cis-regulatory dynamics drive phenotypic wing patterning variation. Here, by re-analysing and re-evaluating available data, we present a comprehensive new description of a cis-regulatory atlas for Heliconius wing development by integrating chromatin accessibility dynamics (ATAC-seq) with histone modification profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me3). High-confidence peak sets enabled robust annotation of promoters and enhancers, revealing regulatory distributions consistent with canonical regulatory organisation. Promoters displayed comparatively higher conservation of transcription factor motifs, whilst enhancers exhibited greater sequence diversity, broader genomic distributions and more variable motif repertoires. Comparative analysis revealed cis-regulatory divergence to be primarily temporal, with substantial chromatin remodelling and differential histone enrichment across development, while regulatory dynamics were highly conserved between forewing and hindwing tissues. Extending these experimentally characterised regulatory landscapes, a convolutional neural network was trained for sequence-based enhancer prediction, achieving test AUROC and AUPRC values of 0.909 and 0.913, respectively. Predictions across 34 Heliconiini assemblies displayed significant enrichment within independently characterised accessible chromatin and conserved non-exonic elements (CNEEs), supporting their putative regulatory function. Overall, this study provides a large-scale characterisation of cis-regulatory dynamics and extends enhancer annotation across Heliconiini, providing a foundation for comparative investigations of regulatory conservation and diversification.

papers.abstract: The study of complex disorders is limited by the lack of structured data sets that integrate genetic association signals with rich functional annotations. papers.abstract_full: The study of complex disorders is limited by the lack of structured data sets that integrate genetic association signals with rich functional annotations. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) provide large collections of associated variants, these are heterogeneous, study-dependent, and not directly suitable for machine learning applications. Although frameworks such as Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) offer comprehensive variant-level features, there is no standardised procedure to construct curated, balanced, and reproducible data sets for the systematic study of complex traits. We introduce a scalable and reproducible pipeline for generating CADD-annotated variant data sets associated with complex disorders defined via Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) terms. The pipeline integrates GWAS summary statistics, genome mapping, chromosome-stratified negative sampling, and large-scale annotation, while addressing class imbalance and feature redundancy. The resulting data sets provide curated, balanced, and annotation-rich representations of variant–trait associations, suitable for statistical learning, systematic model evaluation and comparison, and analysis of functional annotation contributions and interactions.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients face a significantly elevated risk of heart failure (HF), but population-level evidence and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We aimed to assess the RA-HF association using national data and identify dietary compounds targeting shared inflammatory pathways. METHODS: We analyzed NHANES data (n=2,931) and performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Integrated machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, clinical samples, and in vitro experiments identified therapeutic targets and evaluated the effectiveness of dioscin (a yam-derived saponin). RESULTS: The rate of HF in RA patients is high, and RA patients with HF have a worse prognosis. MR analysis also revealed that RA was a significant HF risk factor. IL15RA emerged as a shared causal target, whose silencing suppressed TNF-α-induced ICAM-1 in endothelial cells and reduced M1 (CD86+) macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, MIF signaling were strongly implicated in the crosstalk between endothelial cells and macrophages. Dioscin bound IL15RA and reduced its expression in both cell types, phenocopying IL15RA silencing. CONCLUSION: This study identifies IL15RA as a key therapeutic target linking RA and HF, and dioscin as a dietary phytochemical with anti-inflammatory potential. Our findings provide a population-based framework and a readily translatable nutritional strategy for mitigating cardiac comorbidity in RA patients.

papers.abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. papers.abstract_full: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. Yet, in clinical practice the molecular information that matters most to a surgeon-IDH status, 1p/19q codeletion, and methylation class-typically arrives days to weeks after the operation it was meant to inform. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to close that gap. Over the past several years, a growing body of work has demonstrated that AI models can extract diagnostically relevant molecular and histological information from data sources available in the operating room, in real time, at the point of surgical decision-making. In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art intraoperative AI models available to neurosurgeons during brain tumor resections. They examine AI-augmented approaches to established intraoperative techniques, such as cryosection and fluorescence-guided surgery, before turning to novel technologies including nanopore sequencing and stimulated Raman histology (SRH). The authors conclude by discussing barriers to widespread clinical adoption and what lies ahead for this field. For cryosection, models such as LGNet and the Cryosection Histopathology Assessment and Review Machine (CHARM) have demonstrated strong performance on intraoperative discrimination of primary CNS lymphoma and molecular subtyping of glioma, respectively, with CHARM achieving areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88-0.93 across glioma subtypes. In fluorescence-guided surgery, hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning has enabled classification of tumor type, grade, and IDH mutation based on the 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA) signal with up to 93% accuracy, extracting molecular information from a modality already present in the operating room. For nanopore-based methylation classification, ensemble models such as Rapid Nanopore Brain Intraoperative Classification (ROBIN) have achieved 90% concordance with the final diagnosis prospectively in under 2 hours. In SRH, foundation models for infiltration detection now outperform FLAIR, contrast enhancement, and 5-ALA fluorescence in identifying tumor margins, while molecular classification models have achieved over 90% glioma subtype accuracy in multi-institutional cohorts. At the single-cell level, morphometric profiling of SRH images has revealed nuclear features distinguishing IDH-mutant from IDH-wildtype tumors, opening new avenues for interpretability. Despite this progress, widespread adoption remains limited by the absence of randomized clinical trials demonstrating patient-level benefit. Addressing this gap and realizing the potential of multimodal AI systems that integrate imaging, pathology, and molecular data represent critical next steps for the field.

papers.abstract_full: Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy shaped by genetic alterations and cytokine-mediated immune interactions. However, integrative characterization of cytokine-related regulators using genetic, single-cell, and computational approaches remains limited. This study aimed to identify genetically supported cytokine-related candidates in breast cancer, characterize their immune and cellular contexts, and explore their potential regulatory and therapeutic relevance. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to identify differentially expressed cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction-related genes, followed by two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), functional enrichment, immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, CellChat analysis, in silico gene perturbation, AI-assisted compound screening, and molecular docking. A total of 882 differentially expressed genes and 20 cytokine-related candidates were identified. MR provided the most consistent support for CXCL10, with genetically predicted higher expression associated with increased breast cancer risk (OR = 1.112, 95% CI: 1.026-1.206, p = 0.010). PRLR was significant only in the IVW analysis and was therefore considered a candidate requiring further validation. The CXCL10/PRLR model achieved an AUC of 0.810 (95% CI: 0.774-0.846) for discriminating breast cancer from normal samples. CXCL10 was predominantly associated with immune-cell populations, interferon-related programs, and predicted chemokine communication. In silico perturbation, AI-assisted screening, and docking further generated computational hypotheses regarding CXCL10-associated regulation and candidate compounds. CXCL10 represents a genetically supported immune-associated candidate in breast cancer. Overall, the findings are computational and hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts and experimental models.

papers.abstract: Cutaneous scarring spans regenerative and normal remodelling; keloid, hypertrophic, atrophic and contractile outcomes; dyspigmentation; radiation- and inherited-fragility-associated fibrosis; and rare malignant transformation. papers.abstract_full: Cutaneous scarring spans regenerative and normal remodelling; keloid, hypertrophic, atrophic and contractile outcomes; dyspigmentation; radiation- and inherited-fragility-associated fibrosis; and rare malignant transformation. Diagnostic labels alone do not capture the molecular, cellular, spatial and clinical states that shape these outcomes. This review is the first to treat the whole cutaneous scar spectrum, rather than keloid and hypertrophic scar alone, as a single computable phenotype space, and to audit jointly the provenance of the underlying datasets and the depth of validation of the resulting models. We searched four sources (PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex and Crossref) on 20 June 2026 and combined systematic searching with evidence mapping; 26,575 records were identified, 920 entered the evidence map and 120 were prioritised for synthesis. Bulk studies identify tissue-level fibrotic programmes, whereas single-cell and spatial approaches resolve fibroblast, immune, endothelial and epithelial states and niches. Evidence remains concentrated in keloid and hypertrophic scar, and often reuses public datasets or extrapolates from associated cutaneous-fibrosis systems. Atrophic scars are represented mainly by quantitative imaging and treatment studies: topography and dermal loss are measurable, but no mature molecular or spatial atlas is available and atrophic acne scars are usually excluded from molecular cohorts. Scar pigmentation lacks interoperable labels, calibrated colour measurement, melanocyte-resolved spatial resources and skin-tone-stratified assessment. Fourteen studies applied artificial intelligence directly to scar data, but only one explicitly reported independent external validation. Molecular biomarkers and treatment-response models remain at discovery or internal-validation stages. Future work should standardise multidimensional phenotypes, build prospective skin-tone-stratified cohorts across the full scar spectrum, resolve rare populations such as melanocytes, and complete causal and external validation before clinical deployment. Scars are not one condition. A burn, a surgical incision, trauma or acne can heal into a flat mature scar, a raised keloid or hypertrophic scar, a sunken atrophic scar, a tight contracture, or an area of changed skin colour. Most laboratory research on scars has studied keloids and raised scars, so the other scar types are much less well understood, and treatments still depend mainly on scar type, site and clinical experience. New laboratory and computer methods are changing this. Sequencing single cells, mapping molecules within tissue slices, and measuring scars with cameras, ultrasound and stiffness devices can describe a scar in far more detail than a clinical photograph, and artificial intelligence can use these measurements to predict how a scar may behave. These tools help only if scars are described in the same way, if the measurements are calibrated, and if the results hold up in new patients. This review maps the available evidence across the whole scar spectrum. It shows that molecular studies still concentrate on keloids and raised scars, that atrophic scars are studied mainly by imaging, and that changes in scar colour are measured inconsistently. Of the 14 studies that applied artificial intelligence to scar data, only one tested its model on independent data. We conclude that clearer descriptions of scar type, prospective and representative patient groups, experiments that test cause and effect, and independent testing are needed before these methods can guide treatment.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Ranked as the fifth leading global health burden in 2022, diabetes mellitus is the driver of diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a condition responsible for nearly half of end-stage kidney disease cases. Despite its significant impact, therapeutic progress in DKD is hindered by an incomplete understanding of the underlying cell-specific molecular mechanisms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing data (GSE183276) from the kidney precision medicine project, including kidney samples from 20 healthy individuals and 14 DKD patients, were obtained. After quality control, batch effect correction, and cell type annotation, cell type-specific differentially expressed genes were identified. Enrichment analyses were performed using WebGestalt. Trajectory inference was conducted to characterize dynamic cellular states. Finally, DrugTar, a previously developed deep learning tool, was applied to identify the most druggable genes. RESULTS: Among the 22 annotated cell types, collecting duct principal cells exhibited the largest number of differentially expressed genes, even after adjustment for cell abundance. This finding was also observed in an independent human kidney single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE211785), suggesting that this cell type experiences a profound transcriptional reprogramming in response to a diabetic milieu. Notably, trajectory analysis revealed distinct transcriptional states within principal cells, with mitochondrial metabolic processes being enriched across these subpopulations. Furthermore, a list of the most druggable genes is proposed as potential candidates for targeted delivery to principal cells. CONCLUSION: This study underscores the significant transcriptional reprogramming of principal cells in DKD pathogenesis, a phenomenon that has rarely received attention in previous works. These cells can be considered as candidates in strategies aimed at targeted drug delivery for DKD.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. This study provides a comprehensive characterization of the transcriptomic landscape, cellular composition, and immune architecture of lung adenocarcinoma using multiomics approaches. METHODS: Gene expression data were obtained from GEO (GSE131907) and TCGA-LUAD (n = 526). LRCD gene sets were curated from GeneCards, MSigDB, and published literature. Analyses included differential expression profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE131907, n = 11,376 cells), GSEA, and cell-cell communication mapping. A LASSO-based prognostic model with 10-fold cross-validation was built and validated across three independent cohorts using ROC and Kaplan-Meier analyses. RESULTS: Fourteen prognostically relevant genes were identified, including protective factors (BTK, CLNK, CTSG; HR < 1) and risk factors (CTSV, HMOX1; HR > 1). Single-cell analysis profiled 11,376 cells from one primary tumor and one normal lung sample. The prognostic model achieved moderate-to-good discrimination (AUC : 0.545-0.692) and effectively stratified patients by risk. Model genes correlated significantly with immune cell infiltration and checkpoint expression across risk groups, and functional enrichment highlighted immune trafficking, cytokine signaling, and cell adhesion pathways. CONCLUSIONS: This multiomics study identifies reliable LRCD-based prognostic markers and offers mechanistic insights into lung adenocarcinoma biology, with potential utility for clinical risk stratification.

papers.abstract_full: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a major cause of end-stage renal disease, involves podocyte injury and immune dysregulation. We integrated GEO transcriptomic datasets to identify 839 differentially expressed genes and 33 differential mitophagy-related genes via differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Machine learning identified six candidate diagnostic biomarkers, SLIRP, BLVRB, ATP6V1F, COX5B, TMEM14A, and TRMT112, with moderate-to-good discriminatory capacity across cohorts. xCell analysis revealed extensive renal immune remodeling in FSGS with expanded pro-inflammatory cells, diminished naive T cells and Tregs, and tight correlations between hub genes and immune profiles. Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis suggested a trend of downregulation of hub genes in FSGS podocytes, alongside suppressed transcriptomic signatures of mitochondrial energy metabolism and mitophagy-related pathways. qRT-PCR and western blot validated their downregulation at the whole-renal-tissue level in FSGS mouse models. These six genes may serve as diagnostic candidates and provide research clues for exploring mitophagy mechanisms in FSGS.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: High-grade gliomas (HGGs) are aggressive primary brain tumors with high recurrence rates and poor prognosis. Survival benefit from adjuvant temozolomide (TMZ) varies substantially across patients, and reliable preoperative biomarkers for treatment stratification remain limited. This study aims to develop an interpretable multimodal deep learning model integrating whole-slide histopathological images and multiparametric MRI to preoperatively predict survival benefit from adjuvant TMZ in HGG patients. METHODS: A Transformer-based multimodal fusion model was proposed. Key tumor regions were identified from whole-slide pathology images via weakly supervised clustering, and pathological features were extracted using attention-based multiple instance learning. Concurrently, 2.5D tumor subregional features were derived from multiparametric MRI sequences. These multimodal features were deeply fused using a Transformer encoder. The model was developed and validated on a multicenter cohort (504 patients), and its biological basis was explored through transcriptomic analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, protein-protein interaction networks, and immune deconvolution. RESULTS: The fusion model achieved AUCs of 0.910, 0.861, and 0.833 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis implicated DNA damage repair processes in high-benefit patients, suggesting that enhanced DNA repair capacity may contribute to TMZ sensitivity. Immune deconvolution showed higher M1 macrophage infiltration and lower regulatory T cell abundance in the high-benefit group, consistent with a less immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Importantly, low-benefit patients who completed TMZ chemotherapy had shorter survival than those treated with concurrent chemoradiotherapy alone or surgery alone. CONCLUSION: This model identifies patients unlikely to benefit from standard TMZ chemotherapy, providing a tool for postoperative personalized treatment stratification and optimization of therapeutic strategies in HGGs.

papers.abstract_full: Platelet RNA profiling is a promising liquid biopsy approach, offering minimally invasive insights into systemic diseases, such as cancer. Yet, the effect of leukocyte-associated RNA retention on platelet transcriptomic signatures remains unclear. This study provides the first comprehensive evaluation of how leukocyte-associated RNA retention influences platelet RNA sequencing and machine learning (ML)-based cancer detection. Using the largest publicly available platelet transcriptomic dataset (2351 human RNA samples) and single-cell/single-platelet RNA sequencing from 29 donors, we quantified leukocyte-associated RNA retention in matched sample groups (low vs. high retention) via a novel 132-gene leukocyte marker panel. Diagnostic implications were assessed using 10 ML algorithms for binary classification (cancer vs. healthy), examining the contribution of leukocyte-derived transcripts. Interestingly, models trained on high-retention samples often showed slightly improved performance, suggesting complementary diagnostic value from leukocyte signals. Importantly, post hoc correction using remove unwanted variation (RUV) and linear modeling effectively mitigated retention effects. However, adding the leukocyte-associated RNA retention score to the full-cohort classifier changed cancer-detection AUC only minimally (0.9247 to 0.9249). Thus, whether this signal should be corrected, recalibrated, or reported should depend on the study question rather than assuming routine removal.
