papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Bull fertility is a key parameter in the dairy cattle industry, with significant economic implications. DNA methylation is an epigenetic mark essential for fertility, and recent works have highlighted sperm DNA methylation as a promising source of biomarkers for male fertility, but no operational tool has been developed for predicting bull fertility based on DNA methylation. Here, we leveraged existing methylation data to evaluate the potential of DNA methylation for predicting bull fertility with machine learning models. RESULTS: Our study was conducted on a cohort of 351 Holstein commercial bulls, classified as subfertile, neutral and fertile based on a field fertility index (non-return rate of the inseminated cows after 56 days post-insemination). This dataset includes the largest cohort assembled for bull fertility prediction from epigenetic markers. We developed classification models to discriminate subfertile and fertile individuals using a subset of predictors derived from reduced representation bisulfite sequencing data obtained on frozen semen. Four machine learning algorithms were compared: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Neural Networks. To optimize performances of each algorithm and conduct an unbiased assessment of classification accuracy, we used a three-fold cross-validation before final testing on an independent test set. To increase the robustness of the results, model performances were averaged over 20 partitions of the data into training and test sets, to account for variability in bull distribution across sets. All models performed better than random classification. The best model was LASSO according to classification accuracy (0.62) and Random Forest according to Area Under Curve (0.69) computed with the independent test set. CONCLUSIONS: Even with this moderate performance, our models would lead to a 12.4% point increase of the probability of identifying subfertile individuals. These results suggest that sperm DNA methylation holds potential as a relevant source of predictive markers for bull fertility.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Although macrophage-mediated inflammation is associated with UC progression, its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to identify UC-associated molecular biomarkers and explore their roles in immune dysregulation. METHODS: Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multi-algorithm machine learning. The machine-learning model was evaluated in independent validation cohorts, and a nomogram was subsequently constructed and evaluated in an additional colonic-tissue cohort. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, pseudotime analysis, and scTenifoldKnk-based virtual knockout were used to investigate hub genes. RT-qPCR, WB, and IHC validated the findings in a DSS-induced mouse model and clinical samples, while siRNA-mediated LILRB3 knockdown was performed in THP-1-derived macrophages. RESULTS: Differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 55 candidate genes. Through screening of 127 machine-learning algorithm combinations, DPP10, LILRB3, MTMR11, and SLC6A14 were identified as UC-associated molecular biomarkers. A separately constructed logistic regression nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.989. LILRB3 was predominantly expressed in myeloid cells, particularly M1 macrophages, and was associated with inflammatory immune cell infiltration. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that LILRB3⁺ M1 macrophages exhibited active intercellular communication involving MHC-II-CD4 and other inflammation-related signaling pathways. Experimental validation showed increased PirB expression in the colonic tissues of DSS-induced colitis mice and elevated LILRB3 expression in human UC colonic tissues. Knockdown of LILRB3 in THP-1-derived macrophages significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β mRNA expression. CONCLUSION: LILRB3 is a candidate UC-associated molecular biomarker in colonic tissue and may be associated with proinflammatory macrophage remodeling and myeloid immune dysregulation, warranting mechanistic investigation.

papers.abstract_full: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the common mental disorders affecting children and is often diagnosed with an important delay. This neurodevelopmental disorder is usually identified by symptoms such as a deficit in attention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness. There are clinical and data-oriented methods for ADHD diagnosis. Recently, artificial intelligence techniques for ADHD diagnosis have been taken into consideration. In this article, we have reviewed state-of-the-art deep learning and classical machine learning networks using a wide range of neuroimaging, neurosignal and related data, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetoencephalography (MEG), questionnaires, genome data, mo-tion data, performance tests and game simulation. In addition, we identified common validation methods and analyzed them. As an important aspect for clinicians, the brain regions of ADHD patients identified as discriminative by existing machine learning-based studies are investigated. In the end, we identify exiting research gaps, notably the lack of publicly available large-scale multimodal datasets, non-interpretability and inexplicability of many algorithms and the use of architectures that are unable to efficiently model the spatiotemporal features of the brain. Ultimately, we hope that researchers will implement explainable machine learning-based studies that use several neuroimaging modalities to aid clinicians in supporting their decisions for diagnosis, prognosis and for treatment planning.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide, and liver fibrosis stage is the strongest determinant of long-term morbidity and mortality in affected patients. However, the molecular switches driving the transition from compensated steatosis to progressive fibrogenesis remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of early diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic interventions.  Methods  We integrated machine learning-based bulk transcriptome screening, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic validation, and transcriptional regulatory network analysis to systematically dissect the functional roles and interplay of ACVR1C and GAS6 during MASLD progression.  Results  We identified the ACVR1C-GAS6 antagonistic axis as a central regulatory hub governing hepatocyte metabolic homeostasis and macrophage functional polarization. ACVR1C exerts a previously unrecognized homeostatic gatekeeper role in sustaining hepatocyte detoxification pathways, whereas GAS6 is progressively upregulated across fibrosis stages with a distinct expression threshold marking fibrogenesis onset. Mechanistically, GAS6 drives polarization of heme-related macrophages via the MERTK-STAT3 cascade, which synergizes with direct hepatic stellate cell activation to promote liver fibrosis through a dual pathway. Spatial transcriptomic analysis in a mouse MASLD model further confirmed enhanced in situ co-localization of Gas6 and Mertk in diseased liver tissue.  Conclusions  The ACVR1C-GAS6 axis provides a novel molecular framework for understanding MASLD progression, and represents promising candidate biomarkers for disease risk stratification and therapeutic targets for clinical translation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Multiple myeloma (MM) is clinically heterogeneous, and the International Staging System (ISS) captures this heterogeneity only in part. We aimed to build a transcriptomic risk model anchored in single-cell and stage-associated gene expression, and to explore its immune context and therapeutic implications. Methods  Bone marrow single-cell RNA sequencing data from 18 MM and 18 control samples were integrated with ISS stage-stratified RNA sequencing data from the MMRF CoMMpass cohort (n = 764). Candidate genes were filtered by univariate Cox regression, and 101 combinations of 10 machine learning algorithms were benchmarked. The model was validated in three independent cohorts (GSE136337, GSE2658 and GSE4581) and examined with T cell subclustering, immune deconvolution, drug sensitivity prediction, genetic dependency data and molecular docking. Results  Integration yielded eight candidate genes, five of which (  DLGAP5  ,  CENPF  ,  PFDN2  ,  HNRNPF  and  MAP2K1  ) were associated with overall survival. A random survival forest plus supervised principal components model achieved a C-index of 0.69 in training and 0.62 to 0.63 in validation, outperformed 16 published MM signatures and remained independently prognostic after adjustment for age, sex and ISS stage (HR 2.02, 95% CI 1.70 to 2.41). High-risk patients had lower immune and stromal scores, higher TIDE scores and fewer predicted immunotherapy responders. Docking supported binding of risk-associated compounds to  MAP2K1  . Conclusion  This five-gene signature refines risk stratification beyond ISS, marks an immune-depleted high-risk phenotype and nominates  MAP2K1  as a candidate therapeutic target in MM.

papers.abstract_full: Invasive breast cancer remains the most frequently diagnosed malignancy and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Despite therapeutic advances, early detection, tumor heterogeneity, and treatment resistance remain significant challenges. This review examines advances in diagnosis and treatment, emphasizing molecular characterization and precision medicine. A narrative literature review was conducted using PubMed to identify publications from 2016 to 2026 on breast cancer molecular classification, diagnosis, and treatment. 99 out of 192 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the study. Molecular classification into luminal A, luminal B, HER2-positive, and triple-negative breast cancer has enabled personalized treatment. Next-generation sequencing, multigene assays, liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence-assisted imaging, and minimal residual disease monitoring improve risk stratification, diagnosis, and surveillance. Management integrates surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and systemic therapies. Endocrine treatments remain central to hormone receptor-positive disease, while HER2-targeted agents improve outcomes in HER2-positive cancers. PARP inhibitors and antibody–drug conjugates have expanded treatment options for selected patients with triple-negative disease. Molecular diagnostics and precision oncology are transforming breast cancer care. However, as resistance, recurrence, and tumor heterogeneity continue to limit long-term outcomes, further research into innovative diagnostics and individualized therapies is essential to improve treatment efficacy, survival, and life quality.

papers.abstract_full: Rapid microbial identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction are fundamental to precision diagnostics, effective infection control, and antimicrobial stewardship. Artificial intelligence-assisted spectral microbiology is increasingly being investigated to convert complex spectral and imaging data into rapid microbiological identification and antimicrobial resistance prediction outputs. This review critically examines the integration of AI with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, Raman spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and automated colony imaging for microbial identification, strain discrimination, and AMR prediction. This work focuses on spectral preprocessing, feature engineering, machine-learning architectures, interpretability, validation, and clinical translation. Emerging evidence shows substantial potential to accelerate diagnostics while improving analytical precision and scalability. papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Reliable determination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is fundamental to healthcare research and practice. High-quality research evidence is essential for guiding accurate AMR detection which, in turn, informs antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) decision-making. This scoping review is directed at a critical evaluation of the recent strategies in AMR detection across the globe. METHODS: Pertinent primary studies on AMR-associated strategies were identified by a comprehensive literature search on scholarly databases (PubMed, Google Scholar, and EMBASE) in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. The final set of pertinent studies published during the last 5 years (2021-2026) included 58 studies. Subsequent analysis critically evaluated the evidence of integration of advanced technologies into AMR detection and prediction programs. RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS; n = 37 articles) was the primary method for AMR screening across the included studies. Metagenomic sequencing (MGS) data was used for AMR characterization in 6 studies, while PCR/multiplex PCR was used in 10 articles. An interesting trend was the use of machine learning (ML) models for predicting AMR. Almost all studies which developed, validated and/or employed ML models (n = 21 studies) reported excellent time- and cost-efficiency, high accuracy and precision, and good concordance with conventional methods for AMR screening. Building on this synthesis, we propose the Integrated Diagnostic-Stewardship-Workforce (IDSW) model, a hypothesis-generating, five layered conceptual framework linking diagnostic innovations, workforce-mediated decision making, AMS intervention, contextual modifiers, and outcome feedback loop. CONCLUSION: The reviewed evidence supports the adaptation of AMR detection practices for clinical decision support systems, with potential downstream implications for technology-enhanced stewardship programs. Further, the proposed IDSW model offers a framework for guiding future research, policy making, and implementation efforts that integrate diagnostics and workforce roles, with AMS as a key downstream application.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches. METHODS: CRSwNP transcriptomic datasets (GSE136825, GSE179265) and single-cell data (GSE276503) were obtained from GEO database. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, differential expression analysis using limma, and Weighted Gene co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) were performed to identify methionine metabolism-related candidate genes. Three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with SHAP interpretation screened core genes. Functions and mechanisms were explored through single-gene GSEA, ceRNA network construction, transcription factor prediction, immune infiltration analysis, and pseudotime trajectory analysis. Potential therapeutic drugs were identified via molecular docking. RESULTS: Among 14 candidate genes, CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1 were identified as core genes with excellent diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.85). SHAP analysis revealed CSTB and IGFBP3 as disease risk-promoting factors, while TCN1 showed protective effects. Single-cell analysis demonstrated all three genes were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells with significant differential expression patterns. They were enriched in primary immunodeficiency pathways and significantly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly M2 macrophages and activated dendritic cells. Molecular docking identified five potential therapeutic drugs including ambroxol, carbamazepine, and curcumin with favorable binding energies. CONCLUSION: Methionine metabolism participates in CRSwNP pathogenesis by regulating CSTB, IGFBP3, and TCN1, affecting epithelial cell function and immune microenvironment. These genes represent promising biomarkers for diagnosis and potential therapeutic targets, providing theoretical basis for developing metabolic-immune intervention strategies in CRSwNP management.

papers.abstract_full: Sequence-to-function models are increasingly used as oracles to score designed regulatory elements, on the untested assumption that an effect measured at one locus holds at another. Taking chromatin and host loci from multiple sclerosis risk regions, we kept four questions apart: sequence realism, transfer of discrimination, edit stability, calibration. A sixth-order Markov chain reproduced the cell-type-specific motif enrichment a trained transformer missed, despite its lower held-out likelihood. Scores differ in level between loci far more than between inserts at one locus, yet inserts selected by an Enformer-derived index kept 85% of their advantage at four unseen loci. Once GC was matched, however, the index separated peak-derived from inaccessible sequence at none of 12 hosts, and from random sequence in opposite directions at different hosts. Placing identical inserts and an identical CpG edit at 24 host loci, the effect varied far beyond sampling noise on host identity alone ([Formula: see text]), unpredicted by 18 host properties. It survives scoring only the bins the insert occupies ([Formula: see text], and across 200 loci), so is no artefact of aggregation; the apparent host dominance, however, falls from 25-fold to 3-fold under that localised score, and the one locus positive under the whole-window score reverses under it. Borzoi reproduced the heterogeneity but not its amplitude, and the objective did not predict lentiMPRA activity. For these two oracles and this edit, the size of a predicted effect depends on where it is measured, and its direction at any one locus is not robust.

papers.abstract: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique B-cell malignancy characterized by a small number of malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells embedded within an extensive and highly organized inflammatory microenvironment. Recent studies have highlighted that the biological behavior of cHL is largely determined by dynamic interactions between HRS cells and surrounding immune populations, including CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, eosinophils, mast cells, natural killer cells, an…
papers.abstract_full: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique B-cell malignancy characterized by a small number of malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells embedded within an extensive and highly organized inflammatory microenvironment. Recent studies have highlighted that the biological behavior of cHL is largely determined by dynamic interactions between HRS cells and surrounding immune populations, including CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, eosinophils, mast cells, natural killer cells, and stromal elements. HRS cells actively reshape the tumor microenvironment through the secretion of chemokines and cytokines, including CCL17, CCL22, IL-6, IL-10, and TGF-β, promoting immune cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, and immune tolerance. Concurrently, genetic alterations affecting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, antigen-presentation pathways, and key signaling cascades such as NF-κB and JAK/STAT facilitate immune escape and tumor persistence. We distinguish diagnostic, prognostic, predictive, and response-monitoring applications and grade biomarkers as established (immunophenotyping, EBER, clinical scores, interim PET), clinically promising (serum TARC, circulating tumor DNA), or investigational (PD-L1-based prediction, spatial and single-cell profiling, artificial intelligence). A deeper understanding of the interplay between immunity and inflammation in cHL may refine disease classification and guide the development of novel immunomodulatory strategies aimed at improving long-term outcomes and overcoming resistance to current therapies.

papers.abstract_full: Codon optimization (CO) is a key design variable in biotherapeutics that is used to enhance expression of recombinant proteins, gene therapies, and vaccines. Although synonymous codon substitutions were historically considered neutral, codon choice can influence messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, translation kinetics, cotranslational folding, and immunogenicity. Current optimization strategies integrate computational parameters including codon adaptation indices, tRNA availability, mRNA structure, cytosine-phosphate-guanine dinucleotide content, codon pair bias, and machine learning approaches to balance expression and product quality. Additionally, dynamic tRNA modifications within the epitranscriptome modulate codon-biased translation in a context-dependent manner. While CO has not been implicated in adverse clinical outcomes, its context-dependent effects on protein conformation, post-translational modifications, and immune responses necessitate rigorous characterization. This opinion article presents our viewpoint on mechanisms, applications, and regulatory considerations for CO in biologics.

papers.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has changed cancer treatment, with neoantigen-based vaccines emerging as a promising strategy to induce tumor-specific immune responses while minimizing adverse effects on healthy tissues. papers.abstract_full: Cancer immunotherapy has changed cancer treatment, with neoantigen-based vaccines emerging as a promising strategy to induce tumor-specific immune responses while minimizing adverse effects on healthy tissues. Advances in next-generation sequencing, immunopeptidomics, artificial intelligence, and computational prediction have accelerated the identification of patient-specific neoantigens and enabled the development of personalized cancer vaccines. Despite encouraging safety profiles and robust induction of neoantigen-specific T-cell responses, clinical efficacy has remained inconsistent. Tumor evolution driven by genomic instability continuously reshapes the neoantigen landscape through intratumoral heterogeneity, immune-mediated selection, and antigen gain or loss, facilitating immune escape and limiting durable therapeutic responses. In addition, T-cell dysfunction and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment further compromise vaccine efficacy. In this review, we discuss the origin and diversity of tumor antigens, recent advances in neoantigen identification and vaccine development, and the biological mechanisms that constrain the clinical success of personalized cancer vaccines. We summarize evidence from clinical trials that highlights both the promise and the current limitations of neoantigen-based immunotherapy, and discuss the importance of incorporating tumor evolution into vaccine design. Finally, we present Variable Epitope Libraries (VELs), a vaccine strategy that uses immunogens based on combinatorial libraries of highly mutated epitope variants designed to broaden immune recognition, reduce immune escape, and improve the durability and effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: To identify the competencies that pharmacists need to evaluate, implement, and oversee technology-enabled care and propose a longitudinal framework for developing these competencies within PharmD education. FINDINGS: Drawing on the 2025 National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) Pharmacy Workshop, this paper links emerging technologies to new pharmacist roles across clinical, regulatory, managed care, and industry settings. The new technologies demand that pharmacists validate artificial intelligence (AI) recommendations, implement digital therapeutics, apply pharmacogenomic (PGx) data, and interpret real-world evidence (RWE), all of which extend beyond traditional pharmacotherapy training. We propose four longitudinally scaffolded domains: Technical Understanding, Critical Evaluation, Ethical and Professional Stewardship, and Discipline-Specific Application. SUMMARY: Technology is not diminishing the pharmacist's role. Rather, it highlights the importance of pharmacists' clinical expertise. Preparing graduates requires deliberate curricular design, faculty investment, and recognition that clinical judgment remains the irreplaceable complement to any algorithm.

papers.abstract_full: Spatial transcriptomics enables gene expression profiling with preserved spatial context, yet accurate spatial domain delineation remains challenging. We present RIF, a robust and interpretable deep learning framework for fine-grained spatial domain identification. RIF leverages graph neural networks semi-supervised with pseudo-labels to preserve tissue structural integrity. It incorporates a dual-preprocessing ensemble strategy to improve model robustness and generalization. It further enables spatially variable gene detection through network interpretability. Across multiple sequencing platforms, RIF outperformed state-of-the-art comparison algorithms in spatial domain identification. In mouse brain tissue, RIF identified corresponding hippocampal subfields in the spatially separated dorsal and ventral regions and resolved the laminar organization of the olfactory bulb. In breast cancer, RIF-defined domains suggest suppressed T cell activity associated with hypoxic and oxidative microenvironments. In an invasive ductal carcinoma dataset of more than 720,000 cells, RIF-defined domains suggest an epithelial-mesenchymal transition gradient, including reduced hormone dependence and extracellular matrix remodeling.

papers.abstract_full: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) represents the majority of lung cancer cases and remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Early detection, accurate staging, and individualized therapy are crucial for improving patient survival. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have transformed NSCLC care through the automated analysis of imaging, pathology, and molecular datasets. Deep learning (DL) and machine learning (ML) models, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), have demonstrated high accuracy in tumor detection, histologic classification, biomarker prediction (PD-L1, EGFR, KRAS) and prognosis assessment. Integration of the AI with whole slide imaging (WSI), computed tomography (CT), PET/CT and liquid biopsies enables non-invasive tumor characterization, early recurrence detection and prediction of treatment response. Multimodal AI approaches that combine imaging, genomic, and clinical data offer superior patient stratification and personalized treatment planning compared with traditional methods. Beyond diagnosis, AI facilitates therapeutic development through radiomics based nodule classification, multi-omics data interpretation, and drug discovery. Radiomics, in particular, extracts quantitative imaging biomarkers that capture tumor heterogeneity beyond human perception. The AI further supports clinical decision-making in surgery, radiotherapy, and systemic therapy, enhancing workflow efficiency. Despite challenges in data quality, interpretability, and clinical adoption, AI holds significant promise for advancing precision oncology and improving outcomes in NSCLC management.

papers.abstract: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. papers.abstract_full: An opening salvo of lawsuits in US courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: Product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack. This Perspective points out that these converging paths share a unifying principle, built on the very engineering architecture of machine learning (ML) itself. Every ML system, across all variants, is constituted by a human-specified objective function before learning begins. Training data, deployment context, user interaction, and postdeployment oversight add further layers of deliberate human intention traceable to identifiable actors. AI output is therefore not the expression of a single speaker but a composite of layered human intents. It takes a village to raise an AI, and everyone in that village bears a duty of care. This transforms AI accountability from a philosophical puzzle into a tractable legal inquiry: Trace the chain of intentional design decisions across the ML pipeline, grade each actor's responsibility by their intent's specificity and foreseeability, and apportion liability accordingly, following the standard three doctrine-neutral questions (attribution, causation, apportionment). Sufficient for most cases, four gaps remain: who owes what share when many hands build one system, proving fault inside an opaque model, harms that surface only after deployment, and remedies that match the technology's pace. Targeted reforms drawing on environmental, vaccine, and financial regulatory precedents can close these gaps without requiring new legal categories, AI speech rights, AI legal personhood, or defining AI consciousness.

papers.abstract_full: Genomic DNA is wrapped around core histones to form nucleosomes, which are organized in cells from euchromatin to heterochromatin with distinct genome functions. Although transcription is known to shape chromatin behavior in live cells, it remains unclear how different transcription systems act across chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments. We develop machine learning-assisted Repli-Histo labeling to classify euchromatin and heterochromatin classes (classes IA, IB, II, and III) and combine it with single-nucleosome imaging in living human cells. Nucleosome motion is progressively constrained from euchromatin to heterochromatin. RNA polymerase II inhibition by THZ1, DRB, or α-amanitin increases nucleosome motion in euchromatic classes IA and IB and in heterochromatin around nucleoli, but not at the nuclear periphery. In contrast, RNA polymerase I inhibition by CX-5461 selectively increases nucleosome motion in Class III heterochromatin around nucleoli. Our study reveals that Pol II and Pol I transcription shape chromatin behavior in distinct chromatin classes and nuclear subcompartments.

papers.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
papers.abstract: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regula…
papers.abstract_full: The regulation of chromatin accessibility is critical for cell function and identity. Advances in single-molecule long-read footprinting have enabled near-nucleotide-resolution readout of chromatin fiber organization, capturing both coordination of transcription factor (TF) binding and variation in nucleosome positioning previously obscured by bulk methods. Here we combine this technique with deep learning to study how protein-DNA interactions are coordinated within different types of cis-regulatory elements in mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we quantify the frequency with which pairs of positions are simultaneously accessible on individual molecules. Then, we train ChAI-Net, a neural network that predicts these locus-specific chromatin co-accessibility maps from the underlying DNA sequence. Through model interpretation and in silico experiments, we show that ChAI-Net learns unique combinations of sequence motifs underlying co-accessibility within enhancers, promoters, and CTCF-bound sites. Many of these motifs are missed when modeling average accessibility, suggesting a specific role in coordinated binding. ChAI-Net's regulatory grammar also highlights the importance of TF motif orientation, spacing, positioning, and co-occurrence in driving co-accessibility. Thus, our framework for extracting regulatory rules from footprinting data expands understanding of TF cooperativity, while laying the groundwork to elucidate how these rules vary across cellular contexts as single-molecule genomics is deployed at scale.

papers.abstract: Rapid detection of drug resistance in fungi is becoming increasingly urgent. While multiple loci and mutations were linked to antifungal resistance in  Candida albicans , the utility of whole genome sequencing in predicting resistance has not been tested thoroughly. We address this by integrating more than 1000  C. albicans genomes, with associated resistance phenotypes to six antifungals, a curated repository of resistance-causing mutations and variant effect predictors. papers.abstract_full: Rapid detection of drug resistance in fungi is becoming increasingly urgent. While multiple loci and mutations were linked to antifungal resistance in  Candida albicans , the utility of whole genome sequencing in predicting resistance has not been tested thoroughly. We address this by integrating more than 1000  C. albicans genomes, with associated resistance phenotypes to six antifungals, a curated repository of resistance-causing mutations and variant effect predictors. We used Genome Wide Association Studies and Machine Learning approaches to associate genetic variants to resistance phenotypes. We found that well curated databases like FungAMR are able to accurately identify markers predictive antifungal resistance. Curated mutations were detected in 56–74% of isolates with reduced azole susceptibility and 57–90% of those with reduced echinocandin susceptibility, revealing incomplete coverage of resistance across both drug classes. Complementary variant- and gene-level association analyses recovered established resistance determinants and uncovered additional candidate loci, whereas copy-number changes provided limited independent explanatory power. Genomic prediction declined when genetic backgrounds were absent from training, and when leading predictive features differed among backgrounds. We also found that models trained on a curated list of mutations and variant effect predictors performed well when classifying drug-susceptible strains, but the drug-resistance trait was predicted with a lower accuracy. These findings support the potential of genome-based resistance prediction while highlighting the need for broader population sampling, functional validation of candidate variants and expanded resistance catalogues to improve prediction across genetic backgrounds.

papers.abstract_full: Many phage proteins remain functionally uncharacterized despite advances in structural-similarity-based annotation. We introduce PhageFlare, a deep learning framework for predicting phage protein functions lacking significant structural matches to annotated references. Across three structure-disjoint benchmarks, where no significant Foldseek match was detected between training and test proteins (E-value thresholds of 10  -3 , 10  -4 , and 10  -2 ), PhageFlare achieved macro-averaged F  1 scores of 0.871, 0.889, and 0.738 outperforming the strongest baseline (0.789, 0.814, and 0.732). Systematic evaluations demonstrated that protein language model selection critically influences performance, with ESM-C achieving stronger overall performance than ESM-2 and ProtBert. Embedding-guided case studies revealed local structural correspondences among proteins with limited global similarity. Applied to the efam and Metagenomic Gut Virus datasets, PhageFlare annotated 38.0% and 51.8% of proteins unresolved by Foldseek, respectively. Furthermore, PhageFlare identified lysogenic potential in 1,866 prophage-designated genomes misclassified as lytic by BACPHLIP. These results show that PhageFlare complements structural-similarity-based annotation and expands functional discovery across viral dark matter.

papers.abstract: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested, because doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies. Given a source manuscript and a target scRNA-seq dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and m…
papers.abstract_full: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested, because doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) studies. Given a source manuscript and a target scRNA-seq dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and mechanistic findings, generates and executes analyses for the testable findings, and reports which findings transfer and suggests follow-up. Applied to 121 studies across six cancer types, SMART identified findings that transfer across cancers, including a lung cancer prognostic signature that we confirmed to be associated with survival in liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and pleural mesothelioma. SMART also generated new mechanistic hypotheses, demonstrating how agentic discovery transfer can extend published findings beyond their original setting.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Pollen development is highly sensitive to heatwave conditions in many plant species. Oftentimes, heatwave-induced pollen abortion leads to reduced yield, which is detrimental to crop cultivation and ultimately food security. Though genetic studies have identified loci that affect the level of pollen heatwave tolerance in a few species, no causal genes have been identified, yet. Exploring natural variation for pollen heatwave tolerance is key to finding novel genetic elements involved in protection against damage. In this study, we developed a novel pollen phenotyping protocol, combining MTT-staining with automated image analysis for machine-learning-based pollen classification in Arabidopsis. This assay was employed to screen an Arabidopsis diversity panel consisting of 208 accessions originating from the Iberian Peninsula and Morocco exposed to a controlled long-term, heatwave-like temperature regime. Using GWAS, we identified a QTL encompassing a cluster of immune-associated nucleotide-binding protein (IAN) genes (  IAN2  to  IAN5  ). The  ian2 ian3 ian4 ian5  quadruple mutant was more tolerant to heatwave-like conditions, indicating that these genes repress pollen viability under these conditions. These findings validate our novel phenotyping assay and, together with previous reports that IAN genes repress pollen tolerance to more severe heat, identify the IAN genes as candidate breeding targets for adaptation of crops to a warmer climate.

papers.title: Creator 1.0: Phylogeny-Guided Stagewise Pretraining for Plant Genome Foundation Models across 1,000 Species
papers.abstract: Genomic language models have advanced DNA sequence analysis, but their applicability to plant-specific tasks and representation changes during pretraining remain poorly characterized. Here, we present Creator 1.0, a 2-billion-parameter parameter plant genome foundation model pretrained on 1,000 plant genomes using phylogeny-guided stagewise pretraining (PGSP). Training comprised 83 consecutive stages and produced 52 cumulative checkpoints associated with distinct plant orders. On GENEB, the stag…
papers.abstract_full: Genomic language models have advanced DNA sequence analysis, but their applicability to plant-specific tasks and representation changes during pretraining remain poorly characterized. Here, we present Creator 1.0, a 2-billion-parameter parameter plant genome foundation model pretrained on 1,000 plant genomes using phylogeny-guided stagewise pretraining (PGSP). Training comprised 83 consecutive stages and produced 52 cumulative checkpoints associated with distinct plant orders. On GENEB, the stage 83 checkpoint ranked first among 46 models across 10 plant-related tasks, with a mean Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.565, and fourth across all 100 tasks. Evaluation of 52 checkpoints on six plant lncRNA tasks identified different optimal stages under full-data, 10-shot and 1-shot settings, corresponding to stages 71, 72 and 29, respectively. Checkpoint performance varied across tasks, without consistent advantages for corresponding plant orders. These findings demonstrate the competitive performance of Creator 1.0 and highlight the potential of PGSP to provide task-adaptable checkpoints for plant genomic applications.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Objective  To evaluate large language model (LLM) generation of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) phenotyping SQL and the effect of database implementation context. Materials and Methods  Eight publicly accessible LLM-based systems generated SQL under progressively richer prompts using synthetic and University of North Carolina (UNC) Health electronic health record (EHR) data, both based on the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) model. Outputs were compared with the Electronic Medical Records and Genomics (eMERGE) T2DM reference phenotype using SQL executability, F1, positive predictive value (PPV), and recall. Results  Fewer than 55% of limited-context synthetic outputs and no limited-context UNC EHR outputs executed without modification. Detailed codebooks (L3) increased executability to 81.3% in synthetic OMOP and 100% in UNC EHR; adding sample rows (L4) increased synthetic executability to 100%. Limited-context recall was as low as 0.01, whereas high-context outputs achieved recall ≥0.99 at synthetic L4 and >0.90 at UNC L3, although UNC PPV remained substantially lower than recall. At the highest available context levels, Beta F1 ranged from 0.72–0.99 in synthetic OMOP and 0.57–0.68 in UNC EHR; all UNC models exceeded the diagnosis-code baseline (F1=0.54). The top synthetic performer fell from F1=0.99 to 0.64 on UNC EHR. Discussion  Richer database context was associated with more consistent SQL executability and recall, while model rankings varied across datasets. Conclusion  LLMs can generate clinically meaningful T2DM phenotyping SQL when provided with sufficient database context, but limited PPV in real-world data underscores the need for local validation.

papers.title: Characterization of heterogeneous bioinformatics training needs in the AI era
papers.abstract: Bioinformatics training providers serve heterogeneous audiences, a challenge sharpened by fast-evolving technologies such as generative artificial intelligence (AI). Analyzing training-needs surveys in aggregate can mask this heterogeneity. We present a network-based clustering protocol that groups respondents by the similarity of their Likert-type topic ratings: respondents form a Spearman correlation network, and community detection groups them into learner profiles with shared training needs,…
papers.abstract_full: Bioinformatics training providers serve heterogeneous audiences, a challenge sharpened by fast-evolving technologies such as generative artificial intelligence (AI). Analyzing training-needs surveys in aggregate can mask this heterogeneity. We present a network-based clustering protocol that groups respondents by the similarity of their Likert-type topic ratings: respondents form a Spearman correlation network, and community detection groups them into learner profiles with shared training needs, independent of demographics. We demonstrate the protocol on the 2026 SIB Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics (SIB) training needs survey (n=260), covering topics, barriers, and formats. We identified four interpretable learner profiles: AI and data, infectious disease genomics, functional genomics, and biochemistry, imaging & AI. Each had distinct topic priorities, barriers, and format preferences that an aggregate analysis hides. For example, LLM-based knowledge extraction ranked 2nd overall but only 16th in the infectious disease genomics profile, whereas phylogenetics ranked 17th overall but first there. Across profiles, AI/LLM skills and reproducible data practices were in high demand, whereas AI-assisted learning was, unexpectedly, the least preferred format. Because the protocol requires only a shared Likert scale, it is reusable for other training-needs assessments; the implementation is openly available. Profile-based curricula can target each group’s topics, formats, and barriers. Biographical note  the authors are members of the SIB Training group that provides training to ensure that life scientists make the best of the latest advances in computational biology. Key points  We present a validated, openly available network-clustering method for identifying learner profiles from training-needs survey data. Applied to the 2026 SIB training needs survey, the method identified four thematically distinct, reproducible learner profiles, capturing training-need heterogeneity that demographics miss. AI/LLM skills are the top training gap across all profiles, alongside strong demand for FAIR/reproducible data practices — yet respondents prefer human-led formats over AI-assisted learning. Curricula should be tailored to learner profiles rather than demographics or aggregate topic rankings, which each hide profile-specific needs.

papers.abstract: Engineering agronomically relevant traits in crops often requires changing a gene’s activity in a specific tissue, developmental stage or environmental condition while preserving its roles in other contexts. papers.abstract_full: Engineering agronomically relevant traits in crops often requires changing a gene’s activity in a specific tissue, developmental stage or environmental condition while preserving its roles in other contexts. Designing such selective changes requires predicting how cis-regulatory sequences are interpreted in different biological states, as the same edit can have different effects across contexts. Genomic models have made substantial progress in predicting gene expression from DNA sequence, yet sequence-only predictors do not receive an explicit description of biological states. We introduce CROP-1 (  C ontext-aware  R egulatory  O utput  P rediction model), which combines DNA sequence with transcription factor binding motifs and measured expression to predict gene activity as a function of both sequence and regulatory state. On a held-out test set spanning six plant species, CROP-1 achieves a median per-gene Pearson correlation across contexts of 0.831, compared with 0.486 for its parameter-matched sequence-only counterpart, and 57–246% higher median correlations than three genomic foundation models fully fine-tuned on the same task. Prediction accuracy also improves with scale: increasing model capacity reduces validation error by 48%, while expanding training data to include more diverse biological contexts reduces it by 58%. We then use gradient-based sequence optimisation to translate a desired gene expression pattern into candidate edits of its cis-regulatory sequence, targeting up- or down-regulation in one context while preserving expression in others. In soybean and tomato, edit designs with 1–20 nucleotide substitutions produce strong predicted target responses and much smaller average changes across non-target contexts. By connecting scalable learning of sequence–state relationships to selective edit design, CROP-1 provides a computational foundation for controlling where, when and under which conditions endogenous crop genes are active.

papers.abstract_full: Single-cell RNA velocity has transformed our capacity to predict future cell states from sequencing snapshots, but existing methods rely on constant or binary kinetic assumptions that fail to capture the heterogeneous splicing dynamics of cellular differentiation. Here we present JuloVelo, a deep learning framework that demonstrates that identifying gene kinetics patterns to initialize neural network training dramatically improves RNA velocity model performance. By pre-determining whether each gene follows a Circle, Complete induction, or Complete repression pattern across cellular differentiation, JuloVelo initializes training with pattern-matched, pre-trained network weights, effectively guiding the cell-specific kinetics optimization away from biologically implausible parameter regimes. Additionally, JuloVelo demonstrates that multiome datasets can also be processed and modeled by utilizing promoter chromatin accessibility to guide kinetics pre-determination, and integrates an  in silico perturbation framework to simulate transcription factor modulation on cell fate. Validated across eight datasets spanning erythrogenesis, neurogenesis, and endocrinogenesis, JuloVelo consistently outperformed constant-rate and cell-specific models, resolving the entire five-lineage differentiation program in hippocampal neurogenesis. Multiome processing improved both intrinsic and extrinsic velocity stability, and JuloVelo reduced computational execution time by approximately 70% compared to cellDancer. JuloVelo is available as an open-source package at  https://github.com/jhlabtw/JuloVelo.jl .

papers.abstract_full: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) have transformed our ability to learn the evolutionary language encoded in genomes, yet their potential for programmable regulatory DNA engineering remains underexplored. Regulatory function depends on combinatorial interactions among distributed sequence elements, motivating generation with bidirectional context. Here, we introduce DAPE-PD (  D iffusion  A daptation of  P retrained  E vo for  P romoter  D esign), which adapts the autoregressive Evo model into a bidirectional masked diffusion model without foundation-scale retraining. DAPE-PD combines pretrained genomic representations with iterative unmasking to generate regulatory DNA sequences. Following genus-specific fine-tuning on genome-derived intergenic sequences, DAPE-PD generated sequences that retained genus-associated compositional features despite low similarity to the fine-tuning datasets. Experimental validation identified functional de novo promoters, while in silico prioritization recovered active designs from small experimental candidate sets across three non-model gut commensals. This framework connects genomic pretraining with diffusion-based generation, extending GFMs from sequence understanding toward functional  cis -regulatory DNA engineering in living cells.

papers.abstract_full: There exist a wide range of Neural Networks (NNs) that have modelled genomic sequences well. The architectures of these NNs consist of three steps:  k -mer embedding, sequence embedding, and output mapping. The NNs are primarily differentiated from one another by their sequence embedding components. Although different NNs have been compared before, these comparisons are often either limited or involve drastically different NNs. Another issue is that some NNs are configured for a specific sequence length, and different length sequences require manual modification of the architectures. This study examines the architectures of established NNs for genomics sequences. Based on these architectures, a novel NN called Mimic is developed that provides a unified architecture for the principled comparison of NN components.  Mimic was used to model two different types of genomic datasets: protein-DNA interactions and enhancer activity. Along with other architecture components, different sequence embedding strategies were tried such as recurrent layers and convolutional layers. It was found that there exist specific NN components that yield significantly better performing models. Furthermore, Mimic significantly outperformed prevailing standard NNs, Bichrom and DeepSTARR, in modelling protein-DNA interactions and enhancer activity, respectively. This study provides a framework for more extensive studies toward a general prescription of NN architecture for modelling genomics data.
bullets: This study examines the architectures of established NNs for genomics sequences.
It was found that there exist specific NN components that yield significantly better performing models.

papers.abstract: Drug repurposing offers an efficient strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing medicines. However, conventional predictive models often lack mechanistic interpretability, limiting their translational reliability. Mechanism-guided AI integrates computational predictions w…
papers.abstract_full: Drug repurposing offers an efficient strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing medicines. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and systems pharmacology have enabled the analysis of complex biological and clinical datasets to identify potential drug–disease associations. However, conventional predictive models often lack mechanistic interpretability, limiting their translational reliability. Mechanism-guided AI integrates computational predictions with molecular interactions, signaling pathways, multi-omics data, causal inference, and biological networks to improve the identification and prioritization of repurposable drugs. This review examines key computational approaches, including knowledge graphs, explainable AI, molecular docking, network-based drug discovery, and causal modeling, highlighting their applications across major disease categories. It also discusses the integration of computational findings with experimental pharmacology, pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic assessment, biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and clinical trial development. Furthermore, the review evaluates challenges associated with data heterogeneity, model bias, causal validation, drug safety, reproducibility, and regulatory acceptance. Integrating real-world evidence, pharmacovigilance data, and patient-specific molecular profiles may further strengthen therapeutic predictions and support precision medicine. Future progress requires transparent reporting, standardized benchmarking, rigorous experimental validation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Mechanism-guided AI may bridge computational drug discovery and clinical pharmacology by generating biologically plausible, experimentally testable, and clinically relevant therapeutic hypotheses, ultimately supporting more efficient and evidence-based drug repurposing.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Non-typhoidal salmonellosis is a major foodborne infection mostly due to the consumption of contaminated animal-derived food. However, the proportions among  Salmonella  serovars causing human disease differ from those isolated from food-producing animals, suggesting differences in virulence. This study investigated whether specific genetic determinants are associated with the hypothesized virulence difference among  Salmonella  serovars. We analysed 1,720 genomes of six serovars, categorized as virulent or attenuated based on their epidemiological data, using machine learning to identify differences in gene repertoires. Discriminatory genes underwent semantic analysis using gene annotation embeddings and genomic localization to identify adjacent genes. Phylogenetic analysis assessed the distribution of the minimal discriminatory gene-set across common  Salmonella  serovars. Machine-learning clearly distinguished virulent from attenuated serovars. Discriminatory genes comprise several virulence genes enriched in virulent serovars. The minimal discriminatory gene-set included  Salmonella  Pathogenicity Island (SPI) 13 and 14 genes, essential to cause gut inflammation and to respond to the immune metabolite itaconate. SPI-13 and SPI-14 genes are absent in the evolutionary branch including attenuated serovars and in one phylogenetically unrelated serovar showing epidemiological patterns consistent with attenuation. Our results support the hypothesis of differential virulence among non-typhoidal  Salmonella  serovars and identify genetic differences potentially associated with this variation.

papers.abstract_full: This manuscript unifies global registries with molecular kinetics to resolve the inverse comorbidity between cancer and Alzheimer's disease. We propose this inversion represents a binary, tissue-specific allocation of cell survival strategies dictated by the solubility of the Filamin A (FLNA) cytoskeletal scaffolding network under systemic cobalamin insufficiency. Chronic exposure to trace environmental nitrous oxide (N₂O) pollution passivates cobalamin, arresting the cell-autonomous one-carbon cycle. In post-mitotic neural architectures, this bioenergetic arrest forces membrane potential collapse and dynorphin-driven non-opioid excitotoxic decay, activating caspase-3 to execute the primary cleavage of the FLNA matrix into structural intermediates; subsequent calcium influx activates calpains to remodel these intermediates, driving the definitive altered conformation bound by simufilam, before executing terminal hinge-domain fragmentation that liberates compact 90-kDa C-terminal fragments (FLNA-90) for nuclear translocation to enact a genomic tumor-suppressor checkpoint. Conversely, peripheral tissues with high metabolic plasticity escape collapse via malignant transformation. Upstream accumulation of the oncometabolite methylmalonic acid (MMA) acts as an epigenetic reprogrammer, driving TGF-β and SOX4 cascades to force KRAS transcription into constitutive overdrive. This active KRAS pool fuels downstream kinase networks that keep the peripheral FLNA matrix intact, soluble, and hyper-phosphorylated at Serine 2152 (pS2152) to complex with cytoplasmic Cyclin D1/CDK4 networks. This structural configuration shields the scaffold from calpain-mediated cleavage, reconfiguring FLNA into an active motility engine driving invasive lamellipodia but stalls proteolytic processing and forces an absolute loss of the nuclear FLNA-90 tumor-suppressor brake, unleashing uninhibited c-Myc oncogenic transcription. Crucially, this malignant transformation functions as an active metabolic adaptation; the hyper-stabilization of the intact 280-kDa platform operates in tandem with the active downregulation of the MMAB protein via a direct, transcription-independent cytosolic protein interaction with SMAD4 to drive its proteasomal degradation entirely independent of canonical TGF-β signaling cascades. By shutting this internal gate, the cell prevents its own expanding somatic structure from natively consuming cobalamin cofactors, transforming the emerging biomass into a high-powered cytoplasmic motility engine and a strict systemic refinery sink. Using hyper-glycolytic GSH and NADPH reserves to forcefully reduce passivated corrin rings [Co(III)→Co(I)], the tumor coordinates active metastatic seeding to locate uncompromised nutrient sources and export bioavailable cobalamin via ABCC1 pumps, rescuing central neural networks from homeostatic collapse. Filamin A thus serves as the definitive structural, conformational, and proteomic switch governing this inverse disease matrix.

papers.abstract_full: Cervical cancer is a major global health challenge, especially in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, screening methods and established treatments. Cervical cancer is primarily caused by persistent infection with high-risk HPV, but persistent infection is necessary, but not sufficient, for the development of cancer. Advances in understanding HPV genetic diversity, viral persistence, and virus-host molecular interactions are creating new opportunities to improve precision in HPV prevention and treatment. HPV genotype distribution and differences in oncogenic potential inform vaccine development and screening strategies. The viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 disrupt host tumor-suppressor pathways, driving cellular immortalization and genomic instability. Molecular events such as viral insertion, epigenetic modifications, APOBEC-associated mutations, and immune escape contribute to disease progression. These discoveries have revealed molecular vulnerabilities that can be targeted therapeutically. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates are used clinically in specific contexts of cervical cancer presentation and treatment. At the same time, therapeutic vaccines, adoptive cellular immunotherapies, RNA interference, and genome editing are being investigated as complementary strategies to target HPV-associated cervical cancer. With advances in next-generation sequencing, molecular biomarkers, and artificial intelligence, these tools could further refine risk stratification and therapy selection. This review explores the current understanding of HPV genetic variation and virus-host interactions driving a shift from traditional prevention and treatment strategies to precision prevention and targeted therapeutics, and critically assesses remaining challenges.

papers.abstract_full: Accurate interpretation of germline variants remains a central challenge in clinical genomics. Existing  in silico pathogenicity predictors often provide incomplete coverage or restricted to missense variants from the coding region, leaving the variants from splice sites, -UTR, and intronic regions under-scored. We present AGVarPred, a gradient-boosted classifier designed to predict the pathogenicity of germline mutants, with a broad consequence-class coverage across SNVs and indels. Here, the population allele frequency from gnomAD, functional consequence annotations from Ensembl VEP, and cell-type-specific functional genomic scores from the AlphaGenome platform were integrated to develop the classifier. Using a gene-level split of 134,002 high-confidence ClinVar variants across 9,222 genes, AGVarPred achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.9753 (95% CI 0.9731-0.9775) and a AUC-PR of 0.9606 on 12,385 scored internal test variants. A paired DeLong analysis showed that the full model significantly outperformed an allele-frequency-plus-VEP model (ΔAUC = 0.1539, 95% CI 0.1489-0.1589; p < 1 × 10  -300 ), supporting a substantial incremental contribution from AlphaGenome-derived features. Performance remained strong when restricted to SNVs (AUC-ROC 0.9558) and was also high for indels (AUC-ROC 0.9532). On five external benchmarks, AUC-ROCs ranged from 0.528 on a functional-assay-derived benchmark to 0.977 on a clinically curated deafness database, reflecting its dependence on benchmark composition and label source. A separate analysis of the VIP Database, whose pathogenic labels are ClinVar-derived, showed consistent performance (AUC-ROC of 0.892) in held-out genes. AGVarPred scored 100% of evaluated variants in the external benchmarks, whereas AlphaMissense and REVEL covered only small fractions of non-missense variants. Model interpretation indicated that gnomAD allele frequency was the dominant individual predictor; the 111 AlphaGenome features provided complementary functional signal, with splicing and chromatin assays contributing to the largest share of the AlphaGenome SHAP mass. A web-based interface for AGVarPred is available at  https://pankaj357.github.io/AGVarPred/ to facilitate the submission of normalized GRCh38 germline variants and retrieval of pathogenicity predictions using the frozen AGVarPred model.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Adolescent psychotic-like experiences, particularly those that are distressing and persistent (dpPLEs), may elevate risk for a range of psychiatric disorders, yet the relative predictive contributions of brain structure, genetics, and environment to dpPLEs remain unknown. Using four timepoints from 7,399 children in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, we developed stacked ensemble machine-learning models integrating cortical morphometry and whole-brain microstructural properties, polygenic risk scores, family psychiatric history, and childhood environmental factors to predict adolescent dpPLEs. Environmental predictors alone, driven by area deprivation index, neighborhood drug-related crime, and cumulative early adversity, were the strongest predictive domain (ROC-AUC = 0.687 ± 0.003), outperforming genetic (0.619 ± 0.020) and all imaging models (0.588-0.650). Adding genetic risk to environmental features produced the best-performing model overall (ROC-AUC = 0.697 ± 0.007), whereas adding neuroimaging yielded no further incremental gain (ROC-AUC=0.683-0.696). Beyond environmental exposures, family history of psychosis, cross-disorder polygenic risk, and both globally distributed and regionally specific imaging components contributed to prediction. Childhood environmental factors thus capture a core predictive signal preceding dpPLEs, while genetic and neuroimaging features added comparatively modest discriminative prediction value, but may offer complementary biological insights.

papers.abstract_full: Short tandem repeats (STRs) are highly mutable, multiallelic variants with distinctive mutation dynamics and have been associated with phenotypic variation across diverse species. However, genome-wide STR variation remains poorly characterized in olive, and the large number of naturally occurring alleles creates a challenge for variant interpretation. Genomic language models offer a potential way to assess how STR length changes alter learned sequence representations, but their responses to natural multiallelic STR series have not been systematically evaluated. Here, we identified 117,119 polymorphic STRs across 212 Iranian and Mediterranean olive accessions. STRs recovered the major SNP-defined ancestry axes while resolving additional geographically structured subcomponents. We then quantified STR-induced embedding perturbation using three plant genomic language models: AgroNT, PlantCAD2, and GPN. Across all three models, embedding distance generally increased with repeat-length difference from the reference allele, and 7,417 loci were embedding-sensitive in all three models. These signals were robust to fixed-length input construction and exceeded those of matched nonrepetitive indels at most tested loci. Integration with oil-composition associations prioritized four exploratory loci supported by all three models. Overall, we provide a genome-wide olive STR resource and show that plant genomic language models capture reproducible responses to natural STR length variation. Combining cross-model embedding evidence with phenotype association provides a potential framework for prioritizing candidate STRs for further investigation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Purpose  : Detection of carbapenemase-production in  Pseudomonas aeruginosa  is challenging due to the co-occurrence of multiple resistance mechanisms. We developed a novel machine learning approach to predict carbapenemase production based on inhibition zone diameters (IZD) from routine disk diffusion testing.  Methods  : A CatBoost model (CBM) was trained on 246 whole-genome-sequenced clinical  P. aeruginosa  isolates, including 95 carbapenemase-producing  P. aeruginosa  (CPPA). Models based on different antibiotic combinations were evaluated and externally validated on two independent datasets. Performance was benchmarked against the phenotypic screening algorithm described by Gill  et al.  Results  : For Dataset 1, CBM achieved a sensitivity and specificity of 94% and 98%, compared with 94% and 38% for the Gill  et al.  algorithm. For Dataset 2, sensitivity/specificity were 95%/98% for CBM vs 100%/0% for the Gill algorithm. This represented a reduction in isolates requiring confirmatory testing of 76% in Dataset 1 and 52% in Dataset 2.  Conclusions  : CatBoost models trained on IZD represent a valuable tool for carbapenemase prediction in PA, substantially improving diagnostic performance and reducing the number of confirmatory tests required. These findings highlight the potential of machine learning to streamline the detection of resistance mechanisms within routine susceptibility testing workflows and may improve recognition of CPPA, especially in resource-limited settings.  Importance  : This approach could reduce unnecessary confirmation-testing for carbapenemases in  P. aeruginosa  , saving time and resources in clinical settings. It underscores the value of integrating machine learning with phenotypic data to address antimicrobial resistance challenges.

For Dataset 2, sensitivity/specificity were 95%/98% for CBM vs 100%/0% for the Gill algorithm.
This represented a reduction in isolates requiring confirmatory testing of 76% in Dataset 1 and 52% in Dataset 2.

papers.abstract_full: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a leading cause of coronary artery disease (CAD), characterized by the gradual accumulation of plaques within arterial walls, resulting in severe health complications such as myocardial infarctions and strokes. Recent advancements in multi-omics technologies including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics have significantly enhanced our understanding of the complex molecular mechanisms underlying atherosclerosis. These technologies provide a comprehensive view of the disease by integrating diverse biological data that extend beyond traditional risk factors. The integration of network medicine with multi-omics approaches further enhances our ability to elucidate the intricate interactions among biological components in both health and disease states related to atherosclerosis. This interdisciplinary framework not only facilitates the identification of novel diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets but also improves patient stratification for personalized interventions. By employing machine learning (ML) techniques, we can combine multiple omics and clinical datasets into innovative tools that support the development of tailored diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. However, challenges such as data quality, integration, and privacy remain significant barriers to progress. This review offers a comprehensive overview of various multi-omics technologies and their contributions to precision medicine in managing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). Additionally, we address current challenges and limitations while outlining future research directions aimed at improving patient outcomes through innovative methodologies. The convergence of multi-omics data with network medicine signifies a critical shift toward more effective and individualized treatment paradigms in combating ASCVD, presenting substantial opportunities for advancements in clinical practice and patient management.

papers.abstract_full: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading global cause of mortality and morbidity, necessitating continuous advancement in secondary prevention strategies. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a cornerstone of comprehensive cardiovascular care, has been significantly enhanced by innovations in exercise medicine, evolving towards more personalized and accessible paradigms. This review synthesizes the current frontiers in exercise-based CR, focusing on the synergistic integration of three transformative domains: technological innovation, precision medicine, and population-specific strategies. We first delineate the established physiological benefits and evidence-based efficacy of exercise therapy within CR frameworks. Subsequently, we examine the application of digital and intelligent technologies-including wearable devices, remote monitoring, artificial intelligence (AI), and big data analytics-which enable dynamic, data-driven patient management and remote care delivery. The paper further explores the paradigm of precision exercise prescription, guided by biomarkers, genetic profiling, and other individual biological data, to tailor interventions for optimal safety and therapeutic yield. Special emphasis is placed on addressing the heterogeneous needs of key patient populations, such as the elderly, women, and those with specific comorbidities like heart failure or arrhythmias, by outlining individualized strategies that improve engagement and effectiveness. Finally, we discuss future directions, highlighting multimodal technology platforms and in-depth precision medicine applications as key drivers for the next generation of CR, while critically evaluating the evidence readiness of emerging technologies and addressing implementation barriers. This review aims to inform clinical practice and guide future research towards developing more personalized, technology-enabled, and equitable cardiac rehabilitation models.

papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment. PURPOSE: To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Dynamic MRI reconstruction often requires accurate, fast, and low-latency algorithms that generalize across multiple applications, sampling schemes, and rates, without problem-specific parameter tuning. Existing methods either lack generalizability or require extensive parameter adjustment. PURPOSE: To develop generalizable, low-latency MRI reconstruction algorithms based on low-rank (LR) and low-rank + sparse (L+S) models that are accurate, fast, and require minimal parameter tuning across diverse dynamic MRI settings. METHODS: We propose a novel Alternating Gradient Descent and Minimization (AltGDmin) approach for L+S matrix recovery from column-wise undersampled measurements, and extend it to a 3-level hierarchical L+S model for dynamic MRI. A few-shot (FS) learning modification (AGM-L+S-FS) is introduced to enable near low-latency reconstruction with per-frame processing time comparable to or faster than scan time. A simpler LR-only variant is also evaluated. RESULTS: The proposed algorithms were validated on 6 prospective and 12 retrospective dynamic MRI datasets, covering cardiac, speech, and abdominal applications, with Cartesian, pseudo-radial, radial, and spiral sampling schemes. Experiments demonstrate accurate reconstruction, generalizability across datasets and sampling rates, and low-latency performance. Detailed comparisons with state-of-the-art LR, L+S, low-latency, and unsupervised deep learning methods show superior or comparable performance. CONCLUSIONS: Our AGM-L+S-FS approach provide generalizable, fast, and low-latency MRI reconstruction across multiple dynamic MRI applications and sampling schemes, without the need for problem-specific parameter tuning.

papers.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. papers.abstract_full: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconception and pregnancy through infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older age. These life stage-specific processes intersect with (epi)genetic, metabolic and microbiome factors, as well as social, psychological, behavioral, and environmental/geographic influences, contributing to heterogeneity in health outcomes. Addressing this complexity requires not only multimodal predictive models but also frameworks that integrate data standards and harmonization, systems biology, implementation science, and community engagement. To provide a structured approach to this complexity, we developed a seven-pillar Precision Nutrition Framework encompassing prevention for all, data sources, quantitative sciences, qualitative sciences, intervention implementation, communities, and education and workforce training. Using this framework and a lifespan perspective, we examine opportunities for promoting cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, and circadian/sleep health, synthesize evidence on key nutrients, dietary patterns, and emerging biomarkers, and adapt and expand the "precision nutrition plate" for implementation research in clinical and community settings. We highlight critical research gaps, including the need for phenotype-guided trials, standardized data integration, and scalable implementation strategies. By integrating biological, behavioral, and broader environmental dimensions across the life course, precision nutrition can advance more effective, accessible, and sustainable approaches for disease prevention and health promotion.

papers.abstract: Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) is associated with morbidity, mortality, and interruptions to cancer treatment.
