papers.abstract_full: Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) is associated with morbidity, mortality, and interruptions to cancer treatment. Current cardio-oncology clinical assessment tools generally rely on a limited range of clinical data; however, in the era of precision medicine, it may be possible to leverage multimodal data, including imaging and multi-omic inputs, to personalise CTR-CVT prediction and assessment. In this review, we examine the genotypic and phenotypic predictors of CTR-CVT and the evidence supporting their incorporation into multimodal risk models. Most research focuses on cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). We identify a strong evidence base for multimodal imaging-guided prediction, particularly cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)-derived global longitudinal strain measurements. Emerging evidence also supports the potential value of novel imaging parameters, including computed tomography (CT) and TTE-derived radiomic features. From the genomic and proteomic perspective, truncating titin variants and microRNA-126 may be informative predictors of cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). At the same time, the literature also highlights potential epigenomic markers of CTR-CVT. Finally, we consider how these diverse data can be integrated into multimodal risk models and how digital innovation and advanced machine learning methods may further improve model predictive performance. However, a large implementation gap remains, with challenges such as data privacy and a lack of external validation studies preventing routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_full: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is a leading cause of unexpected mortality worldwide and represents a major challenge in pathology, especially when conventional autopsy fails to identify a definitive cause of death. In these cases, molecular autopsy (MA) has emerged as a valuable diagnostic approach, enabling the identification of pathogenic genetic variants associated with inherited cardiomyopathies, channelopathies, and other cardiovascular diseases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the current role of MA in the investigation of SCD, highlighting recent advances in postmortem genetic testing and their impact on forensic practice. The evolution of sequencing technologies, from targeted gene panels to whole-exome and whole-genome sequencing, as well as new long-read sequencing approaches, is discussed. Emphasis is placed on the interpretation of genetic variants according to current international guidelines, the integration of molecular findings with autopsy, histopathological, and toxicological investigations, and the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration between forensic pathologists, molecular geneticists, cardiologists, and genetic counselors. We also examine current challenges, including variants of uncertain significance, limited genotype-phenotype correlation, ethical considerations, and the need for standardized international protocols. Finally, we explore prospects, including multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence-assisted variant interpretation, and improved data sharing initiatives, which may improve diagnostic accuracy and facilitate clinical translation. In addition to determining cause of death, MA has become an essential tool for identifying at-risk relatives through cascade screening, thus extending the role of forensic genetics from postmortem diagnosis to preventive cardiovascular medicine.

papers.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous myocardial disease associated with a broad spectrum of clinical outcomes, including heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. papers.abstract_full: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous myocardial disease associated with a broad spectrum of clinical outcomes, including heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays a central role in the comprehensive assessment of HCM by enabling integrated evaluation of myocardial morphology, ventricular and atrial function, tissue characterization, myocardial deformation, and longitudinal disease progression within a single comprehensive imaging modality. However, conventional CMR interpretation remains limited by manual post-processing, interobserver variability, sequence-dependent measurements, and reliance on a relatively restricted set of predefined imaging parameters. These limitations may hinder the full exploitation of the rich multidimensional information contained in CMR datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, together with radiomics-based quantitative image analysis, provide new opportunities to extend the diagnostic and prognostic value of CMR to extract high-dimensional and quantitative information from cine imaging, late gadolinium enhancement, parametric mapping, and feature-tracking-based deformation analysis. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced CMR may facilitate automated image analysis, improve diagnostic classification, support differentiation of HCM from phenocopies, enable tissue- and deformation-based phenotypic characterization, and enhance individualized risk prediction. Although several studies have included independent or external testing, many remain retrospective, rely on selected populations or internal validation, and lack prospective assessment of clinical utility. High discrimination performance should not be interpreted as established clinical utility, because calibration, decision-curve analysis, clinically relevant thresholds, and prospective clinical impact remain insufficiently evaluated. In addition, interpretability and clinical generalizability remain important challenges for translation into routine practice. This review summarizes the current role of CMR in HCM and discusses emerging applications, methodological challenges, and future directions of AI-enhanced CMR for diagnosis, phenotypic characterization, and risk stratification.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic heart disease and a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. This study aims to map the research landscape of Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy -related sudden cardiac death over the past 2 decades using bibliometric methods. METHODS: We performed a bibliometric analysis of 712 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (2005-2025). Using Cite Space, we examined publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation patterns, and keyword dynamics. RESULTS: Annual publication output rose markedly, with pronounced accelerations after the 2014 European Society of Cardiology and 2020 American heart association/American College of Cardiology guidelines. The United States led in productivity (203 publications) and network centrality (0.40), while China ranked second in output (123 publications) but exhibited limited international collaboration (centrality = 0.01). Co‑citation analysis indicated that clinical guidelines and risk‑prediction models form the field' score knowledge base, and five of the ten most cited references were international guidelines. Keyword analysis defined 4 principal thematic clusters disease entity, clinical outcomes, imaging biomarkers, and risk stratification and documented a shift from early mechanistic studies to multimodal risk prediction, followed more recently by artificial intelligence-driven models and targeted pharmacological therapies (e.g., mavacamten). CONCLUSION: This study provides a systematic, data-driven overview of the knowledge structure and evolutionary trends in Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-related sudden Cardiac death research. The findings underscore the field' s guideline-driven character, document the rise of AI-based risk stratification, and describe a paradigm shift toward disease-modifying therapies, offering actionable insights for prioritizing future research and informing clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_full: Continuous analysis of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals is essential for diagnosing cardiovascular diseases, particularly arrhythmias, which contribute significantly to global mortality. With the increasing use of wearable devices for non-clinical cardiac monitoring, real-time ECG processing encounters challenges due to memory constraints, particularly when memory is wasted by recording false positives. Noise in real-life ECG monitoring, such as motion artifacts, complicates automatic arrhythmia detection and recording, and calls for efficient methods to selectively filter out noisy signals that may be falsely classified (and recorded) as arrhythmias in devices with limited storage. This study develops and systematically compares machine learning and deep learning approaches for ECG noise detection using real-world wearable data acquired outside controlled clinical environments. By employing various models for classification, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Multi-Layer Perceptron, Gradient Boosting and Convolutional Neural Networks, we investigated four approaches, using as input features: i) raw signal data, ii) Heart Rate Variability-related time-domain features, iii) a combination of Heart Rate Variability-related time-domain and frequency-domain features, and iv) the parameters of a Genetic Programming-based reconstruction algorithm, analyzing both memory and computational requirements and classification performance of the corresponding architectures. Our findings indicate that the Multilayer Perceptron model, combined with Heart Rate Variability-related time- and frequency-domain features, offers an optimal trade-off between accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score. This study presents a scalable classification approach specifically designed for real-life arrhythmia detection in wearable devices, demonstrating the potential to enhance continuous cardiac monitoring and to facilitate the integration of such algorithms into wearable devices suitable for clinical and real-world settings.

papers.abstract_full: ABSTRACT  Background  The poor conservation of lncRNA genes limits their comprehensive functional studies, as genetic engineering of relevant animal models presupposes the presence of corresponding defined orthologs. This limitation is prominently evident in cardiovascular research, where heart-related lncRNAs are rarely conserved between humans and other vertebrates, despite the highly conserved nature of cardiac function. Because lncRNAs frequently regulate neighboring protein-coding genes essential for cardomyocyte function (herein termed cardiomyocyte indispensable, CMIs), we hypothesized that they are under evolutionary pressure to retain their genomic position and transcriptional activity, irrespective of sequence similarities to prototypical human lncRNA genes. Results  By integrating mouse cardiac knockout phenotypes with human single-cell transcriptomics data, we systematically identified heart-expressed CMIs and their neighboring. lncRNA genes. Cross-species synteny analyses revealed regions flanking 109 CMIs with conserved relative positions and transcriptional orientations across vertebrate genomes. As most of these loci reside within poorly annotated non-coding regions, we developed  VertLncRNAchecker, a neural network-based web interface, that predicts lncRNA-like genes within these regions, which we termed “positional ancestors”. Finally, we validated  in situ that these positional ancestors express mature lncRNA transcripts in the hearts of mice, pigs, and frogs, mirroring the expression of their human lncRNA counterparts.  Conclusions  We present an accurate and retrainable computational platform for cross-species lncRNA discovery that prioritizes conserved genomic position over sequence conservation or existing genome annotations. This pipeline revealed putative ancestors of human heart-related lncRNAs hidden within the vertebrate non-coding “dark genome”, providing novel insights into lncRNA evolution and a useful resource for cardiovascular research. papers.title: FBXO17 promotes osteosarcoma progression by regulating glycolysis and macrophage polarization.

papers.abstract_full: Osteosarcoma (OS) is the most common primary malignant bone tumor, characterized by high aggressiveness and poor prognosis. Glycolytic reprogramming and immune microenvironment imbalance contribute to OS progression, but the role of E3 ubiquitin ligases in coordinating glycolysis and macrophage polarization remains unclear. This study aimed to identify key E3 ubiquitin ligases regulating glycolysis and immune microenvironment in OS. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from the GSE309091 lncRNA-sequencing dataset using DESeq2. Glycolysis-related genes from GeneCards and E3 ubiquitin ligases from UbiBrowser were integrated with DEGs, and Random Forest machine learning was applied to select core genes. Immune cell infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT. Key gene expression was analyzed across the GSE309091 and GSE36001 datasets, with protein expression validated via Western blot. OS cell proliferation, cell cycle, apoptosis, invasion, and glycolysis were evaluated using colony formation, EdU, flow cytometry, Transwell assays, and glucose/lactate measurements. THP1-derived macrophages co-cultured with OS cell-conditioned medium were used to assess M1/M2 polarization. The expression of inflammatory cytokines was detected using ELISA. Potential FBXO17 substrates were predicted using UbiBrowser 2.0, and its regulatory relationship with PGC-1α was examined using Co-IP, ubiquitination, CHX-chase. Xenograft mouse models determined in vivo effects of FBXO17. FBXO17, SIAH2, BRCA1, and TRIM32 were identified as core genes associated with glycolysis and ubiquitination. Immune infiltration analysis showed their expression correlated with immune cell composition in OS. FBXO17 was highly expressed in GSE309091 and GSE36001 datasets, as well as in OS cell lines. FBXO17 knockdown inhibited OS cell proliferation, invasion, and glycolytic activity, induced G0/G1 arrest, promoted apoptosis, and enhanced M1 polarization of THP1 macrophages. FBXO17 interacted with PGC-1α and promoted its polyubiquitination and degradation. FBXO17 knockdown slowed PGC-1α degradation, whereas FBXO17 overexpression in FBXO17-knockdown cells reduced PGC-1α protein accumulation and partially restored lactate production. In vivo, FBXO17 silencing significantly suppressed tumor growth. FBXO17 promotes OS progression and glycolytic reprogramming, at least in part, by facilitating the ubiquitination and degradation of PGC-1α and is also involved in regulating macrophage polarization. Therefore, FBXO17 may represent a potential therapeutic target for OS.

In vivo, FBXO17 silencing significantly suppressed tumor growth.
Therefore, FBXO17 may represent a potential therapeutic target for OS.

papers.abstract_full: Streptococcus suis is a major swine pathogen and is considered an emerging zoonotic agent. Serotyping plays a crucial role for epidemiological investigations, pathogenicity assessment, and vaccine strategy. The present study evaluated the applicability of Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, using the IR Biotyper system, for the serotype discrimination of 94 S. suis isolates belonging to 13 distinct serotypes. Analysis of the 1300-800 cm-1 spectral region demonstrated the highest discriminatory power. Principal component analysis (PCA)/linear discriminant analysis (LDA) showed clear separation among the tested serotypes, except for serotypes 1/2 and 2. The classifier achieved overall accuracy of 90%, which increased to 96.7% when serotypes 2 and 1/2 were considered as a single category. These findings demonstrate that FT-IR spectroscopy represents a promising, rapid, and cost-effective tool for S. suis serotype discrimination. Its performance, ease of use, and compatibility with machine learning approaches support its potential implementation in routine diagnostic and epidemiological workflows. As previously reported for other clinically relevant bacteria, FT-IR spectroscopy may serve as a valuable complementary method to molecular typing, particularly in settings requiring rapid decision-making and high-throughput analysis.

papers.abstract_full: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) poses significant clinical challenges due to pronounced tumor heterogeneity. To identify robust, consistent biomarkers across cohorts, we integrated bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from GSE127165 and GSE142083 and validated candidate biomarkers in the external cohort GSE13060. Candidate gene prioritization incorporated differentially expressed genes, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) results, and markers of malignant epithelial cells exhibiting high copy number variation (High-CNV) derived from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) (GSE206332). Additional analyses included functional enrichment, immune association (adjusted for tumor purity), quasi-temporal analysis, and CellChat inference to elucidate the biological roles of top genes. The integrated approach identified 254 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 86 upregulated and 168 downregulated genes. WGCNA revealed a tumor-associated module containing 870 genes. Intersecting these findings with high-CNV malignant epithelial markers reduced the candidate pool to 16 genes, and LASSO regression retained five key features: MYBL2, KRT17, UCHL1, PTHLH, and ODC1. Among these, MYBL2 demonstrated the strongest and most consistent performance. MYBL2 was further associated with proliferative programs, including E2F targets, the G2/M checkpoint, DNA repair, and MYC targets. Gene signatures from these subclusters were enriched in bulk tumors and positively correlated with MYBL2 expression in independent cohorts. The results also indicate that MYBL2-high malignant epithelial states are linked to distinct connectivity patterns within the tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract_full: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic and end-stage kidney disease, and current therapies leave patients at high risk. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF), a traditional Chinese medicine, reduces proteinuria in DKD, but the compounds and molecular targets responsible remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that specific bioactive compounds of TWHF ameliorate DKD through interactions with cell-type-specific molecular targets, thereby modulating inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways involved in disease progression. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, immune-infiltration profiling, single-cell RNA sequencing, virtual gene knockout analysis, and molecular docking, this study developed a comprehensive computational framework to investigate the cell-type-specific and multi-target mechanisms of TWHF in DKD. Using the GEO study GSE30529 (with 22 microdissected human kidney samples), we intersected predicted TWHF targets with DKD-associated and differentially expressed genes from human kidney tubules, and identified four key genes (CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9) that were upregulated in DKD and negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate. The immune microenvironment in diseased kidneys was found to be remodelled based on an immune-infiltration analysis. Single-cell analysis localized MMP7 to loop-of-Henle epithelial cells, CCR2 to leukocyte, and PLK2 and PSMB9 to endothelial cells, and these genes were implicated in epithelial remodeling and endothelial dysfunction based on virtual gene knockout analysis. Furthermore, molecular docking predicted interactions between the four key proteins and three hub TWHF compounds, with triptolide showing the strongest predicted affinity. In an independent triptolide-response dataset generated from A549 cells, triptolide produced a dose- and time-dependent reduction in PLK2 expression. Collectively, CCR2, MMP7, PLK2, and PSMB9 were identified to be candidate therapeutic targets and Triptolide as a leading active compound, with the potential triptolide-PLK2 regulatory relationship should be further investigated. These results support our hypothesis that TWHF acts through direct, multi-compound engagement of multiple cell-type-specific targets, pointing to a multi-target, multi-pathway mechanism for TWHF in DKD and providing a mechanistic framework for subsequent experimental validation.

papers.abstract_full: The diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) remains challenging and is frequently delayed. Imaging is central to diagnosis, but relevant inflammatory and structural abnormalities may be subtle, heterogeneous, or overlap with findings related to mechanical stress, anatomical variation, and degeneration. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is therefore being investigated to support image interpretation, lesion detection, quantification, and standardized assessment. We synthesize evidence from 12 studies applying convolutional neural networks and related architectures to magnetic resonance imaging and radiographs, automate imaging scores, and combine imaging-derived information with clinical variables. Several models achieved performance comparable to experienced human readers, including during external validation. However, performance may decline in heterogeneous real-world populations for study-specific reasons not explained solely by scanner or protocol differences. No AI tool currently has regulatory clearance for autonomous use in axSpA, and applications remain largely confined to research and clinical trials.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) density provides prognostic information in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), but the additional value of TIL spatial organization remains unclear. METHODS: We developed CoATIL, a computational pathology framework quantifying TIL spatial architecture from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. The study included 461 patients with microsatellite-stable or MSI-low COAD. The model was trained using 140 patients from University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, validated internally in 52 patients, and externally in The Cancer Genome Atlas (n = 130), and Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital (n = 139). Prognostic performance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression. CoATIL was compared with a clinical model and eight foundation-model-based multiple-instance learning approaches. RESULTS: CoATIL was associated with progression-free survival (HR per standard-deviation increase, 1.32; 95% CI 1.13-1.55; p < 0.001; C-index=0.66) and remained prognostic after adjustment for clinicopathologic factors in each validation cohort (adjusted HRs, 2.00-4.40; all p < 0.05). High-versus-low-risk stratification was retained within stage II (HR 3.07; 95% CI 1.83-5.15; p < 0.001) and stage III disease (HR 3.24; 95% CI 1.28-8.19; p = 0.013). The combined clinical-CoATIL model achieved a higher C-index than the clinical model alone (0.69 versus 0.61; paired bootstrap difference, 0.08; 95% CI 0.03-0.14). Exploratory genomic analyses associated AMER1 and FBXW7 mutations with lower and higher CoATIL risk scores, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Spatial immune architecture extracted from routine histology provides complementary prognostic information in COAD. Prospective validation is warranted.

papers.abstract_full: Neuromuscular disorders (NMDs) encompass conditions that affect the peripheral nervous system. They are often caused by genetic alterations that impair skeletal muscle function. Molecular diagnosis remains challenging because some causal genes have not yet been identified. We therefore used feature-selection approaches to characterize genomic properties that distinguish NMD genes from other protein-coding genes. Curated genes implicated in NMDs (n = 639; GeneTable of NMDs) were merged with 134 genomic features for autosomal protein-coding genes spanning gene complexity, genetic variation, expression patterns, and other gene traits. Machine-learning-based feature selection using Boruta was combined with statistical analyses to compare NMD genes with other protein-coding genes. We also evaluated NMD genes against high-confidence non-NMD disease genes, examined variation across NMD subgroups, and assessed genes added to the NMD catalogue between 2020 and 2024. Compared with other protein-coding genes, NMD genes showed higher expression in disease-relevant tissues, including skeletal muscle and heart; greater transcript complexity and population genetic constraint, and stronger conservation across several evolutionary measures. Of 33 features that distinguished NMD genes from both high-confidence non-NMD disease genes and other autosomal genes, 28 were expression measures. Feature profiles varied across NMD subgroups, while genes added between 2020 and 2024 showed profiles similar to established NMD genes across all Boruta-confirmed features. This study identified genomic features that distinguish NMD genes from high-confidence disease genes and broader autosomal protein-coding genes. These findings provide insight into the gene architecture, expression, constraint, and evolutionary conservation of NMD genes and may inform candidate-gene prioritization in genetically unresolved NMDs.

papers.abstract_full: Cardiovascular disease is the world's top cause of death. Short recording times and a dependence on clinical settings are two practical drawbacks of traditional methods like Holter monitoring and standard 12-lead ECG. Two significant trends have come together in recent years: the broad availability of consumer-grade wearable technology, including smartwatches and adhesive ambulatory ECG patches, and the quick advancement of deep learning and artificial intelligence. Four main themes currently dominate research in this field: diagnostic accuracy under controlled conditions, algorithmic innovation for real-time and on-device analysis, real-world implementation and performance in large prospective studies, and the persistent technical, clinical, and regulatory challenges that limit widespread deployment.AI-based systems have shown consistently high performance in controlled environments and curated datasets, with reported sensitivities and specificities commonly ranging between 92% and 99%.However, performance, especially specificity and generalizability, frequently declines significantly if these algorithms are exposed to the messiness of daily movement, a variety of patient demographics, fluctuating skin contact, and hardware limitations outside of the lab. More advanced transformer architectures and multimodal techniques that combine ECG signals with photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms, as well as lightweight convolutional neural networks that can operate directly on the device itself and provide true real-time detection, have been the focus of recent algorithmic work. The present status of wearable ECG and PPG technology for AI-enabled arrhythmia detection is examined in this narrative review. It critically evaluates diagnostic performance, translational gaps that still exist and paying special attention to the major prospective studies that have shaped the field. All things considered, the data indicates that wearables driven by AI have real potential for screening for arrhythmias at the population level and have already shown promising signs of clinical utility. The field will require larger, longer, and more diversified prospective trials that are sufficiently powered to identify significant differences in hard clinical outcomes. This systematic literature review explores the current state of GenAI language models applications in various medical domains, assessing their effectiveness, applicability, and limitations. papers.abstract_full: UNLABELLED: The rapid evolution of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) presents significant opportunities to transform healthcare, particularly in generating personalized treatment recommendations. This systematic literature review explores the current state of GenAI language models applications in various medical domains, assessing their effectiveness, applicability, and limitations. The review addresses nine specific research questions to understand the potential and challenges of integrating GenAI into clinical practice. We use the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. From a pool of 3237 studies, 42 were selected based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. These studies were analyzed to evaluate the use of generative language models, such as GPT-3 and GPT-4, in various medical domains including oncology, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, and ophthalmological care. The analysis revealed that most GenAI applications in healthcare rely on general purpose LLMs to provide treatment recommendations. Fine-tuning with domain-specific data and prompt engineering were found to significantly improve output quality and reliability. However, persistent challenges include lack of clinical validation, ethical concerns such as bias, and issues related to transparency and regulatory compliance. While GenAI demonstrates strong potential to support clinical decision-making, real-world deployment remains limited due to unresolved ethical and validation issues. Future research should prioritize the development of interpretable, domain-specific models and rigorous clinical trials to ensure safe and effective integration into healthcare settings. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s41666-026-00242-y.

Despite the growing demand for dedicated, well-curated resources to advance polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery, such resources remain severely limited. Here, we present MultiTargetDB, a database of multitarget ligands integrated with comprehensive biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. At the small molecule level, MultiTargetDB integrates chemical structures (including molecular scaffolds), their drug development stages, and target information, whereas at the target level, MultiTargetDB incorporates protein domains and families, functional associations, and pathway-disease annotations. The current release contains 173 977 multitarget molecules, 6496 protein targets, and 474 749 standardized quantitative bioactivity records, complemented by 46 234 high-confidence protein functional associations, 370 pathways from the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG), and 2493 diseases. MultiTargetDB supports multitarget ligand retrieval, target-combination analysis, quantitative activity profiling, inspection of source-level evidence, and biological interpretation of molecule-target-pathway-disease relationships, with a natural-language query assistant facilitating flexible database exploration. The integrated quantitative, pharmacological and biological data further provide a basis for drug-repurposing exploration, computational modeling, and machine-learning applications. MultiTargetDB v1.0 is freely accessible at https://multitargetdb.inflygent.com/.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Esophageal cancer (EC) remains a significant public health burden in China. Current diagnostics modalities such as endoscopy and imaging are invasive, poorly accessible, or insensitive for early-stage cases. DNA methylation alterations in circulating free DNA (cfDNA) are promising for non-invasive cancer detection. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to develop and validate a methylation PCR-based assay for EC detection using EC-specific DNA methylation targets. Here, we report myESCAP, a PCR-based assay that amplifies and quantifies levels of EC-specific methylation in cfDNA METHODS: We conducted a multi-center, retrospective case-control study with 489 EC cases and 555 non-malignant controls (benign esophageal/gastric diseases or asymptomatic) to develop myESCAP, a methylation-specific PCR assay containing 11 EC-specific methylation markers from our previous genome-wide methylation screening, selected for strong discriminative performance and PCR compatibility. cfDNA was collected, bisulfite-converted, and tested by myESCAP, and results were analyzed by six modeling strategies (generalized linear model, k-nearest neighbors, C5.0 decision tree, gradient boosting machine, random forest, support vector machine) to train EC-prediction models using 347 EC cases and 349 non-malignant controls, and validated in 142 EC cases and 206 controls. RESULTS: All myESCAP markers demonstrated significant differential methylation between ECs and non-malignant controls, with adjusted p values between 5.8×10⁻3 and 3.1×10⁻88. The six models showed robust performance in the training cohort (average AUC = 0.835, average sensitivity = 76.13%, average specificity = 90.88%). They maintained performance in the validation cohort (average AUC = 0.823, average sensitivity = 75.59%, average specificity = 89%). Specifically, for stage I cases, myESCAP had an average sensitivity of 47.2%, highlighting the challenge of early detection with limited circulating tumor DNA and the need for further optimization. CONCLUSION: myESCAP accurately differentiated EC from non-malignant controls. The six models collectively confirm myESCAP's robustness and clinical potential as a cost-effective, non-invasive diagnostic tool for EC.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUNDS: Lysine crotonylation (LCR) is an emerging post-translational modification, yet its clinical significance and therapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain poorly understood. METHODS: Multi-omics data were collected from public repositories. Consensus clustering based on 18 LCR-related genes (LCRGs) was performed to define molecular subtypes. Co-expression modules identified via WGCNA were integrated into 101 machine-learning combinations to establish a LCR-related signature (LCRS). The signature was evaluated for survival prediction, immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug response across multiple cohorts, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate therapeutic targets and compounds were screened using DepMap CRISPR dependency data and pharmacogenomic databases (CTRP and PRISM). RESULTS: Two distinct molecular subtypes (C1 and C2) were identified, displaying significant differences in survival, immune infiltration, and signaling pathways. Integrating WGCNA hub genes with an optimal machine-learning framework yielded a robust 15-gene LCRS, which served as an independent prognostic factor in the TCGA cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized signature genes predominantly to endothelial cells. Pharmacogenomic profiling indicated higher sensitivity to sunitinib among high-risk patients, whereas low-risk patients displayed elevated sensitivity to axitinib and pazopanib. Furthermore, dependency screening prioritized CLCNKA as a key therapeutic target along with ten candidate compounds for high-risk patients. CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a robust LCR-related prognostic signature and nominates CLCNKA as a novel therapeutic vulnerability, offering actionable insights for personalized stratification and treatment in ccRCC.

papers.abstract_full: Digital cytology, telecytology, and artificial intelligence (AI) are reshaping cytopathology by expanding access to primary diagnosis, remote rapid on-site evaluation, consultation, quality assurance, education, archiving, and research. This review summarizes the technological basis of digital cytology, its current clinical and educational applications, implementation strategies, telecytology platforms, and emerging AI tools in gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytology. Compared with surgical pathology, digital cytology faces greater technical challenges because cytologic specimens often contain three-dimensional cell clusters, variable thickness, and overlapping cells, which increase demands on focusing, scanning time, image storage, and infrastructure. Recent advances in z-stacking, extended depth of focus, and whole-slide imaging have improved digital visualization, while updated professional guidance has supported broader validation of digital cytology for primary diagnosis and rapid on-site evaluation. Telecytology has shown high diagnostic concordance and has improved access to expert assessment, particularly for rapid on-site evaluation in resource-limited or remote settings. AI applications have shown promising performance in screening, classification, and quality control, especially in cervical cytology, with expanding use in non-gynecologic specimens. However, implementation remains constrained by technical complexity, variable image quality, regulatory and medicolegal concerns, infrastructure requirements, cost, and the need for robust validation and training. Overall, digital cytology and AI are guiding the transition into a Cytopathology 2.0 era characterized by greater connectivity, scalability, and data‑driven practice, although widespread adoption will depend on further standardization, robust validation, and smooth integration into everyday workflows.

papers.abstract_full: In the ongoing AI boom-now supercharged by large language models and generative AI tools-the rapid integration of AI into health care and public health has created an urgent need for professionals who combine deep domain expertise (clinical, epidemiological, ethical, and contextual expertise in health and public health) with AI fluency (the ability to understand, critically evaluate, use, and oversee AI systems effectively). Without domain guidance, AI risks producing biased, unsafe, or contextually irrelevant outputs that compromise patient safety and exacerbate disparities. Conversely, domain experts lacking AI fluency may underuse or misuse these technologies, missing opportunities to improve care quality, operational efficiency, and population health. A foundational understanding of the modern AI system stack-comprising energy, accelerators, infrastructure, models, and applications-empowers health professionals to make informed decisions on adoption, evaluation, governance, and ethical use without needing to code or build models themselves. This stack framework highlights critical interdependencies and health care-specific challenges, including regulatory compliance, data privacy, sustainability, and resource constraints, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This paper argues that cultivating domain-AI bilingualism is essential for safe, effective, and equitable AI integration worldwide. It outlines the 5-layer AI system stack applied to health care, key reasons for hybrid expertise, and a practical 4-step pathway: awakening (recognizing AI's transformative role), intrepidity (courageously engaging foundational AI concepts), bilingualism (translating between clinical needs and AI capabilities), and visionary leadership (driving organizational and policy readiness). It outlines major barriers, targeted strategies, and recommendations for educators, institutions, and policymakers. By bridging domain knowledge with AI fluency, health professionals can direct-rather than be directed by-AI technologies, including emerging agentic systems, toward more precise, sustainable, and human-centered outcomes while mitigating risks. This hybrid capability represents a nonnegotiable competency for the health workforce for thriving in the post-2026 AI era.

papers.abstract_full: AI models have enabled substantial advances in health care. Since the entry into force of the European Union (EU) AI Act in 2024, these systems have become subject to a common regulatory framework in the EU intended to harmonize AI governance across all member states. One of the act's distinctive features is that it accommodates existing economic, technological, and regulatory differences among European countries by leaving certain implementation responsibilities to national authorities. This is evident in regulatory sandboxes, supervised environments for developing, testing, and validating AI systems before deployment. In this viewpoint, we provide a policy-oriented analysis of health care regulatory sandboxes under the EU AI Act and propose recommendations for their design. These recommendations address the need to document model compression techniques that may affect the classification of large high-risk systems above the 1025 floating point operations per second threshold, incorporate explainability into AI systems from the design stage, identify and document biases in health care datasets, clarify the treatment of federated learning parameter updates under the General Data Protection Regulation, and strengthen the oversight of AI agents in clinical environments. The implementation timeline makes this discussion particularly timely given the approaching deadline of August 2, 2027, by which all member states must have established at least one national regulatory sandbox.

papers.abstract_full: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly entered the healthcare discourse, often framed through the lens of frontier models, generative systems, and transformative potential. Yet for many healthcare data teams, the practical path from curiosity to capability remains unclear. Concerns about data privacy, regulatory compliance, brittle systems, and misaligned expectations frequently stall progress before meaningful experimentation can begin. This paper presents ten simple rules for teaching practical AI to healthcare data teams, grounded in real-world data, privacy-first experimentation, and system-level thinking. Drawing on hands-on training experiences and existing educational and methodological literature, we argue that AI education in healthcare must prioritize workflows over models, systems over components, and institutional capability over isolated technical success. These rules are intended to help educators and organizational leaders move teams beyond the AI hype cycle toward building trustworthy, sustainable, and context-aware AI systems that matter.

papers.abstract_full: The structural diversity of RNA is central to molecular medicine, RNA-targeted drug discovery, and synthetic biology, where engineered RNA molecules are increasingly used in therapeutic, regulatory, and nanotechnology applications. While the rapid development of deep learning methods has heightened the demand for large, diverse structural datasets, high-quality RNA data remain scarce compared to protein datasets. Synthetic RNA structure datasets can help address this gap by enabling large-scale exploration of conformational space; however, their practical utility depends on careful curation and validation to ensure reliability. Here, we present a pipeline, RNA-SyntHub, for systematically constructing curated synthetic RNA datasets. The workflow integrates data from multiple structure-generation approaches with a meta-scoring function to identify low-quality models and select high-confidence candidates. As a proof of concept, we applied this method to a dataset of 447,402 synthetic RNA structures predicted by RFDiffusion, obtaining a curated subset of approximately 16,000 structures, further complemented with predictions from Boltz-1 and RNAComposer. This study provides both a methodological framework for generating and curating large collections of synthetic RNA 3D models under explicitly stated assumptions and a concrete dataset that supports methodological development, exploratory analyses, decoy-based applications, and selected deep learning workflows in RNA design, synthetic biology, and nanotechnology.

papers.abstract_full: A central challenge in generative biology is translating knowledge learned from natural sequences and experiments into designs with desired functions. In-context learning (ICL) is an emergent capability of large language models that allows them to adapt to new tasks from a few examples without additional training, enabling these models to become general-purpose learners. Here, we show that the genome language model, Evo 2, exhibits generative ICL in biological sequence design. Prompting with just tens of examples conditions Evo 2 to generate novel and diverse regulatory DNA sequences without any additional training. Mechanistic analysis suggests that genomic ICL may originate from induction, similar to phenomena observed in natural language. Reinforcement learning leveraging sequence-to-function models as experiment-derived rewards further strengthens ICL. We first validate this approach by generating enhancers that drive cell-type-specific gene expression in three human cell lines. Extending this approach in vivo, enhancers designed using human regulatory element data selectively label layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the mouse cortex with high specificity and stronger activity than existing enhancers. Our study provides evidence of emergent properties in genomic sequence models and introduces a promising approach for improving functional conditioning in generative biology.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Sequence-to-contact-map models are trained with pixel-wise losses, although the features of interest (insulation, domain boundaries, loops) are summaries of the map. Insulationbased losses help Hi-C resolution enhancement. No pre-specified test has asked whether they improve sequence-based prediction, judged against annotations independent of the training data. Proposed study. HiFold-Mamba predicts 448 × 448 maps at 2,048 bp from 1,048,576 bp of DNA on the DNALongBench contact-map task. Every component is reverse-complement-equivariant: convolutional tower, bidirectional Mamba blocks, multi-scale mixer and symmetric pairwise head. We pre-register three hypotheses: » H1: it exceeds each of three trained baselines (reproduced Akita, a parameter-matched Transformer and a parameter-matched CNN) by ≥0.01 stratum-adjusted correlation (SCC). » H2: an insulation and boundary loss, computed from the predicted map with the operator used on the observed map, improves boundary AUROC and loop AP against independent 4DN boundary calls and ENCODE CTCF ChIA-PET loops, at equal training steps and without loss of SCC. » H3: pretraining plus few-shot adaptation beats training from scratch on four held-out cell lines.Tests use a paired bootstrap over 237 one-megabase test blocks (one-sided α = 0.025). Pilot data. » Verification. The benchmark target, the window coordinates and the networks equivariance were verified. » Locus-shared reference. Copying other cell lines measured maps at the same locus matches published Akita on the benchmarks SCC (0.227 vs. 0.230). » SCC weightings. Two weightings in common use weight distance strata in opposite directions and agree only moderately (ρ = 0.54). » Comparison rule. In simulations calibrated on the pilot data, a per-block-best comparison against several baselines has no power. We therefore test against each baseline, which gives ≥ 90 % power at a true gain of 0.02 when between-model correlation is ≥ 0.95. » H2 positive control. On validation windows, observed maps recover the independent boundaries (AUROC 0.61 − 0.91) and loops (0.86 − 0.90). This fixed the insulation window and showed that these annotations are largely shared across cell types.

Biobanks are now developing genomic, proteomic, lipidomic, and metabolomic data sets on the order of hundreds of thousands of people. However, bridging the gap between population-level data and the individual--a major challenge in precision medicine--remains a novel and challenging task. Methods: We analyzed the landscape of contemporary multiomics data and the drivers of population and personal molecular variability using a longitudinal cohort uniquely suited to precision health applications. Using healthy routine visit data (94 participants, median five visits per participant), we profiled the human multiome across eight molecular omic types and 1.2 million measurements, with replication in a sister multiomic cohort (322 participants). Results: Molecular data tended to cluster by omes, with the metabolome and proteome showing less intraomic correlation than other data types. While most blood-based molecular measurements followed log-normal distributions, between 2.0% and 8.1% of molecules showed evidence of bimodality, with cases driven by genetic polymorphisms or dietary differences (e.g., SERPINA5 [P = 1.4e-6], 2-piperidinone [P = 5.7e-5]). Molecular variation across the population was generally higher than that within an individual over time (e.g., xenobiotic metabolites, progestin steroids). Analyzing personal molecular variation identified several participants with notable temporal shifts (intraindividual CV > 4 SDs higher than population CV) in free fatty acids (FFA 20:1 and FFA 20:2) or cytokines (IL-17F and IFN-beta), which were unlikely to be detected cross-sectionally. Body mass index (BMI) had a much larger multiomic footprint (23.6% of molecules associated) than demographic factors like sex or age (5.7% and 1.9%, respectively), although machine-learning predictive models of sex (top ROC AUC of 0.98) were more successful than those for BMI (top R2 of 0.59 by cytokines) or age (top R2 of 0.34 by metabolites). Purely multiomic predictive models explained modest to high proportions of variation (R2 = 0.22 to 0.94) in 20 common clinical tests, highlighting the potential clinical utility of these data even within a modestly sized cohort. Conclusion: Analysis of the molecular distributions, variation, and covariation of longitudinal multiomics data revealed clinically relevant differences at both the population and personal levels. Based on these findings, we conclude with six key considerations for the next generation of population omics as the field advances toward the goals of precision medicine.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic skeletal disorder in which altered protein-secretory homeostasis may contribute to impaired bone remodeling. We integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets GSE56815 and GSE2208 with the single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset GSE147287 to identify protein secretion pathway-associated genes and their cellular context in OP. Differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, three machine-learning algorithms, immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, regulatory network construction, and single-cell analyses were performed, followed by RT-qPCR validation. PPWD1 and TMEM50B were prioritized as key genes and were consistently upregulated in OP. Both genes were associated with proteasome, ribosome, and spliceosome pathways. Single-cell analysis highlighted bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) as a relevant cell population and suggested differences in PPWD1 and TMEM50B expression along pseudotime, together with candidate CXCL12-CXCR4-mediated communication. RT-qPCR confirmed increased expression of both genes in OP samples. These findings identify PPWD1 and TMEM50B as protein secretion pathway-associated genes in OP and provide a transcriptomic framework linking proteostasis-related signatures, BM-MSC states, and osteoimmune alterations while requiring further functional validation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Accounting is going through the greatest regulatory and technological reconfiguration in recent decades, marked by new international sustainability reporting standards and the emergence of advanced analytics. This dynamism drove a sustained growth in academic production, the meaning of which remains unexplored. The study analyzes the accounting agenda of Q1 journals as a field structured by institutional pressures and geographical inequalities, to determine whether its recent expansion led to a transformation of the topics it investigates. A quantitative approach was adopted with a bibliometric, descriptive, and retrospective design. Following the PRISMA 2020 framework, the corpus gathered 28,807 documents published between 2020 and 2025 in the 63 Q1 journals of the Scopus Accounting category, processed in RStudio with bibliometrix through performance analysis, collaboration networks, thematic mapping, and Spearman correlations. Production grew at an annual rate of 13.45%, with a disproportionate share of high-volume open access journals, although editorial productivity was not associated with scientific impact. The United Kingdom and the United States accounted for 64.2% of the network's intermediation, while high-production countries, such as Indonesia, showed marginal integration. Corporate governance remained at the stable core, sustainability occupied a peripheral position despite regulatory pressure, and machine learning entered the service of consolidated questions. The accounting agenda was transformed in its editorial infrastructure, in its geographical composition and in its methodological repertoire, while the content of its research problems remained stable.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a widely used plasticizer designated as a priority water pollutant in China, is an established endocrine disruptor with carcinogenic, teratogenic, and mutagenic potential. Although environmental exposure to DEHP through food and water is pervasive, its specific role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is poorly defined. Here, we systematically identified 485 putative DEHP-associated targets in LUAD by integrating multiple public databases. These targets are significantly enriched in cancer-related pathways such as those regulating epithelial cell proliferation, cell adhesion, extracellular matrix remodeling, and the PI3K-Akt pathway.Three complementary machine-learning algorithms converged on CAV1 and PECAM1 as core targets; their differential expression and diagnostic performance were validated in TCGA and GEO transcriptomic cohorts. CIBERSORT analysis showed that these core targets associate closely with tumor immune infiltration, and single-cell data delineated their cell-type–specific expression. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable binding of DEHP to CAV1, with a binding free energy of -29.62 ± 3.89 kcal/mol. Drug-response survival analysis indicated that PECAM1 could serve as a predictive marker for pemetrexed chemotherapy.Together, these findings suggest a potential DEHP–CAV1/PECAM1–immune microenvironment regulatory axis in LUAD and provide computational evidence for future experimental validation.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly used across healthcare to analyze complex clinical data, support diagnosis, guide precision medicine, accelerate drug discovery, and enable remote monitoring. This review examines established AI/ML techniques and their current clinical and commercial applications while considering the requirements for trustworthy adoption. Evidence reviewed across medical imaging, electronic health records, drug discovery, precision medicine, and remote patient monitoring shows broad use of supervised, unsupervised, deep-learning, hybrid, and ensemble approaches. Reported benefits include improved diagnostic and predictive performance, earlier risk identification, and support for individualized treatment. Recurring barriers include data privacy, model opacity, computational demands, algorithmic bias, limited external validation, workflow integration, and workforce readiness. Explainable AI, privacy-preserving learning, human-in-the-loop oversight, and evolving regulatory frameworks are prominent responses to these challenges. AI/ML is moving from experimental development toward practical healthcare use, but dependable adoption requires more than predictive accuracy. Robust external validation, transparent and interpretable models, privacy protection, equitable datasets, appropriate regulation, and effective clinician-AI collaboration are central to building trustworthy clinical systems.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Tay-Sachs disease is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by mutations in the HEXA gene, which lead to a deficiency of the enzyme beta-hexosaminidase A and the toxic accumulation of GM2 gangliosides in the nervous system. Currently, many HEXA missense variants fall into categories of uncertain or conflicting clinical significance. This study aimed to evaluate these diagnostic discrepancies by comparing clinical classifications from ClinVar with automated machine-learning pathogenicity predictions from AlphaMissense across 30 HEXA missense variants. A targeted subset of seven variants, 5 with conflicting classifications (Trp474Leu, Ser486Asn, Thr467Ile, Pro471Arg, and Pro475Ser) and two reference variants (Arg247Trp and Gly478Arg), were selected for three-dimensional structural modeling and rotamer strain analysis in PyMOL. Structural analysis demonstrated that buried residues within the tightly packed hydrophobic core (Ser486Asn, Thr467Ile) produced consistently higher rotamer strain values and reduced flexibility compared to surface-exposed residues (Trp474Leu, Pro475Ser), which achieved low-strain conformations without steric clashes. A boundary residue (Pro471Arg) exhibited extreme structural tension due to increases in side-chain bulk and charge. These findings suggest that HEXA protein stability is highly sensitive to core disruptions and highlight how using 3D structural modeling can help resolve diagnostic discrepancies for Variants of Uncertain Significance, supporting ongoing research into therapeutic development for Tay-Sachs disease.

papers.abstract_full: Nigeria's 2023 Presidential Election represented the country's most technologically ambitious electoral exercise, with the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) to enhance voter accreditation, transparency, and public confidence. Yet the election revealed a fundamental contradiction: technologies introduced to strengthen electoral integrity became, in practice, sources of suspicion and contestation. Existing scholarship has largely examined electoral technologies and AI-driven disinformation as separate phenomena, leaving insufficient attention to how their interaction shapes perceptions of electoral integrity. This study addresses that gap by examining the paradoxical relationship between Artificial Intelligence, digital technologies, and electoral integrity in Nigeria, using the 2023 Presidential Election as a case study. Guided by the Cyber-Elections framework and employing a qualitative content analysis, the study analyses official reports, judicial decisions, election observer reports, fact-checking evidence, and relevant academic literature. The findings reveal two interrelated paradoxes. First, the infrastructural paradox demonstrates that although BVAS significantly improved voter accreditation, IReV's failure to upload presidential election results in real time, together with inconsistent official explanations for the failure, weakened public confidence in the results collation process. Second, the informational paradox shows that the same digital platforms that expanded civic participation also enabled AI-generated deepfakes, coordinated disinformation, and misinformation, creating competing narratives among state institutions, political actors, and citizens regarding the credibility of the election. The paper argues that electoral integrity in the digital era depends not only on technological innovation but also on the interaction between infrastructural reliability, institutional transparency, effective communication, political trust, and digital literacy. It concludes with five policy recommendations aimed at strengthening electoral technology, legal and regulatory frameworks, institutional communication, digital literacy, and independent oversight to enhance the credibility of future elections in Nigeria.

papers.abstract_full: Background:  Three-dimensional chromatin organization is tightly linked to gene regu- lation and genome function, yet quantitative descriptors connecting local contact patterns to functional state remain limited. Standard approaches such as A/B compartments (PC1), topologically associating domains (TADs), and chromatin loops are global or domain-level, and require complex computational pipelines. Methods. We propose two simple local features computed directly from a Hi-C contact profile: Shannon entropy of the contact distribution and normalized LZ-complexity of the binarized contact pattern. Their ability to predict chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq coverage) was assessed with multiple linear regression, gradient boosting, and graph convolutional networks (GCN). The analysis was performed on two human cell lines—GM12878 (lymphoblastoid) and K562 (erythroleukemic)— for all 23 chromosomes (1–22, X) at 100 kb resolution. Results. Linear regression with entropy, LZ, and PC1 showed that entropy (β = −2.97, p  0.22), whereas the contribution of PC1 was smaller (0.12–0.19) and that of LZ was the smallest (0.05–0.11). Conclusions. Local entropy and LZ-complexity are simple, interpretable, and independent predictors of chromatin accessibility that outperform the standard compartment index in linear models. Graph neural networks provide an additional gain by exploiting local graph topology. The proposed approach is computationally efficient, requires no additional experimental data, and demonstrates stable results across two different cell lines, indicating generalizability. This work opens new avenues for studying the relationship between 3D genome structure and function using simple structural measures.

Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank pr…
papers.abstract_full: Abstract  This study empirically investigates the impact of regulatory technology (RegTech) adoption on the financial performance of Indian commercial banks. Utilizing a comprehensive panel dataset of 32 listed banks from 2016 to 2025, the research employs Python-based text-mining techniques on published annual reports to construct a novel RegTech adoption index, which is bifurcated into Core Regulatory Technology and RegTech Enabling Technology. To account for the dynamic persistence of bank profitability and resolve potential endogeneity issues, the study utilizes a two-step System GMM estimator alongside baseline Random Effects modeling. The empirical results reveal a significant asymmetrical relationship. Investments in RegTech Enabling Technology such as artificial intelligence and big data yield a strong, positive, and statistically significant enhancement to the Return on Assets (ROA). Conversely, Core Regulatory Technology dedicated strictly to automated compliance acts primarily as a mandatory operational safeguard, demonstrating a statistically insignificant impact on overall profitability. Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis uncovers that the financial benefits of foundational enabling technologies are heavily concentrated among large institutions and private sector banks, whereas the substantial capital expenditures required for core compliance systems actively compress the asset returns of large banks. These core findings are rigorously validated through extensive robustness checks, including the use of alternative dependent variables (ROE), lagged effects, outlier removal, and a Monte Carlo placebo test. Ultimately, this research provides vital strategic insights for bank management and policymakers regarding the operational costs and monetization potential of digital compliance infrastructures.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Study rationale and knowledge gap:  Canine visceral leishmaniasis is a major zoonotic disease in which intracellular Leishmania infantum persists within macrophages, while treatment limitations and emerging resistance highlight the need for improved therapeutic strategies. MicroRNA-mediated regulation of host immune responses and nanoparticle-based drug delivery offer complementary approaches, but their integration with artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted target identification has not been adequately investigated in canine visceral leishmaniasis. This study addressed this knowledge gap by integrating computational miRNA–gene prioritization with nanoparticle-mediated drug delivery and ex vivo validation in primary canine macrophages. Methods  Publicly available transcriptomic datasets and experimentally supported miRNA–gene interactions were analysed using machine-learning approaches to prioritize candidate regulatory miRNAs. The selected candidates were evaluated in primary macrophages obtained from 16 dogs using miltefosine-loaded PLGA nanoparticles, miRNA modulation and combination treatment. Parasite burden, cell viability, cytokine responses and expression of selected immune-related genes were assessed during the experimental period. Results  The computational framework identified miR-155 and miR-146a among the principal candidates for experimental investigation. The selected machine-learning model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.89 during cross-validation and 0.84 during transfer to the canine dataset. Experimentally, the combination of PLGA-miltefosine nanoparticles with miR-155 modulation produced the greatest reduction in intracellular parasite burden, reaching a 78% reduction in infection index at 48 h compared with infected untreated controls. Further studies incorporating target-level validation, nanoparticle uptake, broader immune profiling and in vivo evaluation are needed to determine the therapeutic relevance of this combined approach.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Background: Congenital heart disease (CHD) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) co-occur more frequently than expected, suggesting shared developmental susceptibility. We aimed to identify cross-tissue molecular candidates linking cardiac and neurodevelopmental abnormalities. Methods: CHD- and ASD-associated genes were curated from MalaCards and SFARI Gene, and their intersection was defined as the CHD- and ASD-associated gene set (CAGES). Shared gene enrichment was assessed against the human protein-coding genome. CHD and ASD genome-wide association data were integrated with heart and brain cis-expression quantitative trait loci using Bayesian colocalization and summary data-based Mendelian randomization with HEIDI testing. Candidates were further evaluated using bulk transcriptomics, six machine learning feature selection methods, independent cohorts, and scTenifoldKnk virtual knockout analyses in developing human heart and cerebral cortex. Results: Seventy-three genes were shared between CHD and ASD. CHD7 showed suggestive colocalization for CHD and ASD, while lower genetically predicted CHD7 expression was associated with higher odds of both disorders, with nonsignificant HEIDI tests. MEF2C was downregulated in tetralogy of Fallot myocardium and selected by all six ASD machine learning methods, with consistently lower expression in ASD. CAGES-derived signatures discriminated independent CHD, ASD cord blood, and cortical cohorts. CHD7 virtual knockout analysis identified MEF2C as a computationally predicted regulatory candidate in the prenatal brain, particularly in late-fetal excitatory neurons and intermediate progenitor cells, with cell-type-specific predicted effects also observed in the developing heart. Conclusions: CHD and ASD share molecular susceptibility involving pleiotropic developmental mechanisms. CHD7 and MEF2C emerge as connected cross-tissue candidates across complementary genetically informed, transcriptomic, and developmental regulatory analyses, highlighting prenatal neuronal populations and developmental windows for investigating the heart-brain axis.

selected_papers.abstract_full: Congenital heart disease (CHD) and neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) frequently co-occur, indicating that cardiac and neural phenotypes can arise from shared developmental disturbances rather than exclusively from the physiological consequences of heart disease. Copy number variations (CNVs) provide a major genomic basis for this overlap, but their effects extend beyond changes in protein-coding gene dosage. This review synthesizes evidence from recurrent CNV syndromes, genomic cohorts, developmental studies, and experimental models to define how CNVs jointly influence heart and brain development. We examine four interconnected mechanisms: dosage alteration of pleiotropic and multiple genes, disruption of non-coding regulatory elements, remodeling of non-coding RNA networks, and reorganization of three-dimensional chromatin architecture. We further describe how developmental timing, cell-type-specific regulatory context, additional genomic variants, cardiac physiology, and clinical exposures shape incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity. Together, these findings support a layered model in which a primary CNV establishes cross-organ susceptibility, whereas genetic and developmental modifiers determine whether CHD, NDD, or both become clinically manifest. Clinically, CNV diagnosis can inform neurodevelopmental surveillance, multisystem management, and genetic counseling. Genotype-first longitudinal cohorts, developmental multi-omics, parallel cardiac and neural models, and prospective clinical studies will advance individualized risk prediction and intervention.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Variants in LMNA are established causes of inherited dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM); however, the clinical significance of many rare missense variants remains uncertain. We identified the rare LMNA c.929 A > G (p.Gln310Arg) variant in a patient with progressive DCM and performed preliminary variant-specific functional characterization in an AC16 transient overexpression model. METHODS: Duo whole-exome sequencing and copy-number variation analysis were performed in the proband and his son. Wild-type and p.Gln310Arg lamin A expression constructs were transiently transfected into AC16 cells. Flag-tagged protein expression, Flag-based transfection efficiency, and lamin A/C distribution were assessed by western blotting and immunofluorescence staining. Mitochondrial membrane potential and intracellular ROS-associated fluorescence were assessed using JC-1 and DCFH-DA staining, respectively. ERK1/2, JNK, and p38 MAPK phosphorylation was evaluated by western blotting. Hypertrophy-associated NPPA and NPPB expression was measured by RT-qPCR, and cell area was quantified after phalloidin staining. RESULTS: The LMNA c.929 A > G variant was classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Wild-type and p.Gln310Arg lamin A constructs showed comparable Flag-tagged protein expression and Flag-based transfection efficiency. Expression of p.Gln310Arg lamin A was associated with an increased proportion of cells displaying ring-like lamin A/C staining patterns. Variant-expressing cells showed increased intracellular DCF fluorescence, reduced JC-1 red-to-green fluorescence ratio, and selectively increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation, whereas no significant changes were detected in JNK or p38 MAPK phosphorylation. The same cells also showed a hypertrophy-like phenotype characterized by increased NPPA and NPPB expression and enlarged cell area. CONCLUSION: In an AC16 transient overexpression model, expression of p.Gln310Arg lamin A was associated with altered lamin A/C distribution, increased intracellular ROS-associated fluorescence, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, selectively increased ERK1/2 phosphorylation, and a hypertrophy-like cellular phenotype. These findings provide preliminary variant-specific functional evidence but do not establish the pathogenicity of the variant or the causal relationships among the observed cellular abnormalities. Further validation in endogenous and physiologically relevant cardac models is required.

selected_papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVES: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with severe left ventricular (LV) dysfunction in infants and young children is a life-threatening condition and carries a high risk of mechanical circulatory support and heart transplantation (HTx). Pulmonary artery banding (PAB) has been proposed as a recovery strategy, but data on medium- and long-term outcomes remain limited. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center observational study included infants and young children who underwent surgical PAB between 2006 and 2024. Inclusion criteria were ROSS functional class (FC) III/IV, spherical left ventricular-dilated cardiomyopathy (LV-DCM) with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <35%, and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD) z-score >+4 with preserved right ventricular function. Primary endpoints were overall survival and transplant-free recovery, defined as sustained normalization of LV systolic function with reverse remodeling. RESULTS: Fifty patients (27 female) met the inclusion criteria and underwent PAB at a median age of 188 days, 70% were in ROSS FC IV, and 42% were listed as urgent for HTx. DCM etiology was idiopathic in 42%, genetic in 22%, and myocarditis-associated in 36%. There was no procedural mortality. Overall survival was 90% and 72% achieved transplant-free functional recovery. Following PAB, magnetic resonance imaging-derived LVEF improved from 19% ± 7% to 56% ± 11%, and LVEDD z-scores decreased from +6.3 to +1 (P < .001). In 33 patients, recovery was sustained over a median follow-up of 7 years, including 15 patients with stable LV function for over 10 years. CONCLUSIONS: In infants and young children with severe LV-DCM, PAB is associated with high long-term survival, sustained transplant-free recovery, and durable reverse cardiac remodeling.

selected_papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Family screening is recommended in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), but risk stratification of relatives of probands without pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (gene-elusive) remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to define the incidence, prognosis, and predictors of disease development in first-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands. METHODS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands from 4 international referral centers who underwent baseline electrocardiography and echocardiography were included. The primary outcome was the development of the disease, defined as DCM or isolated left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction (LV ejection fraction: <50%). Major adverse cardiac events were exploratory secondary outcomes. Age-adjusted Cox models with family-clustered robust standard errors were used to identify disease predictors. RESULTS: Among 292 relatives (median age: 36 years, 48% male), 14 (5%) were affected at baseline. During a median follow-up of 52 months, 21 additional relatives developed disease, corresponding to an incidence rate of 17 per 1,000 person-years. Familial DCM (HR: 4.24; 95% CI: 1.38-13.1; P = 0.012), QRS duration >120 ms (HR: 7.24; 95% CI: 2.25-23.3; P < 0.001), lower LV ejection fraction (HR: 3.73; 95% CI: 2.46-5.65; P < 0.001), and LV dilatation (HR: 6.19; 95% CI: 2.27-16.9; P < 0.001) were predictors of disease development. Age at diagnosis in probands significantly correlated with age at onset in relatives (r = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.55-0.92; P < 0.001). Major adverse cardiac events occurred in 9 patients (4%). CONCLUSIONS: First-degree relatives of gene-elusive DCM probands have a relatively low but non-negligible risk of disease development. Familial clustering, electrocardiographic or echocardiographic abnormalities, and age of disease expression in the proband may help tailor surveillance intensity.

selected_papers.abstract: Inherited cardiomyopathies are major causes of heart failure, malignant ventricular arrhythmia, and sudden cardiac death, and they require lifelong surveillance of affected individuals and clinically at-risk relatives. Their clinical genetics has traditionally been organised around rare monogenic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, especially in sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), titin-related and other sarcomeric forms of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), nuclear-envelope DCM, and …
selected_papers.abstract_full: Inherited cardiomyopathies are major causes of heart failure, malignant ventricular arrhythmia, and sudden cardiac death, and they require lifelong surveillance of affected individuals and clinically at-risk relatives. Their clinical genetics has traditionally been organised around rare monogenic pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, especially in sarcomeric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), titin-related and other sarcomeric forms of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), nuclear-envelope DCM, and desmosomal arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM). This model remains indispensable, but it is incomplete: it does not fully explain genotype-negative disease, variable penetrance, age of onset, disease severity, or discordant phenotypes within the same family. Polygenic risk scores (PRS), which aggregate the weighted effects of common variants, offer a second layer of inherited susceptibility that may refine the interpretation of rare variants and borderline phenotypes. Current evidence is strongest for HCM, increasingly important for DCM, and still weak for ACM and restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCM). The central limitation is equity and transferability. Most cardiomyopathy PRS discovery, calibration, and validation have been performed in European-ancestry datasets. At the same time, Arab and Middle Eastern populations remain underrepresented in GWAS, reference allele-frequency databases, longitudinal cardiac imaging resources, and clinical utility studies. Direct importation of European PRS into Arab cardiovascular genetics would therefore risk miscalibration, variant misclassification, false reassurance, overdiagnosis, and inappropriate counseling. This critical review evaluates PRS evidence across HCM, DCM, ACM, RCM, and related inherited cardiac diseases; explains why PRS is not a diagnostic test or replacement for monogenic testing; and proposes a phased Arab implementation framework based on local discovery cohorts, whole-genome sequencing, ancestry-aware calibration, family-based penetrance studies, harmonized imaging phenotypes, prospective outcome tracking, genetic counseling pathways, and governance safeguards. The future is not monogenic versus polygenic risk; it is integrated genomic risk, implemented only when clinically validated and equitable.

At the same time, Arab and Middle Eastern populations remain underrepresented in GWAS, reference allele-frequency databases, longitudinal cardiac imaging resources, and clinical utility studies.
The future is not monogenic versus polygenic risk; it is integrated genomic risk, implemented only when clinically validated and equitable.
